domains.name: Application
domains.covers: Launching and quitting After Effects, preferences, plug-ins, memory and performance, help and account items.

features.name: 3D preferences
features.summary: Pane for 3D navigation: whether number keys drive camera tools and gizmos or markers, whether Alt/Option-drag navigates or duplicates, the camera manipulation point indicator, scroll-wheel dolly behaviour and direction, and emptying the 3D model cache.

automation.notes: Command 3132 is named Camera3D in the hyperbrew list. Saved in the preferences file. Preferences.savePrefAs* can write raw entries, but the section and key for this option are not documented, so treat scripted changes as unverified. Opens the Preferences dialog (modal). On Windows the path is Edit > Preferences > 3D. Command 3132 opens the modal Preferences dialog at 3D. Its options have no documented preference keys or scripting members.

features.name: Assistant chats
features.summary: Starts new conversations in the Assistant panel and lists active and past chats; includes sample prompts to begin.

automation.notes: Beta Assistant feature; interactive and dependent on Adobe cloud services. No member or command id.

features.name: Generate images and video with the Assistant
features.summary: Asks the Assistant to create still images or video clips from text or reference images using Adobe Firefly and partner models and places them in the project.

automation.notes: Beta Assistant feature that depends on cloud generation services and sign-in and may consume generative credits; interactive, no member or command id.

features.name: Assistant permissions
features.summary: Prompt-bar setting choosing whether the Assistant asks before every action (Always ask permission) or proceeds on its own (Approve permission automatically).

automation.notes: Beta Assistant setting; the Assistant is interactive and depends on Adobe cloud services. No member or command id.

features.name: Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network
features.summary: Permits ExtendScript code to create or modify files and use network sockets; off by default for safety.

automation.notes: Must be enabled before scripts that write files can run; a script cannot grant this to itself through documented members. Id 3131 opens Preferences at Scripting & Expressions (modal); published scripts use it to prompt users to turn the option on. Preferences are under Edit (Windows) or After Effects > Settings (macOS). Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network is a security setting that the user must turn on in the modal Preferences dialog (command 3131). A script cannot grant it to itself through documented members, and these tools deliberately do not write it as a raw preference.

features.name: Appearance preferences
features.summary: Pane for interface appearance: handle size, GPU-drawn viewers, system colour picker, render progress in Info, Project panel thumbnails, timecode-plus-frames display, tool tips, coach marks, colour theme, label-colour usage, mask colours, gradients and motion path keyframe display.

automation.notes: Command 3071 (Appearance in the 2015 list, UserInterfaceColors in the 2025 list) opens the modal Preferences dialog at this pane. Of its options only the colour theme keys are documented (see Color Theme).

features.name: Application
features.summary: Global scripting object (app) that represents the running After Effects instance and gives access to the open project, preferences, settings, menu commands and undo grouping.

automation.notes: executeCommand runs a menu item by numeric id; findMenuCommandId looks an id up by its localized menu name.

features.name: Cache Frames When Idle
features.summary: Background caching that starts after an idle delay, choosing which frames to cache first (from or around the current time, or from the range start) and the range (work area, extended work area or entire duration).

automation.notes: Saved in the preferences file. Preferences.savePrefAs* can write raw entries, but the section and key for this option are not documented, so treat scripted changes as unverified.

features.name: Clear
features.summary: Deletes the current selection without putting it on the clipboard.

automation.notes: Needs a selection.

features.name: Show Coach Marks
features.summary: Turns on short in-app callouts that introduce new or changed features; Reset Coach Marks shows already-seen ones again.

features.name: Color Theme
features.summary: Chooses the interface theme (Darkest, Dark or Light), with an Accessible color contrast option that lowers contrast of buttons, icons and text.

automation.notes: Section "Main Pref Section v2", file PREF_Type_MACHINE_INDEPENDENT: key "User Interface Brightness (4) [0.0..1.0]" (float; in 24.4 Darkest is 0.16 or less, Dark above 0.16, Light above 0.5) and key "Use Reduced Contrast" (bool, the accessible contrast option). The published script only reads them; writing is unverified and the interface may only change after a restart.

features.name: Composition preferences
features.summary: Pane with creation and editing defaults: centred anchor point for new shape layers, where new and split layers start, linear spatial interpolation and separated Position by default, Pen/Mask Feather toggle, mask vertex counts, bounding boxes inside precomps, nested switch behaviour, synchronized time, double-click behaviour and synthetic layer duration.

automation.notes: Pane of the modal Preferences dialog (Edit > Preferences; command 2359 opens the first pane). Its options have no documented preference keys in our sources.

features.name: Copy
features.summary: Places a copy of the current selection on the clipboard without removing it.

automation.notes: Needs a selection in the active panel.

features.name: Crash Repair Options
features.summary: Dialog shown on relaunch after a crash, or a notice naming the suspect effect, offering to disable plug-ins, reset preferences or start in Safe Mode.

automation.notes: Appears only after a crash at launch time.

features.name: Cut
features.summary: Removes the selection (layers, keyframes, items and similar) and places it on the clipboard.

automation.notes: Needs a selection in the active panel.

features.name: Deselect All
features.summary: Clears the selection in the active panel.

automation.notes: Ctrl+Shift+A (Cmd+Shift+A) is an alternate shortcut.

features.name: Enable Disk Cache
features.summary: Stores rendered frames on disk so they can be reused for previews and across sessions; includes maximum size and folder choice.

automation.notes: Section "Disk Cache Controls", key "Enable Disk Cache" in the default (machine-specific) file; a published script checks it with havePref and reads it with getPrefAsLong, so the key may be absent until the option has been changed. Writing it is unverified, and the size and folder keys are not documented in a licensed source. The folder cannot be a drive root and needs 10 GB free beyond the set size.

features.name: Disk preferences
features.summary: Pane for the disk cache (on/off, size, folder, empty, preview from disk, lossless compressed frames), the conformed media cache database and cache locations with cleanup, and XMP metadata handling on import.

automation.notes: Pane of the modal Preferences dialog (Edit > Preferences; command 2359 opens the first pane). Of its options only the disk cache on/off key is documented (see Enable Disk Cache).

features.name: Empty All Caches
features.summary: Button that clears the disk cache, media cache and database cache together, freeing storage and fixing some launch problems.

automation.notes: Button in the modal Preferences dialog (Startup & Repair). Application.purge with PurgeTarget.ALL_CACHES clears memory and disk cache but not the media cache database.

features.name: Empty Disk Cache
features.summary: Button that deletes all frames in the disk cache.

automation.notes: Same effect as Edit > Purge > All Disk Cache (10700). Application.purge with ALL_CACHES also clears disk cache but empties RAM caches too.

features.name: Export preferences
features.summary: Pane for render output defaults: automatic output names, output preview via Mercury Transmit, finish sound, ProRes hardware encoding, segmenting long sequences and movie files, and render notifications.

automation.notes: Command 2363 opens the modal Preferences dialog at this pane under its former name, Output. Of its options only the render-finished sound key is documented (see Render-complete sounds).

features.name: After Effects FAQ
features.summary: Common questions about 64-bit support, RAM guidance, trials, Motion Graphics templates in Premiere and where to get help.

automation.notes: Reference material.

features.name: File Bug Report
features.summary: Button in Startup & Repair preferences that opens Adobe's bug-reporting form.

automation.notes: Opens Adobe's bug-report web form in a browser; nothing changes in After Effects.

features.name: GPU and driver requirements
features.summary: Requirements and advice for NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Apple GPUs and drivers, including minimum CUDA and Intel driver versions and GPU-only VR effects.

automation.notes: System configuration outside After Effects.

features.name: GPU Information
features.summary: Dialog listing the graphics card's capabilities, driver version and supported features.

automation.notes: Read-only dialog opened from Memory & CPU preferences; no member reports the GPU details.

features.name: Grids & Guides preferences
features.summary: Pane for grid colour, style, spacing and subdivisions, proportional grid divisions, guide colour and style, action/title and center-cut safe margins, and transparency checkerboard size and colours.

automation.notes: Opens the Preferences dialog at this pane. Saved in the preferences file. Preferences.savePrefAs* can write raw entries, but the section and key for this option are not documented, so treat scripted changes as unverified. Command 2364 opens the modal Preferences dialog at Grids & Guides. Grid spacing, guide colour and style have no documented preference keys; guides themselves are edited with edit_comp_guides and shown, snapped or locked with set_view_options.

features.name: Hardware Accelerate Composition, Layer, and Footage Panels
features.summary: Uses the GPU (DirectX or Metal) to prepare rendered frames for display, including scaling, overlays and display colour management.

automation.notes: On by default. Saved in the preferences file. Preferences.savePrefAs* can write raw entries, but the section and key for this option are not documented, so treat scripted changes as unverified.

features.name: Updates
features.summary: Checks for and installs After Effects updates through Creative Cloud.

automation.notes: Opens the Creative Cloud app to check for updates; nothing changes in After Effects. Id 10003 (Updates...) is listed only in the 2015 list.

features.name: History
features.summary: Submenu listing recent undoable changes; choosing an entry undoes that change and every change made after it.

features.name: Home screen
features.summary: Start view shown at launch with tabs for New Project, Open Project, New Team Project and Open Team Project plus recent work and learning links; a Home icon switches between it and the open project.

automation.notes: Interactive start screen shown at launch when Enable Home Screen is on (always on for trials); its actions have their own routes (Application.newProject, Application.open).

features.name: Import preferences
features.summary: Pane for import defaults: drop-frame handling for timecode-less NTSC media, unlabeled alpha interpretation, what dragging several files creates, interpretation on replacement, still and sequence durations and frame rate, missing-frame checks, hardware decoding and automatic footage reloading.

automation.notes: Opens the Preferences dialog at this pane. Saved in the preferences file. Preferences.savePrefAs* can write raw entries, but the section and key for this option are not documented, so treat scripted changes as unverified. Command 2362 opens the modal Preferences dialog at Import. Default still and sequence durations and frame rates have no documented preference keys; import_files sets per-import options through ImportOptions instead.

features.name: Performance optimization
features.summary: Adobe guidance for speeding up work: update drivers, leave RAM for other apps, use fast separate disks and a large disk cache, simplify projects with proxies and pre-renders, and limit on-screen drawing.

automation.notes: Guidance page; individual measures are separate features.

features.name: Install in Simplified Chinese or Japanese
features.summary: Steps to get a Simplified Chinese or Japanese install: uninstall, set the Creative Cloud default install language, set OS language and region (and system locale on Windows), restart and reinstall.

automation.notes: OS and Creative Cloud configuration outside After Effects.

features.name: Enable JavaScript Debugger
features.summary: Lets ExtendScript (.jsx) scripts be paused and inspected in a debugger when they fail.

automation.notes: Section "Main Pref Section v2", key "Pref_JAVASCRIPT_DEBUGGER", file PREF_Type_MACHINE_INDEPENDENT (the scripting guide's example reads it with getPrefAsBool). Writing it is unverified and may only take effect after a restart.

features.name: Keyboard Shortcuts
features.summary: Visual editor showing a keyboard map coloured by application-wide and panel-specific assignments, a searchable command list and a modifier list; shortcuts are assigned by typing or dragging, conflicts are flagged, and custom sets are saved with Save As.

automation.notes: Modal dialog. Alt/Option-clicking OK restores the default shortcut set. Property-reveal keys such as A, E, P, U and their doubles cannot be reassigned. Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts (command 3562) opens a modal editor. Shortcut sets are text files in the user preferences folder with no scripting member to read or write them.

features.name: Use Label Color for Layer Handles and Paths / Related Tabs
features.summary: Two options that tint layer handles, mask paths and motion paths, and viewer tabs, with the label colour of the related layer or item.

features.name: Label
features.summary: Edit submenu that assigns one of the 16 label colors (or None) to selected project items, layers, keyframes or composition markers; menu entries show colour swatches.

automation.notes: Labels are numbers 0-16 in scripting; custom label colours cannot be set from scripts. Ids are the colour entries in the hyperbrew list (Red, Yellow, Aqua, ..., Dark Green). Swatches in the menu arrived in 24.4. Needs a selection.

features.name: Labels preferences
features.summary: Preferences pane that sets the default label for each new item or layer type (composition, video, audio, still, folder, solid, camera, light, adjustment, null, shape, text, 3D model) and renames or recolours each of the 16 labels.

automation.notes: Opens the modal Preferences dialog at the Labels pane. Saved in the preferences file. Preferences.savePrefAs* can write raw entries, but the section and key for this option are not documented, so treat scripted changes as unverified. Edit > Preferences > Labels (command 2365) opens the modal Preferences dialog. Label colours and names are saved in the preferences file, but the section and key names for them are not documented, so set_application_settings does not write them; Item.label and Layer.label (set_layer_properties, manage_items) choose a label number but cannot change its colour or name.

features.name: Learn panel
features.summary: Interactive tutorial panel for new users that walks through tasks step by step and marks lessons complete as the user performs them.

automation.notes: Interactive tutorial panel. Its Window item takes an install-specific id (5038), and "Learn" also names a workspace, so a lookup by name is ambiguous.

features.name: Manage Sync Settings
features.summary: Former settings for Sync Settings: which preference groups to sync, whether to upload, download or ask, and clearing the user profile on quit; Clear Settings reset the synced state.

automation.notes: Discontinued with Sync Settings.

features.name: Conformed Media Cache
features.summary: Locations of the media cache database and cache files (conformed audio .cfa, MPEG index files) shared with Media Encoder and Premiere; Clean Database & Cache removes entries whose source files are gone.

automation.notes: Connect all source drives before cleaning, or caches for offline media are removed.

features.name: Memory & CPU preferences
features.summary: Pane showing how RAM is shared with other Adobe apps, with the amount reserved for other applications, buttons for memory usage details and GPU information, and CPU settings.

automation.notes: Command 3124 is listed as MemoryMultiprocessing, the pane's former name. setMemoryUsageLimits sets cache and maximum memory percentages rather than the reserved-RAM figure directly. Multi-Frame Rendering options on this pane are covered by rendering records.

features.name: Memory Details
features.summary: Dialog opened with Show Memory Usage Details that tabulates installed and allowed RAM and each related process's minimum, maximum and current memory and priority, with a Copy button.

automation.notes: Read-only dialog; Application.memoryInUse gives the current total only.

features.name: Mercury GPU Acceleration
features.summary: Project-level renderer choice under Project Settings > Video Rendering and Effects > Use that renders supported effects on the GPU via CUDA, OpenCL or Metal, or falls back to Mercury Software Only.

automation.notes: Check Application.availableGPUAccelTypes before setting Project.gpuAccelType; options depend on the installed GPU and OS.

features.name: Migrate Previous Version Preferences
features.summary: Copies preferences from the previous After Effects version; offered automatically on first launch of a new version when only older preferences exist.

automation.notes: Offered in the Preferences dialog and at first launch of a new version; no member or command id.

features.name: Motion Path
features.summary: Chooses how many keyframes appear on motion paths: none, all, a fixed number around the current time, or those within a time span.

features.name: Paste
features.summary: Inserts clipboard contents into the active panel or selected target, such as layers into a composition or keyframes onto a property.

automation.notes: Result depends on what is selected and which panel is active.

features.name: Path Point and Handle Size
features.summary: Sets the on-screen size of mask and shape vertices, Bezier handles and motion path handles.

features.name: Global performance cache
features.summary: RAM-cached frames survive undo and state changes and are reused wherever identical frames recur, and disk-cached frames persist between sessions and projects once a project is saved.

automation.notes: Automatic behaviour; nothing to invoke.

features.name: Preferences
features.summary: Application-wide settings dialog organised into panes (Startup & Repair, Project, Composition, Previews, Appearance, Grids & Guides, Labels, Type, Import, Export, Audio, Disk, Memory & CPU, Video, 3D, Scripting & Expressions); on macOS it is After Effects > Settings.

automation.notes: Modal dialog. Command 2359 (hyperbrew name General) opens the first pane, which is what the shortcut does. Scripts can read and write raw preference keys through app.preferences. Since 25.4 the app relaunches itself when a changed preference needs a restart. The Preferences dialog (command 2359) is modal. Its options are entries in the preferences files that app.preferences can read (get_aftereffects_info reads any section and key) and write, but the scripting guide documents only a few key names, so set_application_settings writes only those (expand flowchart compositions, JavaScript debugger) plus the memory limits Application.setMemoryUsageLimits sets. Writing undocumented keys is left out because their names and value types are unverified and some changes make After Effects relaunch (25.4 on).

features.name: Preferences
features.summary: Scripting object (app.preferences) that reads, writes, deletes and reloads entries in the preference files by section and key.

automation.notes: Keys are raw section/key strings; PREFType picks which preference file is used. Many values only take effect after a restart.

features.name: Previews preferences
features.summary: Pane for interactive preview behaviour: adaptive resolution limit and 3D reduction, zoom and colour management quality, automatic frame blending and motion blur in previews, audio muting when not real-time, background caching while idle, and magnification type and behaviour.

automation.notes: Command 2705 opens the modal Preferences dialog at Previews. Its options have no documented preference keys in our sources.

features.name: Project preferences
features.summary: Pane holding project-level defaults: keep the current workspace when opening projects, Dynamic Link project-file matching, a template for new projects, the default solids folder name, and auto-save frequency, version count and location.

automation.notes: Pane of the modal Preferences dialog (Edit > Preferences; command 2359 opens the first pane). Options with a documented preference key are recorded on their own records (for example Auto-Save).

features.name: All 3D Cache
features.summary: Clears cached data for imported 3D models.

features.name: All Cache
features.summary: Empties every cache After Effects keeps, in memory and on disk.

automation.notes: Command id is from the hyperbrew list (AllCache, 2024-2025).

features.name: All Disk Cache
features.summary: Deletes the frames stored in the disk cache only.

features.name: All Memory
features.summary: Releases all RAM held by After Effects caches without touching the disk cache.

features.name: All Memory & Disk Cache
features.summary: Empties every RAM cache and the disk cache in one step.

automation.notes: PurgeTarget.ALL_CACHES clears both RAM and disk cache (behaviour since 24.3).

features.name: Image Cache Memory
features.summary: Frees RAM used by cached rendered frames and source images.

features.name: Purge
features.summary: Submenu that frees RAM, disk cache, 3D cache, undo history, image cache or snapshots on demand, for example after an out-of-memory alert.

automation.notes: Alt/Option-choosing All Memory also forces a resync of the project database.

features.name: Snapshot
features.summary: Frees all memory holding viewer snapshots.

features.name: Undo
features.summary: Discards the stored undo history to free the memory it uses.

automation.notes: After purging, earlier changes can no longer be undone.

features.name: Quit
features.summary: Closes After Effects, prompting to save the open project if it has unsaved changes.

automation.notes: app.quit() may raise a save prompt for a modified project; close the project first with Project.close to control that.

features.name: RAM reserved for other applications
features.summary: Amount of installed RAM kept free for the OS and other software; the remainder is shared by After Effects and other Adobe apps in a common pool managed by a memory balancer.

automation.notes: setMemoryUsageLimits sets the image cache and maximum memory percentages, which is the scripted counterpart of this allocation; the value cannot go below a baseline.

features.name: Redo
features.summary: Reapplies the change most recently reversed with Undo.

automation.notes: Types-for-Adobe also lists a Redo2 entry (17); 2035 is named Redo in both lists.

features.name: Reset All Preferences To Defaults
features.summary: Button that returns all preferences, workspaces and the debug database to factory state; takes effect after a restart.

automation.notes: Button in the modal Preferences dialog (Startup & Repair); takes effect after a restart and also resets workspaces. No member or command id.

features.name: Reset background preferences
features.summary: Manual reset done outside the app by renaming the version preferences folder so After Effects rebuilds it on next launch.

automation.notes: Done in Finder or Explorer while After Effects is closed.

features.name: Restore default preferences at startup
features.summary: Holding the modifier combination while After Effects starts discards the current preferences and starts with factory defaults.

automation.notes: Key combination is held during application launch; there is nothing to invoke from a running session.

features.name: Reveal Preferences in Explorer/Finder
features.summary: Button that opens the per-version folder containing preference, shortcut and workspace files so they can be backed up or copied to another machine.

automation.notes: Button in the Preferences dialog that only opens the preferences folder in the operating system file browser.

features.name: Start in Safe Mode
features.summary: Relaunches After Effects with third-party plug-ins and extensions turned off and default preference values, to tell whether a crash comes from preferences or a plug-in.

automation.notes: Triggers an application restart. Offered in the crash repair options; interactive only.

features.name: Scripting & Expressions preferences
features.summary: Pane for script security and debugging options and for expression pick-whip output, error banners and the expression editor's font, highlighting, indentation, completion and colour theme.

automation.notes: Opens the Preferences dialog at this pane. Command 3131 opens the modal Preferences dialog at Scripting & Expressions. Only the JavaScript debugger option has a documented key (Main Pref Section v2 / Pref_JAVASCRIPT_DEBUGGER), which set_application_settings writes; the other options on the pane have no documented keys.

features.name: Show Scripting Progress Dialog
features.summary: Displays a modal progress bar with elapsed time while a script runs.

features.name: Select All
features.summary: Selects every item in the active panel, for example all layers in the Timeline panel or all items in the Project panel.

features.name: Select Label Group
features.summary: Selects every layer or item that shares the label colour of the current selection.

automation.notes: Needs at least one selected layer or item.

features.name: Settings
features.summary: Scripting object (app.settings) for storing and retrieving persistent script-defined values between sessions.

features.name: Shared memory pool
features.summary: After Effects shares RAM with Premiere, Photoshop, Audition and Media Encoder; launching or quitting those apps changes how much RAM is available for previews.

automation.notes: Managed automatically by the memory balancer.

features.name: Show Rendering Progress in Info Panel
features.summary: Reports per-frame render progress in the Info panel (and Flowchart); turning it off saves some screen-update work.

features.name: Show Tool Tips
features.summary: Shows a tooltip with the control name and its shortcut when the pointer rests on interface elements.

features.name: Startup & Repair preferences
features.summary: Pane controlling the Home screen at launch and compatibility alerts, with repair buttons to restart in Safe Mode, empty all caches, reveal or reset preferences, migrate a previous version's preferences, and file a bug report.

automation.notes: Opens the Preferences dialog at this pane. Command 3134 opens the modal Preferences dialog at Startup & Repair. Its options (such as showing system compatibility issues and resetting preferences) have no documented preference keys or scripting members.

features.name: Sync Settings
features.summary: Former Creative Cloud feature that uploaded or downloaded preferences, shortcuts, composition presets, interpretation rules and render/output templates between machines; removed from 24.3 and retired for older versions after December 2025.

automation.notes: Discontinued; relied on Adobe ID sign-in. Copy the preferences folder instead.

features.name: Use System Color Picker
features.summary: Swaps the Adobe colour picker for the operating system's native one.

features.name: System Compatibility Report
features.summary: Report listing hardware, driver and OS issues that may affect After Effects, with recommended fixes; can be shown automatically at startup.

automation.notes: The Show System Compatibility Issues option in Startup & Repair controls the startup alert. Id 2550 is the Help menu entry in the hyperbrew list. Help > System Compatibility Report (command 2550, menu title ends in an ellipsis) opens a dialog that shows the report; there is no scripting member that returns its contents. get_aftereffects_info reports the version, operating system and GPU acceleration types instead.

features.name: System
features.summary: Scripting object (system) that reports the machine and operating system and can run a shell command.

automation.notes: callSystem runs an OS command and returns its output; the other members are read-only.

features.name: Third-party plug-ins
features.summary: Effects and tools from other developers that extend After Effects; Adobe lists partners whose plug-ins support Multi-Frame Rendering.

automation.notes: Installation is outside the app; app.effects lists the effects that loaded.

features.name: Tip of the Day
features.summary: Random practical tip shown in an empty Composition, Footage or Layer panel, such as in a new blank project; tips are localized and use the right modifier keys per OS.

automation.notes: Displayed automatically; no command or member controls it.

features.name: Type preferences
features.summary: Pane setting the font menu preview size, how many recent fonts are listed, and whether to warn about missing fonts when projects open.

automation.notes: Opens the Preferences dialog at this pane. Command 3130 opens the modal Preferences dialog at Type. Its options have no documented preference keys or scripting members.

features.name: Application language
features.summary: After Effects runs in the language chosen as the Creative Cloud default install language, which can differ from the OS language (Chinese still requires a Chinese OS display language).

automation.notes: Changed by reinstalling through Creative Cloud; Application.isoLanguage only reports the current locale.

features.name: Undo
features.summary: Reverses the most recent change to project data; up to 99 changes can be stepped back in sequence. Panel scrolling and tool changes are not undoable.

automation.notes: The menu label names the action being undone. Scripts can wrap their edits in Application.beginUndoGroup/endUndoGroup so one Undo reverses them.

features.name: Undo limit and locking
features.summary: Guidance on the undo stack: only project-data edits are recorded, the stack holds 99 steps, and locking a layer is the safer way to protect it from accidental edits.

automation.notes: Behavioural description; the stack depth is not configurable from scripts.

features.name: Unicode text in interface fields
features.summary: Names and text fields across the UI (projects, layers, effects, dropdown options) accept any Unicode characters, including mixed scripts and emoji in one field.

automation.notes: Script strings are Unicode, so names can be set with any characters through Item.name and Layer.name. Text layers still do not render colour emoji.

features.name: Video preferences
features.summary: Pane enabling HDR/extended range preview and configuring Mercury Transmit output to external monitors and devices.

automation.notes: Command 2704 opens the modal Preferences dialog at this pane under its former name, Video Preview. Its options have no documented preference keys in our sources.

features.name: Warn User When Executing Files
features.summary: Shows a confirmation before a script file chosen through Run Script File executes.

domains.name: Projects
domains.covers: Projects and the Project panel: creating, opening, saving, folders, items, dependencies, collect files, reduce and consolidate.

features.name: After Effects project (.aep)
features.summary: Binary project file that stores compositions and links to source files; the primary format for saving work.

features.name: XML project (.aepx)
features.summary: Text-based XML project in which marker data, footage paths and item names and comments can be edited outside After Effects or by automation; meant for copies, not day-to-day saving.

automation.notes: Created with Save a Copy As XML; renaming to .aep in Save As converts it back to binary.

features.name: Project template (.aet)
features.summary: Template project; opening it creates an untitled project based on it so the template file itself is never overwritten.

automation.notes: Make one by renaming a saved .aep to .aet or saving a copy with that extension.

features.name: Auto-Save
features.summary: Saves backup copies of the open project on a timer and optionally when the render queue starts, keeping a set number of versions next to the project or in a custom folder.

automation.notes: Only Save When Starting Render Queue has a documented key: section "Auto Save", key "Enable Auto Save RQ2" (PREF_Type_MACHINE_INDEPENDENT, 0 or 1), which a published exporter reads, clears and restores around rendering. The interval, version count and location keys are not documented.

features.name: Browse in Bridge
features.summary: Launches Adobe Bridge for browsing, organising and previewing media and presets.

automation.notes: Requires Adobe Bridge to be installed. Needs Bridge installed.

features.name: Close Project
features.summary: Closes the open project, prompting to save if it has changed.

automation.notes: CloseOptions decides whether the script saves, discards or prompts.

features.name: Collect Files
features.summary: Copies the project, its footage and proxies and a report of required files, effects and fonts into one new folder; options choose which comps' sources to collect, report-only, proxy handling, reducing the project, redirecting render output and watch-folder rendering.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog and then a folder chooser; save the project first. Later edits stay in the original project. File > Dependencies > Collect Files... (command 2482) opens a modal options dialog and then a folder chooser; the object model has no Collect Files method, so nothing reaches it unattended.

features.name: Comment column
features.summary: Free-text notes per item; the column can be renamed (Rename This) to serve as a custom sort field such as camera number.

automation.notes: Comments are also searchable when the column is visible.

features.name: Consolidate All Footage
features.summary: Merges duplicate footage items (same source and identical interpretation) into one and repoints layers to the survivor.

features.name: Cross-platform project file paths
features.summary: When a moved project opens, After Effects looks for footage in the project's folder, then the original path, then the volume root, so keeping footage under the project folder makes projects portable between macOS and Windows.

automation.notes: Automatic relinking behaviour; Collect Files is the tool to package a project.

features.name: Delete item
features.summary: Removes selected items from the project with Delete; a modifier variant skips the warning for footage that is in use.

automation.notes: The shortcut listed is the no-warning delete; plain Delete asks first when the item is used.

features.name: Dependencies
features.summary: File submenu grouping commands that gather, deduplicate, trim or locate a project's source files and components.

automation.notes: Submenu only; its commands (Collect Files 2482, Consolidate All Footage 2107, Remove Unused Footage 2109, Reduce Project 2735, Find Missing Effects, Fonts and Footage 4002 to 4004) are recorded on their own records.

features.name: Extend selection in Project panel
features.summary: Adds the next or previous item to the selection with the keyboard.

automation.notes: Shift+Up Arrow extends upward.

features.name: Use Feet + Frames
features.summary: With Frames display, counts time as feet of 16mm or 35mm film plus leftover frames.

features.name: Find
features.summary: Puts the cursor in the Project panel search field; typing filters items by visible columns, and the words missing, unused and used filter by status.

automation.notes: Spaces act as AND and commas as OR; only shown columns are searched except for missing.

features.name: FolderItem
features.summary: Scripting object for a Project panel folder, holding its child items.

features.name: Footage Start Time
features.summary: With Timecode display, chooses whether footage uses its source timecode or starts at 00:00:00:00.

features.name: Frame Count
features.summary: Sets where frame numbering begins: from the item's timecode (Timecode Conversion), from 0, or from 1.

automation.notes: Setting FC_TIMECODE_CONVERSION resets displayStartFrame to 0.

features.name: Increment and Save
features.summary: Saves a numbered copy next to the original (adding or bumping a trailing number) and continues in that new file.

automation.notes: Needs a project that has already been saved.

features.name: ItemCollection
features.summary: Scripting collection of project items (Project.items or FolderItem.items) that can create compositions and folders.

features.name: Item information area
features.summary: Top area of the Project panel showing details and a thumbnail for the selected item; Alt/Option-click shows a footage file's creator ID.

automation.notes: Display only.

features.name: Item
features.summary: Base scripting object for anything listed in the Project panel (compositions, footage, folders), carrying name, comment, label, selection state and parent folder.

features.name: Missing effects
features.summary: Opening a project with effects whose plug-ins did not load shows a warning, and those instances are prefixed Missing in the Timeline panel; FF reveals only missing effects.

automation.notes: 4002 is Find Missing Effects (File > Dependencies) in both command lists; FF needs selected layers or applies to all.

features.name: Missing footage
features.summary: Footage whose source cannot be found is labeled Missing with an italic name and shown as colour bars in compositions until relinked; typing missing in the Project panel search lists such items.

automation.notes: 4004 is Find Missing Footage (File > Dependencies) in both command lists; the help pages describe the search keyword rather than that menu item. FootageItem.footageMissing reports the state.

features.name: Move items into folders
features.summary: Dragging items onto a folder files them there; dragging to the gray information area at the top moves them back to the top level.

features.name: New Folder
features.summary: Creates a folder in the Project panel for organising items; folders can be nested and exist only in the project.

features.name: New Project
features.summary: Closes the current project (asking to save changes) and starts an empty project, or a copy of the chosen template when New Project loads template is on.

automation.notes: newProject() returns null if the user cancels the save prompt for an unsaved project.

features.name: New Project loads template
features.summary: Project preference that makes File > New > New Project start from a chosen .aep, .aepx or .aet template, so every new project begins with preferred settings and folders.

automation.notes: Set with Choose Project Template in the same pane. Preference key not documented.

features.name: Open most recent project
features.summary: Reopens the project that was most recently open.

automation.notes: 2330 is the first recent-project entry (OpenRecentProject1 in Types-for-Adobe; 2331-2334 are the next ones).

features.name: Open Project
features.summary: Opens an existing .aep, .aepx or .aet project file, replacing the open project.

automation.notes: Without a file argument app.open() shows the open dialog. Opening a template creates an untitled copy.

features.name: Open selected item
features.summary: Opens the selected composition in its Composition and Timeline panels or the selected footage in a Footage panel; Alt/Option double-click opens footage in its system player.

features.name: Project Flowchart
features.summary: Flowchart view of the whole project with tiles for compositions, footage and layers and arrows showing how they feed each other; tiles can be selected, deleted or context-clicked but links cannot be edited.

automation.notes: Also opened by the Project Flowchart button at the top of the Project panel scroll bar.

features.name: Item label colour
features.summary: Colour label shown in the Project panel Label column for each item, defaulting by item type and usable to filter and sort.

automation.notes: Values 0-16; custom colours are not scriptable.

features.name: Project
features.summary: Scripting object (app.project) for the single open project: its items and root folder, file, selection, active item, render queue and project settings.

automation.notes: After Effects holds a single open project at any time.

features.name: Project panel
features.summary: Lists compositions, footage and folders with an information area and thumbnail at the top, sortable columns, a search field, and buttons for new folders, new compositions, interpretation, project settings and deletion.

automation.notes: The order of items has no effect on output.

features.name: Project panel columns
features.summary: Columns such as Label, Type, Size, Comment, File Path and source timecode can be shown or hidden from the heading context menu or Columns in the panel menu, dragged to reorder, resized, and clicked to sort.

automation.notes: Column layout is interactive UI state with no documented member.

features.name: Project Settings
features.summary: Dialog with project-wide options for time display, colour, audio sample rate, GPU rendering and the expression engine; also opened from the bit-depth button at the bottom of the Project panel.

automation.notes: Modal dialog. Individual settings are scriptable through Project attributes (see the time display records).

features.name: Template projects
features.summary: Template projects (.aet) carry a preset structure such as folders and settings; opening one yields an untitled project, and designers often lock layers that should stay unchanged.

automation.notes: On Windows choose the template file type in the Open dialog. After Effects does not install templates.

features.name: Project panel thumbnails
features.summary: Item thumbnails in the Project panel use a composition's poster frame; Thumbnail Transparency Grid in the panel menu shows a checkerboard behind transparent areas, and thumbnails can be disabled in Appearance preferences for speed.

automation.notes: Disable Thumbnails in Project Panel is a preference without a documented key.

features.name: Reduce Project
features.summary: Keeps only the selected compositions and what they use, deleting other compositions and unused footage; expressions pointing at removed comps are lost.

automation.notes: Needs compositions selected in the active Project panel; reduceProject takes an array of items to keep. Shows a reminder about expressions.

features.name: Remove Unused Footage
features.summary: Deletes every footage item that no composition uses.

features.name: Rename item
features.summary: Renames a selected composition, footage item or folder by pressing Enter/Return or choosing Rename from its context menu.

features.name: Resolve Fonts
features.summary: Dialog shown when a project uses fonts that are not installed; fonts available from Adobe can be synced automatically and others fall back to a default.

automation.notes: Can be suppressed with the Type preference. 4003 is Find Missing Fonts in both command lists. replaceFont swaps one font for another across the project (scripting since 24.5). Font sync needs Adobe Fonts sign-in.

features.name: Reveal in Bridge
features.summary: Shows the selected Project panel item's source file in Adobe Bridge.

automation.notes: Needs a selected footage item and Bridge installed.

features.name: Reveal Project in Explorer/Finder
features.summary: Opens the operating system file browser with the current project file highlighted.

automation.notes: macOS label is Reveal Project in Finder. Needs a saved project. Project.file gives the path for scripted equivalents.

features.name: Revert
features.summary: Discards all changes and imports since the last save and reloads the saved project; cannot be undone.

automation.notes: Shows a confirmation.

features.name: Save
features.summary: Writes the open project to its current file.

automation.notes: An unsaved project shows a save dialog; pass a File to Project.save to avoid it.

features.name: Save a Copy
features.summary: Writes a copy of the project elsewhere while the open project keeps its own name and location.

automation.notes: Opens a save dialog.

features.name: Save As
features.summary: Saves the project under a new name or location and continues working in the new file; the original is left unchanged.

automation.notes: Project.save(file) saves to a new path; saveWithDialog shows the dialog.

features.name: Save a Copy As XML
features.summary: Writes a copy of the project in the text-based .aepx format.

automation.notes: Opens a save dialog.

features.name: Save a Copy As previous version
menu_path: Save a Copy As <previous major version number>
features.summary: Saves a copy readable by the previous major version; features that version lacks are dropped from the copy.

automation.notes: Ids are the 2025 build entries (Save a Copy As 23.x and 24.x); the target versions and ids change with each release. Opens a save dialog. File > Save As > Save a Copy As <previous version> opens a save dialog, and its command ids (4168, 4169 in the 2025 build) and target version change with every release. Project.save has no option for an earlier version's format.

features.name: Solids folder
features.summary: Project panel folder where solid footage items (used by solids, adjustment layers and nulls) are filed; it can be renamed, nested, swapped for any folder via its context menu, and its default name set in Project preferences.

automation.notes: Only one folder at a time can be the solids folder; nesting is unavailable in Team Projects.

features.name: Source timecode columns
features.summary: Project panel columns Media Start, Media End, Media Duration and Tape Name show the source timecode of footage, while In Point, Out Point and Duration reflect trims or a comp's work area.

automation.notes: Display columns only.

features.name: Time Display Style
features.summary: Chooses whether times across the project are shown as timecode or as frame numbers (optionally feet and frames).

automation.notes: Affects display only, not frame rates. Ctrl/Cmd-clicking a current-time display cycles the style.

domains.name: Footage and import
domains.covers: Importing footage, image sequences, layered files and other formats, and Interpret Footage (alpha, frame rate, fields, pixel aspect, colour).

features.name: Alpha (Interpret Footage)
features.summary: Chooses how an alpha channel is read: Ignore, Straight - Unmatted, Premultiplied - Matted With Color (with a matte color), or Guess.

features.name: Apply Interpretation
features.summary: Pastes previously remembered interpretation settings onto the selected footage items.

automation.notes: Needs selected footage items and a remembered interpretation.

features.name: Automatic Footage Reloading
features.summary: Import preference that reloads changed footage when switching back to After Effects: All Footage Types, Non-sequence Footage, or Off.

automation.notes: Stored in preferences; the key name is not documented.

features.name: Conform To Frame Rate / Assume This Frame Rate
features.summary: Overrides the frame rate After Effects reads from a movie or uses for a still sequence, changing playback speed of the item but not the file.

automation.notes: Setting conformFrameRate to 0 returns to the file frame rate.

features.name: Convert To Layered Comp
features.summary: Turns one layer that uses a merged Photoshop or Illustrator file into a composition of the separate source layers, affecting only that instance.

automation.notes: Needs a selected layer whose source is a layered file; no command id was matched.

features.name: Movie (Create Proxy)
features.summary: Queues a render of the selected footage or composition as a movie proxy with the post-render action set to Set Proxy.

automation.notes: Adds a Render Queue item and asks for an output name; rendering is a separate step. Claimed by create_proxy for compositions: a Render Queue item with PostRenderAction.SET_PROXY. RenderQueue.items.add takes only a CompItem, so a movie proxy of a footage item cannot be queued by script.

features.name: Still (Create Proxy)
features.summary: Queues a render of the current frame as a still proxy for the selected footage or composition, with the post-render action set to Set Proxy.

automation.notes: Adds a Render Queue item and asks for an output name; rendering is a separate step. Claimed by create_proxy for compositions: a Render Queue item with PostRenderAction.SET_PROXY over one frame. RenderQueue.items.add takes only a CompItem, so a still proxy of a footage item (which the menu command also offers) cannot be queued by script.

features.name: Edit Original
features.summary: Opens the source of the selected footage item or layer in the application that created it; saved changes update all uses.

automation.notes: Needs a selected footage item or layer and the original application installed.

features.name: FileSource
features.summary: Footage source that points at a file on disk; scripts can read the linked file, see the path of a missing file, and reload it.

automation.notes: FileSource.file and FileSource.missingFootagePath are read-only; reload() re-reads the file.

features.name: Files metadata
features.summary: Editing fields for selected source files in the Metadata panel writes the change straight into those files, including several at once.

automation.notes: Writes to source files on disk; no object-model member covers file XMP.

features.name: FootageItem
features.summary: Scripting class for an imported or generated footage item in the Project panel; it holds a main source, an optional proxy, and methods that swap its source.

features.name: Footage panel
features.summary: Viewer that shows a footage item with its interpretation applied and offers trimming and edit buttons before the item is used in a composition.

automation.notes: Double-click a footage item or press Enter on the numeric keypad to open it.

features.name: Set In Point / Set Out Point
features.summary: Footage panel buttons that mark the part of a movie to use before it is added to a composition.

automation.notes: Footage panel buttons; FootageItem has no In or Out members. Set Layer.inPoint and outPoint after adding the layer instead.

features.name: FootageSource
features.summary: Scripting class behind the Interpret Footage settings of an item: alpha handling, frame rate conforming, field separation, pulldown removal and looping.

features.name: Force alphabetical order
features.summary: Import dialog option that imports a numbered sequence with gaps in its numbering without inserting placeholders for the missing frames.

features.name: 3GPP (.3gp, .3g2, .amc)
features.summary: Import-only mobile video container.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Advanced Authoring Format (.aaf)
features.summary: Import-only interchange format on Windows, handled by Pro Import After Effects.

automation.notes: Import only; Windows only. Claimed by import_files through ImportOptions; Windows only. AAF goes through the Pro Import After Effects importer, which may show its own options dialog; an unattended scripted import is not yet validated.

features.name: Adobe After Effects project (.aep, .aet)
features.summary: Binary projects and project templates that can be imported into an open project; the XML variant is recorded separately.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Adobe Illustrator (.ai, .eps, .ps)
features.summary: Import-only vector format that stays continuously rasterized; layered files can come in as compositions.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Animated GIF (.gif)
features.summary: Import-only animated image format.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: MXF/ARRIRAW
features.summary: Import-only ARRIRAW footage wrapped in MXF from ARRI cameras.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: AVCHD (.m2ts)
features.summary: Import-only camera video format.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Video for Windows (.avi)
features.summary: Movie container; export only on Windows.

automation.notes: Import and export (export Windows only).

features.name: Bitmap (.bmp, .rle, .dib)
features.summary: Import-only still image format.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: BVH
features.summary: Motion data format listed as a data-driven animation input.

automation.notes: Import only. Claimed by import_files through ImportOptions on the strength of the data-driven animation page, which lists BVH. The supported file formats table does not list it, so whether After Effects imports .bvh at all is not yet validated.

features.name: Cinema 4D (.c4d)
features.summary: Cinema 4D scenes import as footage rendered through the Cineware effect and can be exported.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Camera raw (.crw, .nef, .dng, .cr2, .arw and others)
features.summary: Import-only raw camera stills, adjusted through the Camera Raw dialog; sequences use the first file settings.

automation.notes: Import only; opens the Camera Raw dialog. Claimed by import_files through ImportOptions. Interactive import shows the Camera Raw dialog; whether a scripted import with dialogs suppressed uses the default raw settings without it is not yet validated in After Effects.

features.name: Canon Cinema RAW Light (.crm)
features.summary: Import-only raw footage from Canon EOS C200 cameras.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: CinemaDNG
features.summary: Raw video format handled as a subset of Camera Raw, with settings under More Options.

automation.notes: Import only. Claimed by import_files through ImportOptions. CinemaDNG goes through Camera Raw, whose settings dialog appears on interactive import; an unattended scripted import is not yet validated in After Effects.

features.name: Cineon (.cin, .dpx)
features.summary: Film scan format converted to the project bit depth, importable as frames or numbered sequences.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: CSV (.csv)
features.summary: Import-only comma-separated data read with dataValue in expressions.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Avid DNxHD / DNxHR (.mov)
features.summary: Avid codecs in MOV decoded and encoded natively.

automation.notes: Import and native export.

features.name: DV
features.summary: DV in MOV or AVI or as a raw stream; fields are separated automatically.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: ElectricImage IMAGE (.img, .ei)
features.summary: Import-only 3D render image format; matching EIZ depth files are read from the same folder.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Encapsulated PostScript (.eps)
features.summary: Import-only vector format, including CMYK files converted to RGB.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Adobe Animate document (.fla)
features.summary: Animate files import as a composition of per-layer SWF files, with optional WAV audio, when Animate is installed.

automation.notes: Import only; needs Animate 24.0.13 or later installed. Claimed by import_files through ImportOptions. Import needs Adobe Animate 24.0.13 or later installed, which converts the document to SWF layers; without Animate the import fails.

features.name: Adobe Flash Video (.flv, .f4v)
features.summary: Import-only Flash video containers.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: CompuServe GIF (.gif)
features.summary: Import-only still image format.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: GoPro CineForm (.mov)
features.summary: Intermediate codec decoded and encoded natively on macOS and Windows.

automation.notes: Import and native export.

features.name: H.264 (.m4v)
features.summary: Import-only H.264 video; export goes through Media Encoder or the H.264 output module.

automation.notes: Import only per the formats table.

features.name: HEIF (.heif, .heic)
features.summary: Import-only high-efficiency image format, such as iPhone photos, on supported OS versions.

automation.notes: Import only; Windows needs the HEIF and HEVC extensions.

features.name: H.265 / HEVC
features.summary: Import-only HEVC footage in a QuickTime container or MPEG-4.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: IFF (.iff, .tdi)
features.summary: Maya IFF image format supported for import and export.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: JPEG (.jpg, .jpe)
features.summary: Common compressed still image format.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: JSON (.json)
features.summary: Import-only data file used as footage whose values expressions read through sourceData.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: JSX (.jsx)
features.summary: Import-only script file used as a library of expression functions when JSON syntax is too strict.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Maya camera data (.ma)
features.summary: Import-only Maya scene file whose baked camera and locator data become one or two compositions with a camera and nulls.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: mgJSON (.mgjson)
features.summary: Import-only Motion Graphics JSON whose static or time-varying streams appear as Data properties on a layer.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: MPEG-1 (.mpg, .mpe, .mpa, .mpv, .mod)
features.summary: Import-only MPEG-1 video.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: MPEG-2 (.mpg, .m2p, .m2v, .m2a, .m2t)
features.summary: Import-only MPEG-2; some containers such as .vob may import after renaming.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: MPEG-4 (.mp4, .m4v)
features.summary: Import-only MPEG-4 video.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Media eXchange Format (.mxf)
features.summary: Import-only container; supported payloads include P2 Op-Atom and XDCAM HD OP1a.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Open Media Framework (.omf)
features.summary: Raw media (essence) only, Windows only.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: OpenEXR (.exr, .sxr, .mxr)
features.summary: 32-bpc high dynamic range format whose extra layers and channels are reached with the bundled 3D Channel effects.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Panasonic P2 (MXF Op-Atom)
features.summary: Import-only camera media from P2 cards; spanned clips on one card import as a single item and camera metadata shows in the Metadata panel.

automation.notes: Import only; select one MXF file from the VIDEO folder.

features.name: PCX (.pcx)
features.summary: Import-only still image format available on Windows.

automation.notes: Import only; Windows only.

features.name: Adobe PDF (.pdf)
features.summary: Import-only; only the first page is used and it stays continuously rasterized.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Portable Network Graphics (.png)
features.summary: 16-bpc still format with alpha.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Apple ProRes
features.summary: QuickTime codec natively decoded and encoded, including Rec. 2020 PQ/HLG HDR files on Windows.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Adobe Premiere (.prproj)
features.summary: Premiere projects import as a composition plus folders of clips.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Adobe Photoshop (.psd)
features.summary: Layered image format at 8, 16 or 32 bpc that imports flattened or as a composition keeping layers, styles and masks.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: QuickTime (.mov)
features.summary: Movie container decoded and encoded natively for many codecs, including GoPro CineForm, DNxHD/DNxHR and ProRes.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Radiance (.hdr, .rgbe, .xyze)
features.summary: 32-bpc high dynamic range image format.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: RED (.r3d)
features.summary: Import-only RED camera raw footage interpreted as 32-bpc Rec. 709, with RED source settings.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Discreet RLA/RPF (.rla, .rpf)
features.summary: Import-only 16-bpc 3D render format that carries auxiliary channels and camera data.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: SGI (.sgi, .bw, .rgb)
features.summary: 16-bpc still image format.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Softimage (.pic)
features.summary: Import-only 3D render format; a ZPIC file in the same folder supplies depth.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Sony X-OCN (.mxf)
features.summary: Import-only Sony VENICE and X-OCN camera footage, including anamorphic 4K and 6K modes.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: SVG (.svg)
features.summary: Import-only vector format that arrives as live-linked footage or as a composition of editable shape layers.

automation.notes: Import only; listed as beta.

features.name: Adobe Flash Player (.swf)
features.summary: Import-only; keyframed root animation comes in as one continuously rasterized layer with alpha, without audio or interactivity.

automation.notes: Import only; export was removed after CC 2014.

features.name: Targa (.tga, .vda, .icb, .vst)
features.summary: Still image format with alpha support.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: TIFF (.tif)
features.summary: 8- and 16-bpc still image format.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: TSV (.tsv, .txt)
features.summary: Import-only tab-separated data read with dataValue in expressions.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Vanishing Point (.vpe)
features.summary: Photoshop Vanishing Point export that rebuilds the scene as a camera plus perspective-corrected 3D layers.

automation.notes: Import only.

features.name: Windows Media (.wmv, .wma, .asf, .asx)
features.summary: Import-only Windows Media files on Windows.

automation.notes: Import only; Windows only.

features.name: XDCAM HD and XDCAM EX (.mxf, .mp4)
features.summary: Import-only Sony XDCAM media recorded to MXF or as EX .mp4 essence files.

automation.notes: Import only; XDCAM HD in IMX format is not supported.

features.name: XML (.xml)
features.summary: XML files listed for import and export, such as Final Cut Pro 7 sequences through Pro Import After Effects.

automation.notes: Import and export.

features.name: Guess 3:2 Pulldown / Guess 24Pa Pulldown
features.summary: Buttons in the Interpret Footage dialog that analyse separated footage and pick the pulldown phase automatically.

features.name: Adobe Premiere Project
features.summary: Imports a Premiere project as a composition of its clips plus a folder of footage items, with an option to pick one sequence and to import audio.

automation.notes: Opens a file dialog filtered to Premiere projects, then an options dialog. The menu id for this item is in the plug-in range (5000-5999) and is not cited. Opens a dialog; plug-in command id from the 2025 list (5012 in 2015). Claimed by import_files (Project.importFile with a .prproj). The File > Import > Adobe Premiere Pro Project menu command (plug-in id range) opens a file dialog and an options dialog for choosing a sequence and audio; the scripted import cannot choose a single sequence, and whether the importer shows its options dialog under app.beginSuppressDialogs is not yet validated.

features.name: Import After Effects project
features.summary: Importing an .aep into the open project places all its compositions, footage and folders into a new folder; a movie that embeds a project link can also be imported As Project.

features.name: Import As
features.summary: Import dialog menu choosing how a file arrives: as flattened Footage, as a Composition with layers at frame size, as a Composition retaining layer sizes, or as a Project.

features.name: Import by dragging
features.summary: Dragging files or folders from Explorer or Finder into the Project panel imports them; a folder becomes one image sequence, or separate items when Alt/Option is held while dragging.

automation.notes: Drag gesture from the operating system; the scripted equivalent is Project.importFile with ImportOptions.

features.name: File
features.summary: Opens the Import File dialog to bring one file, a still-image sequence or a folder into the project as footage.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog. Id 2003 is shared by Import > File, Replace Footage > File and Set Proxy > File; the menu acts on the current context. importFile() imports without a dialog.

features.name: Import into a project folder
features.summary: Right-clicking a Project panel folder and choosing Import, or pressing the import shortcut with the folder selected, places the new items directly inside that folder.

automation.notes: Scripts import and then set parentFolder on the new item.

features.name: Multiple Files
features.summary: Keeps the import dialog open so several files or sequences can be imported one after another without reopening the command.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog that stays open until dismissed; scripts call Project.importFile repeatedly instead.

features.name: ImportOptions
features.summary: Scripting class describing a file to import and how: as footage, composition or project, as a sequence, and with forced alphabetical order.

features.name: Placeholder
features.summary: Adds a color-bar placeholder item of a chosen size, frame rate and duration to stand in for footage that is not available yet.

automation.notes: Opens a dialog for name, size, frame rate and duration. Id 2126 is also used by Replace Footage > Placeholder.

features.name: Solid
features.summary: Creates a solid-color footage item in the project without adding a layer to any composition.

automation.notes: Opens the Solid Settings dialog. Id 3000 is shared with Replace Footage > Solid. No ItemCollection method creates a bare solid item; LayerCollection.addSolid creates the item together with a layer.

features.name: Sequence (import option)
features.summary: Import dialog option that treats numbered stills in one folder as frames of a single footage item; it also lists Multiple Sequences for importing several sequences at once.

automation.notes: The Multiple Sequences checkbox has no matching ImportOptions member.

features.name: Main
features.summary: Opens the Interpret Footage dialog for the selected item to set alpha, frame rate, fields and pulldown, pixel aspect ratio, looping and color handling.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; needs a selected footage item. Scripts set the FootageSource attributes directly.

features.name: Proxy
features.summary: Opens the Interpret Footage dialog for the proxy assigned to the selected item rather than its main source.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; needs a footage item with a proxy. Alt/Option-clicking the Interpret Footage button does the same.

features.name: Interpretation rules file
features.summary: A text file of rules (interpretation rules.txt) that sets default interpretation per file type or codec at import; it is edited outside the app while After Effects is closed.

automation.notes: Plain-text configuration edited by hand; nothing in the object model or menus changes it.

features.name: Invert Alpha
features.summary: Swaps the opaque and transparent areas defined by the footage alpha channel.

features.name: Loop
features.summary: Repeats a footage item a whole number of times so one cycle can play continuously.

features.name: Metadata Display
features.summary: Metadata panel menu dialog to show or hide schemas and properties, save, switch and delete display sets, and create custom schemas with Integer, Real, Text or Boolean properties.

automation.notes: Panel-only display configuration with no member or command id.

features.name: Metadata
features.summary: Panel listing static XMP metadata for the project at the top and for selected source files below, editable per schema.

features.name: More Options
features.summary: Button in Interpret Footage that opens format-specific settings, such as the Camera Raw dialog for raw and CinemaDNG files or anti-aliasing quality for Illustrator files.

automation.notes: Opens a format-specific modal dialog (for example Camera Raw); no member.

features.name: Maxon Cinema 4D File
features.summary: Creates a new .c4d file, imports it as footage and opens it in Cinema 4D for editing.

automation.notes: Opens a save dialog and launches Cinema 4D. File > New > Maxon Cinema 4D File... (command 4007) opens a save dialog for the new .c4d file before launching Cinema 4D. No object-model method creates the file, so nothing reaches it unattended.

features.name: Adobe Photoshop File
features.summary: Creates a blank PSD matching the most recent composition, imports it as footage and opens it in Photoshop.

automation.notes: Opens a save dialog and launches Photoshop. File > New > Adobe Photoshop File... (command 3147) opens a save dialog for the new PSD before importing it and launching Photoshop. No object-model method creates the linked PSD, so nothing reaches it unattended.

features.name: Overlay Edit
features.summary: Footage panel button that adds the trimmed footage as the top layer starting at the current time without moving other layers.

automation.notes: LayerCollection.add places the new layer at the top of the stack (honouring the Create Layers at Composition Start Time preference); shift Layer.startTime so it starts at the composition's current time and trim it with inPoint and outPoint. The Footage panel trim itself cannot be read.

features.name: Paste SVG content
features.summary: Edit > Paste turns SVG data on the clipboard, for example artwork copied from Illustrator with Include SVG Code on, into native shape layers in a new or selected composition.

automation.notes: Uses the general Edit > Paste command (id 20); result depends on whether a project and composition are open.

features.name: Editable Layer Styles / Merge Layer Styles Into Footage
features.summary: Choice offered when importing a PSD that uses layer styles: keep supported styles editable, or bake them into the footage for faster rendering and 3D compatibility.

automation.notes: The import dialog's choice for composition imports is remembered in section "Choose Layer Dialog", key "PSD Comp Layer Styles Option v2" (PREF_Type_MACHINE_SPECIFIC; 0 Editable Layer Styles, 1 Merge Layer Styles Into Footage). A published reader of these files records that Project.importFile follows the last choice; setting the key before importing is unverified.

features.name: Pixel Aspect Ratio (Interpret Footage)
features.summary: Sets the pixel aspect ratio assumed for a footage item, such as Square, D1/DV NTSC or PAL, Anamorphic 2:1 or HDV 1.33.

features.name: Placeholder for render output
features.summary: Dragging an output module from the Render Queue to the Project panel creates a placeholder that the rendered file replaces automatically.

automation.notes: Drag gesture; the post-render action becomes Import & Replace Usage (OutputModule.postRenderAction can set that action but not create the placeholder).

features.name: PlaceholderItem
features.summary: Project item standing in for footage that is missing or not yet available, shown as color bars until replaced.

features.name: Drag Import Multiple Items As
features.summary: Import preference that decides whether dragged layered or SVG files arrive as Footage, Composition, or Composition - Retain Layer Sizes.

features.name: Interpret Unlabeled Alpha As
features.summary: Import preference for footage whose alpha type is not labeled: Ask User, Guess, Ignore Alpha, Straight, or Premultiplied with black or white.

features.name: Footage Interpretation on Replacement
features.summary: Import preference choosing whether replacing footage resets interpretation to defaults or keeps the previous settings.

features.name: Report Missing Frames
features.summary: Import preference that warns about gaps in an image sequence and fills them with placeholders.

features.name: Sequence Footage frame rate
features.summary: Import preference giving the frame rate assumed for imported image sequences (30 fps by default).

automation.notes: Section "Import Options Preference Section", key "Import Options Default Sequence FPS", file PREF_Type_MACHINE_INDEPENDENT; factory value 30. Writing it is unverified.

features.name: Still Footage
features.summary: Import preference for the default layer duration of stills: the composition length or a custom duration.

automation.notes: Section "Main Pref Section v2", key "Pref_DEFAULT_STILL_OUT_POINT v2", file PREF_Type_MACHINE_INDEPENDENT; the value is a "value/scale" string (75/25 gives 3 seconds, 0/0 means the composition length). Writing it is unverified.

features.name: Verify Individual Files
features.summary: Slower import preference that checks every file of a sequence, catching unresolved aliases or offline files.

features.name: Preserve Edges (Best Quality Only)
features.summary: Improves quality in still areas of field-separated footage when rendered at Best quality.

features.name: Pro Import After Effects
features.summary: Bundled importer for AAF and OMF sequences from Avid, Final Cut Pro 7 XML and Motion projects.

automation.notes: Plug-in importer that opens a file dialog and its own options dialog; its menu id is install-specific (5013).

features.name: Project metadata
features.summary: XMP properties attached to the project file, shown in Bridge and embeddable in rendered output.

features.name: Reload Footage
features.summary: Re-reads the selected footage items from disk so edits made in other applications appear.

automation.notes: Needs selected footage items.

features.name: Remember Interpretation
features.summary: Copies the interpretation settings of the selected footage item so they can be applied to other items.

automation.notes: Needs one selected footage item.

features.name: Remove (pulldown)
features.summary: Removes 3:2 or 24Pa pulldown from separated video by choosing the phase of whole and split frames.

features.name: File (Replace Footage)
features.summary: Points the selected footage item at a different file, updating every layer that uses it while keeping layer changes.

automation.notes: Opens a file dialog; needs a selected footage item. Id 2003 is shared with Import > File and Set Proxy > File.

features.name: Placeholder (Replace Footage)
features.summary: Swaps the selected footage item for a color-bar placeholder.

automation.notes: Opens a placeholder settings dialog; id 2126 is shared with Import > Placeholder.

features.name: Solid (Replace Footage)
features.summary: Swaps the selected footage item for a solid-color source.

automation.notes: Opens Solid Settings; id 3000 is shared with Import > Solid.

features.name: With Layered Comp
features.summary: Converts every use of a merged layered-file footage item into a composition built from the file layers.

automation.notes: Needs a selected footage item from a layered PSD or AI file; may take a moment.

features.name: Reveal In Composition
features.summary: From a footage item, jumps to a chosen layer instance that uses it inside a composition.

automation.notes: AVItem.usedIn lists the compositions that use the item; open one with CompItem.openInViewer and select the layer whose source is the item. The context-menu ids are negative and install-specific.

features.name: Reveal in Explorer / Reveal in Finder
features.summary: Shows the source file of the selected footage item in the operating system file browser (Bridge has its own Reveal command).

automation.notes: Needs a selected footage item; one id covers the Windows and macOS names.

features.name: Ripple Insert Edit
features.summary: Footage panel button that adds the trimmed footage at the current time and splits and pushes later material to make room.

automation.notes: Needs an open Footage panel and an active composition.

features.name: Scene Edit Detection
features.summary: Analyses selected video layers for cuts and either marks them, splits the layer at each cut, or splits and precomposes each scene.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog; needs selected video footage layers (not precomps or time-remapped layers). Uses Adobe Sensei analysis.

features.name: Create Layer Markers
features.summary: Scene Edit Detection option that adds numbered Segmentation markers at each detected cut.

features.name: Create Pre-comps
features.summary: With layer splitting, precomposes each scene and files the new compositions in a Scene Edit Detection folder.

features.name: Split Layer at Scene Edit
features.summary: Scene Edit Detection option that cuts the layer into one layer per detected scene.

features.name: Separate Fields
features.summary: Splits interlaced frames into full frames per field, using Upper Field First or Lower Field First, or turns field separation off.

features.name: File (Set Proxy)
features.summary: Assigns a file, often a smaller movie or still, as a stand-in for the selected footage item during previews and test renders.

automation.notes: Opens a file dialog; needs a selected item. Id 2003 is shared with Import > File and Replace Footage > File.

features.name: None (Set Proxy)
features.summary: Removes the proxy from the selected footage item.

automation.notes: Needs a selected item that has a proxy.

features.name: SolidSource
features.summary: Footage source of a solid-color footage item; its color can be read and changed by script.

features.name: SVG import options
features.summary: When importing SVG, choose Footage (one continuously rasterized, live-linked layer) or Composition - Retain Layer Sizes (editable shape layers), plus Create Composition and Scalable Vector Graphics Sequence.

automation.notes: SVG import is listed as beta on the formats page; whether ImportOptions.importAs drives it is not documented.

features.name: Proxy indicator
features.summary: Clicking the box beside an item name switches between using its proxy and its original footage everywhere in the project.

features.name: Write XMP IDs to Files on Import
features.summary: Disk preference that stamps a unique ID into source files on import so caches and previews can be shared.

automation.notes: Changes the modification date of imported files the first time.

features.name: Create Layer Markers from Footage XMP Metadata
features.summary: Disk preference that turns temporal XMP metadata into layer markers when a layer is created from the footage.

domains.name: Compositions
domains.covers: Creating and setting compositions, nesting and pre-composing, the work area, composition flowchart and markers.

features.name: Adaptive Sample Limit
features.summary: Maximum number of motion blur samples per frame.

features.name: Add Marker (composition)
