features.summary: With no layer selected, places a composition marker in the time ruler at the current time, even during previews.

automation.notes: Acts on the composition only when no layer is selected; can be dragged from the Comp Marker Bin too.

features.name: Add Marker (layer)
features.summary: Places a layer marker at the current time on each selected layer.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers.

features.name: Anchor (Advanced)
features.summary: Arrow buttons that pin existing layers to a corner or edge when the composition frame is resized.

automation.notes: Composition Settings dialog control; resizing with CompItem.width and height keeps layers relative to the top-left, so a script must reposition layers itself.

features.name: Background Color
features.summary: Color shown behind the layers of a composition; it becomes transparent when the composition is nested.

features.name: Duration (Composition Settings)
features.summary: Length of the composition, limited to three hours.

features.name: Frame Rate (Composition Settings)
features.summary: Number of frames per second at which the composition samples its layers and allows keyframes, up to 999 fps.

features.name: Width and Height
features.summary: Frame size of the composition in pixels, up to 30,000 x 30,000, with an option to lock the aspect ratio.

features.name: CompItem
features.summary: Scripting class for a composition: its frame size, frame rate, duration, work area, background color, motion blur and renderer settings, plus its layers and markers.

features.name: Pixel Aspect Ratio (Composition Settings)
features.summary: Pixel shape used by the composition, which should match the output format.

features.name: Resolution (Composition Settings)
features.summary: Default sampling resolution (Full, Half, Third, Quarter or Custom) for rendering the composition.

features.name: Start Timecode / Start Frame
features.summary: Timecode or frame number given to the first frame of the composition; it changes counting only, not rendering.

features.name: Composition Flowchart
features.summary: Opens the Flowchart panel for the selected composition, showing its footage, layers and nested compositions as connected tiles.

automation.notes: The Flowchart panel only displays relationships; it cannot change them.

features.name: Composition Mini-Flowchart
features.summary: Pop-up map of the compositions directly upstream and downstream of the active one, navigated with arrow keys, with S switching sort order.

automation.notes: Needs an active Composition, Layer or Timeline panel. Composition Mini-Flowchart (command 3792) opens a transient pop-up navigator that is driven with the arrow keys and closes on the next click; it shows relationships and changes nothing, so running it unattended has no result. The relationships it shows are readable from CompItem.usedIn and the layers' sources, and the Composition Flowchart panel is opened by run_comp_command (show_flowchart).

features.name: Composition Navigator
features.summary: Bar at the top of the Composition panel showing the active composition within its chain of nested compositions, with names you click to switch.

automation.notes: Shown or hidden with Show Composition Navigator in the Composition panel menu; display-only with no member or id.

features.name: Preset (Composition Settings)
features.summary: Menu of composition presets, including social-platform sizes, that fills in width, height, pixel aspect ratio and frame rate; custom presets can be saved or deleted, and Alt/Option-click restores the defaults.

automation.notes: Preset menu of the Composition Settings dialog; presets are stored in the preferences file and no member lists them. Scripts set the values a preset fills in (width, height, pixel aspect ratio, frame rate) with the CompItem members.

features.name: Composition Settings
features.summary: Dialog with Basic, Advanced and 3D Renderer tabs for changing the size, timing, color and rendering options of the selected or active composition.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; needs a selected or active composition. Each option maps to a CompItem attribute.

features.name: Crop Comp To Region Of Interest
menu_path: Crop Comp To Region Of Interest
features.summary: Changes the composition frame to the region of interest drawn in the Composition panel.

automation.notes: Needs a region of interest to be set in the viewer.

features.name: Crop Comp to Selected Layer(s) Bounds
menu_path: Crop Comp to Selected Layer(s) Bounds
features.summary: Changes the composition frame size so it matches the visible bounds of the selected 2D layers, cropping or enlarging as needed.

automation.notes: Needs selected 2D layers; not available for 3D layers. No command id matched.

features.name: Delete All Markers
features.summary: Removes every marker from the selected layers or the composition.

automation.notes: Context menu on a marker; scripts remove keys of the marker property in a loop.

features.name: Duplicate composition
features.summary: Makes a copy of the selected composition in the Project panel.

automation.notes: Needs a selected composition; id 2080 is the general Edit > Duplicate command.

features.name: Enable Motion Blur (composition)
features.summary: Composition switch that lets layers with the motion blur switch on actually render motion blur in the viewer.

features.name: Extract Work Area
features.summary: Removes the part of layers inside the work area and closes the gap by moving later material earlier.

automation.notes: Acts on selected layers, or all layers when none are selected.

features.name: Flow Right To Left / Flow Left To Right
features.summary: Composition panel menu choice for the direction compositions are ordered in the navigator bar and Mini-Flowchart; applies globally.

automation.notes: Panel menu display preference with no member or id.

features.name: Frame Render Time
features.summary: Timeline footer readout of the total time needed to render the current frame.

automation.notes: Always-visible readout; no scripting member.

features.name: Go to composition marker
features.summary: Moves the current time to numbered composition marker 0-9.

features.name: Lift Work Area
features.summary: Removes the part of selected layers inside the work area and leaves an empty gap of the same length.

automation.notes: Acts on selected layers, or all layers when none are selected.

features.name: Lock Markers
features.summary: Locks all markers on a layer or composition so they cannot be moved.

automation.notes: Context menu on a marker. Lock Markers (command 2565) is an item of the context menu of a marker the user right-clicks in the Timeline panel; run unattended there is no clicked marker for it to act on, and MarkerValue has no lock member (only protectedRegion), so neither a command nor the object model can lock markers.

features.name: Chapter (marker)
features.summary: Chapter name written as a chapter point when rendering to formats that support chapters.

features.name: Comment (marker)
features.summary: Text label of a marker; composition markers default to a number and layer markers to empty.

features.name: Cue point (marker)
features.summary: Cue point name, type (event or navigation) and parameter pairs embedded in output that supports cue points.

features.name: Marker dialog
features.summary: Composition Marker or Layer Marker dialog for editing a marker time, duration, comment, chapter, web link, cue point, label and protected region.

automation.notes: Opens by double-clicking a marker or with Alt/Option+Numpad * at the current time.

features.name: Duration (marker)
features.summary: Makes a marker span a length of time, set in the dialog or by dragging its out point.

features.name: Label (marker)
features.summary: Color label assigned to a marker from the label colors defined in Preferences > Labels.

features.name: Comment Marker / Segmentation Marker
features.summary: Marker type choice in the Layer Marker dialog; Scene Edit Detection creates Segmentation markers, each type with its own default label color.

features.name: MarkerValue
features.summary: Scripting class holding the data of a composition or layer marker: comment, duration, chapter, URL, cue point, label and protected region.

features.name: URL and Frame Target (marker)
features.summary: Web link and target frame name that become web links in output formats that support them.

features.name: Migrating custom composition presets
features.summary: Custom presets from before the 23.0 preset overhaul are carried over by copying their entries between preset sections of the composition preferences text file while the app is closed.

automation.notes: Manual edit of a preferences text file outside the application.

features.name: Nesting
features.summary: Adding a composition to another composition makes it a precomposition layer whose changes flow to every place it is used.

features.name: New Comp from Selection
features.summary: Builds one composition from selected footage, or one per item, using the item size and frame rate; options include Use Dimensions From, Still Duration, Add to Render Queue and Sequence Layers with overlap and transition.

automation.notes: Opens a dialog when several items are selected; dragging items onto the new-composition button in the Project panel does the same.

features.name: New Composition
features.summary: Creates an empty composition after you fill in the Composition Settings dialog.

automation.notes: Opens the Composition Settings dialog; addComp() creates a composition without it.

features.name: Set numbered composition marker
features.summary: Adds composition marker 0-9 at the current time, or moves it there if that number already exists.

features.name: Pre-compose
features.summary: Moves the selected layers into a new composition that replaces them with a single precomposition layer.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog; needs selected layers.

features.name: Leave all attributes in
features.summary: Pre-compose option for a single layer that keeps its properties and keyframes on the new precomposition layer, sized to the layer.

automation.notes: Passing moveAllAttributes=false; not available for several layers, text or shape layers.

features.name: Move all attributes into the new composition
features.summary: Pre-compose option that keeps the layer properties inside the new composition, which takes the original composition frame size.

automation.notes: Passing moveAllAttributes=true.

features.name: Switches Affect Nested Comps
features.summary: Composition preference that lets quality, effect, frame blending and motion blur switches propagate into nested compositions.

features.name: Synchronize Time of All Related Items
features.summary: Composition preference that moves the current time in all compositions related by nesting together.

features.name: Preserve resolution when nested
features.summary: Keeps a nested composition at its own resolution instead of inheriting the containing composition setting.

features.name: Activate most recently active related composition
features.summary: Switches to the composition most recently active in the same nesting network.

automation.notes: Keyboard command with no menu item, so no command id; no member covers it. The activation history is not exposed; CompItem.openInViewer activates a known composition.

features.name: Delete This Marker
features.summary: Removes a single composition or layer marker; Ctrl/Cmd-clicking or dragging to the Comp Marker Bin also works.

automation.notes: Context menu on a marker.

features.name: Render Time column (Composition Profiler)
features.summary: Timeline column that profiles how long each layer, and within it each mask, style and effect, took to render the current frame, color-coded from green to red.

automation.notes: Shown via the snail button or Columns > Render Time; display-only. Cached items are marked with an asterisk.

features.name: Reveal Composition In Project
features.summary: Selects the active composition in the Project panel from the Composition or Timeline panel context menu.

automation.notes: The hyperbrew name RevealCompInPW is read as Reveal Composition in Project panel.

features.name: Samples Per Frame
features.summary: Minimum motion blur sample count used when adaptive sampling cannot be determined, as for 3D and shape layers.

features.name: Scale Composition.jsx
features.summary: Bundled script that scales a whole composition and its layers by a factor.

automation.notes: Runs from File > Scripts; fails if any layer in the composition is locked.

features.name: Set Poster Time
features.summary: Uses the frame at the current time as the composition thumbnail in the Project panel.

automation.notes: Needs an active composition.

features.name: Shutter Angle
features.summary: Simulated shutter opening in degrees that sets how much motion blur layers receive.

features.name: Shutter Phase
features.summary: Offset in degrees for when the simulated shutter opens relative to the frame start.

features.name: Trim Comp to Work Area
features.summary: Shortens the composition duration to match its work area.

automation.notes: Needs an active composition.

features.name: Update Markers From Source
features.summary: Replaces a layer markers with those of its source: the nested composition markers or the source file XMP metadata, discarding added markers.

automation.notes: Needs a layer whose source has markers or XMP metadata.

features.name: Work area
features.summary: The part of the composition duration rendered for previews and output; its start and end can be set at the current time, dragged, or expanded to the full length by double-clicking.

automation.notes: B sets the start and N sets the end at the current time.

features.name: Set work area to selected layers
features.summary: Fits the work area to the span of the selected layers, or to the whole composition when none are selected.

automation.notes: Keyboard-only command; scripts compute the span from Layer.inPoint and outPoint.

domains.name: Layers
domains.covers: Layer types (solid, null, adjustment, shape, text, camera, light), layer properties and switches, parenting, blending modes, track mattes and arrangement.

features.name: Adjustment Layer switch
features.summary: Converts a layer to an adjustment layer (or back to a normal layer) so its effects apply to the layers beneath it.

features.name: Align layers
features.summary: Lines up selected layers by their left, center or right edges or top, center or bottom edges, against the outermost selected layer or the composition frame.

automation.notes: Needs two or more selected layers (one when aligning to the composition). Text characters within a layer are not affected.

features.name: Align panel
features.summary: Panel with buttons to align or distribute selected layers relative to the selection or to the composition (Align Layers To menu).

automation.notes: Opens the panel from the Window menu. Its menu ids are install-specific (5014, 5049 in the published lists), so look up by name with app.findMenuCommandId("Align"). Its align and distribute buttons cannot be pressed by scripts. Locked layers are not moved.

features.name: Duplicate layers with Alt/Option-drag
features.summary: Duplicates a layer by Alt/Option-dragging it in the Composition panel (2D and 3D); in 3D compositions a preference or a one-time prompt decides whether the gesture duplicates or navigates the camera.

automation.notes: Beta feature at the time of the help page; an interactive drag with no member or command. Layer.duplicate is the scripted equivalent of duplicating.

features.name: Anchor Point
features.summary: The point around which a layer scales and rotates; it can be dragged in the Layer panel, nudged with arrow keys in the Layer panel, or moved without moving the layer by using the Pan Behind tool. Press A to reveal it.

features.name: Audio switch
features.summary: Speaker switch in the A/V Features column that mutes or unmutes a layer with audio.

features.name: Auto-Orient
features.summary: Sets how a layer orientation follows motion: Off, Orient Along Path, Orient Towards Camera (3D layers) or Orient Towards Point Of Interest (cameras and lights).

automation.notes: Modal dialog; needs selected layers. The macOS shortcut on the shortcut page reads Command+Alt+O, so it is omitted here.

features.name: AVLayer
features.summary: Scripting class for layers that have visual or audio content (footage, solids, precomps, shapes, text), adding blending mode, quality, track matte, switches and source access to the base layer.

features.name: Blend Interior Styles As Group
features.summary: When on, interior styles (Inner Glow, Inner Shadow, Color Overlay, Gradient Overlay, Satin, Bevel And Emboss) use the layer blending mode.

features.name: Add
features.summary: Sums layer and underlying channel values, so the result is never darker than either input.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Alpha Add
features.summary: Composites normally but sums complementary alpha channels to remove seams where inverted mattes or edge-to-edge layers meet.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Classic Color Burn
features.summary: The Color Burn math from After Effects 5.0 and earlier, kept for old projects.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Classic Color Dodge
features.summary: The Color Dodge math from After Effects 5.0 and earlier, kept for old projects.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Classic Difference
features.summary: The Difference math from After Effects 5.0 and earlier, kept for old projects.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Color
features.summary: Takes hue and saturation from the layer and luminosity from beneath, preserving gray levels; handy for tinting.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Color Burn
features.summary: Darkens by raising contrast so the result reflects the underlying color; white in the layer has no effect.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Color Dodge
features.summary: Brightens by lowering contrast to reflect the underlying color; black in the layer has no effect.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Dancing Dissolve
features.summary: Like Dissolve but the random pixel pattern is regenerated every frame, so it flickers over time.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Darken
features.summary: Keeps, channel by channel, whichever of the layer and underlying values is darker.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Darker Color
features.summary: Picks the darker of the two whole colors per pixel rather than comparing channels separately.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Difference
features.summary: Subtracts the darker input from the lighter one per channel; useful for lining up two identical layers until the result turns black.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Dissolve
features.summary: Shows each pixel as either the layer color or the underlying color at random, with the chance tied to opacity; not available on 3D layers.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Divide
features.summary: Divides the underlying color by the layer color; in 32-bpc projects results can exceed 1.0.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Exclusion
features.summary: A lower-contrast version of Difference: white inverts the underlying color and black leaves it unchanged.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Hard Light
features.summary: Multiplies or screens depending on the color values, giving a harsh spotlight look useful for adding shadows.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Hard Mix
features.summary: Pushes the contrast of the underlying layer visible beneath a mask on the layer.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Hue
features.summary: Takes the hue from the layer and the luminosity and saturation from the underlying color.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Lighten
features.summary: Keeps, channel by channel, whichever of the layer and underlying values is lighter.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Lighter Color
features.summary: Picks the lighter of the two whole colors per pixel rather than comparing channels separately.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Linear Burn
features.summary: Darkens by lowering brightness to reflect the underlying color; white has no effect.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Linear Dodge
features.summary: Brightens by raising brightness to reflect the underlying color; black has no effect.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Linear Light
features.summary: Burns or dodges by changing brightness according to whether the underlying color is above or below mid gray.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Luminescent Premul
features.summary: Keeps color values that exceed alpha after compositing, useful for premultiplied light effects such as lens flares.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Luminosity
features.summary: Takes luminosity from the layer and hue and saturation from beneath, the inverse of Color.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Blending Mode
features.summary: Submenu (also the Mode column menu in the Timeline panel) for choosing how selected layers combine with the layers beneath; modes are grouped by dividers into eight categories and cannot be keyframed.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. To change modes over time, split the layer.

features.name: Multiply
features.summary: Multiplies layer and underlying channel values, always darkening; black stays black and white leaves the other color unchanged.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Normal
features.summary: Default mode: the layer color replaces what is beneath, mixing only where opacity is below 100%.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Overlay
features.summary: Multiplies or screens depending on whether the underlying color is darker or lighter than mid gray, keeping its highlights and shadows.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Pin Light
features.summary: Replaces colors selectively: darker pixels are replaced over light areas and lighter pixels over dark areas.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Saturation
features.summary: Takes the saturation from the layer and the luminosity and hue from the underlying color.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Screen
features.summary: Inverts both inputs, multiplies them and inverts the product, brightening like overlapping projected images.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. GPU-accelerated in 32 bpc when the layer has motion blur.

features.name: Silhouette Alpha
features.summary: Uses the layer alpha channel to punch a hole through all layers beneath it.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed. The enum value is spelled SILHOUETE_ALPHA in the object model.

features.name: Silhouette Luma
features.summary: Uses the layer luminance to punch holes through all layers beneath, brighter areas becoming more transparent.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Soft Light
features.summary: Gently darkens or lightens the underlying layer depending on whether the layer color is below or above mid gray, like a diffuse spotlight.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Stencil Alpha
features.summary: Uses the layer alpha channel as a stencil so all layers beneath show only inside it.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Stencil Luma
features.summary: Uses the layer luminance as a stencil for all layers beneath, brighter areas being more opaque.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Subtract
features.summary: Removes the layer color from the underlying color; in 32-bpc projects results can go below zero.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Vivid Light
features.summary: Burns or dodges by changing contrast according to whether the underlying color is above or below mid gray.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; blending modes cannot be keyframed.

features.name: Bring Layer Forward
features.summary: Moves selected layers up one position in the stacking order.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name MoveUp (BringForward before 2020).

features.name: Bring Layer To Front
features.summary: Moves selected layers to the top of the stacking order.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name MoveToTop (BringtoFront before 2020).

features.name: Center Anchor Point In Layer Content
menu_path: Center Anchor Point In Layer Content
features.summary: Moves the anchor point to the center of the visible content (a shape, text block or masked area) without moving the layer.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. Ctrl/Cmd-double-clicking the Pan Behind tool does the same.

features.name: Center In View
features.summary: Moves selected layers so their anchor points land at the center of the current view.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Collapse Transformations / Continuously Rasterize
features.summary: Switch that collapses transformations for precomposition layers and makes vector-based layers (Illustrator, PDF, EPS, SWF) re-rasterize every frame so they stay sharp when scaled up; it also moves effects after transforms in the render order.

automation.notes: Shape and text layers are always continuously rasterized. Continuously rasterized layers cannot be opened in the Layer panel. Hyperbrew name Collapse.

features.name: Convert To Editable Styles
features.summary: Turns layer styles merged from an imported Photoshop layer into editable After Effects layer styles.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers based on Photoshop layers; id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list.

features.name: Create layers from footage items
features.summary: Turns selected Project panel items (footage, solids or compositions) into layers by dragging them to the Composition or Timeline panel or onto a composition; with Shift held while dragging the layer snaps to the frame center or edges, or its In point to the current time.

automation.notes: The shortcut adds selected items to the most recently active composition, above the selected layer or at the top of the stack.

features.name: Cycle blending modes
features.summary: Steps selected layers forward or backward through the blending mode list for quick comparison.

automation.notes: Main-keyboard hyphen and equal-sign keys. 2781 NextBlendingMode and 2782 PreviousBlendingMode.

features.name: Distribute layers
features.summary: Spaces three or more selected layers evenly between the two outermost ones by edges or centers.

automation.notes: Needs three or more selected layers; spacing can be uneven for layers of different sizes.

features.name: Duplicate
features.summary: Copies selected layers in one step, including effects, masks, keyframes and expressions; a layer duplicated with its track matte keeps their relative order.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; the same command duplicates masks, effects and shapes when those are selected.

features.name: Edit Value
features.summary: Context-menu dialog on an underlined property value that sets it numerically and lets you change its units (for example pixels or % of composition).

automation.notes: Modal dialog; not every property supports alternate units. Unit choice itself has no known member.

features.name: Effect switch
features.summary: Switch that renders or bypasses all effects on a layer without changing the on/off state of the individual effects.

features.name: Exclude channels from blending
features.summary: Turns the Red, Green or Blue switches in Advanced Blending off so that channel of the layer does not take part in blending; the switches can be animated.

features.name: Extend selection to next layer
features.summary: Adds the next layer down the stacking order to the current selection.

features.name: Extend selection to previous layer
features.summary: Adds the next layer up the stacking order to the current selection.

features.name: Fit To Comp
features.summary: Scales and centers selected layers so they exactly fill the composition frame, ignoring aspect ratio.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Fit To Comp Height
features.summary: Scales and centers selected layers to the composition height while keeping each layer aspect ratio.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Fit To Comp Width
features.summary: Scales and centers selected layers to the composition width while keeping each layer aspect ratio.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Flip Horizontal
features.summary: Mirrors selected layers left to right by negating the horizontal Scale value, around the anchor point.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; a script negates the x component of Scale.

features.name: Flip Vertical
features.summary: Mirrors selected layers top to bottom by negating the vertical Scale value, around the anchor point.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers; a script negates the y component of Scale.

features.name: Guide Layer
features.summary: Turns selected layers into guide layers that are visible in the Composition panel for reference but skipped in output unless the render settings include guide layers; guide layers in nested compositions are not shown upstream.

features.name: Hide Other Video
features.summary: Turns the Video switch off for every layer except the selected ones.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers.

features.name: Hide Shy Layers
features.summary: Timeline composition switch that hides every layer whose Shy switch is on from the layer outline, or shows them again.

features.name: Invert Selection
features.summary: Deselects the selected layers and selects all the others in the composition.

automation.notes: Needs at least one selected layer; also in the Composition panel context menu.

features.name: LayerCollection
features.summary: Ordered collection of the layers in a composition, used by scripts to create new layers of each type and to look layers up by name.

features.name: Layer comment
features.summary: Free-text comment stored on a layer and shown in the Comments column of the Timeline panel, useful for notes and tagging.

features.name: Layer label color
features.summary: Colored label shown in the Label column of the Timeline panel, used to group and identify layers.

automation.notes: Label colors and their names are set in Labels preferences (application domain).

features.name: Layer
features.summary: Base scripting class for every layer in a composition; carries the name, index in the stacking order, timing, parent, switches and the property tree shared by all layer kinds.

features.name: Layer panel
features.summary: Viewer that shows a single layer untransformed; required for paint, Roto Brush and motion-tracking work, with a Render option to show or hide masks and effects and a View menu for anchor point path and masks.

automation.notes: Opened through Open Layer. Text and shape layers and continuously rasterized layers cannot be shown in it. The Render checkbox has no known scripting member.

features.name: Layer Name / Source Name column
features.summary: Switches the Timeline panel name column between layer names and source footage names; layer names that match the source name are shown in square brackets.

automation.notes: Display toggle in the column heading; no scripting member or command id controls which name is shown (layer names themselves are scriptable through Layer.name).

features.name: Bevel And Emboss
features.summary: Combines highlights and shadows to give the contents depth, with separate blending modes for highlight and shadow. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Blending Options
features.summary: Property group added with the first layer style that holds Global Light Angle and Altitude (shared by styles with Use Global Light on) and the Advanced Blending controls.

automation.notes: Present only after a layer style has been added; adding then deleting a style leaves the group in place.

features.name: Color Overlay
features.summary: Fills the layer contents with a single color. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Drop Shadow
features.summary: Casts a shadow behind the layer contents, offset by distance and angle. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Fill Opacity
features.summary: Advanced Blending control that fades the layer contents without fading its layer styles, for example to leave only a drop shadow.

features.name: Gradient Overlay
features.summary: Fills the layer contents with a gradient that can be scaled, reversed and aligned with the layer. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Inner Glow
features.summary: Adds a glow radiating inward from the edges of the layer contents. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Inner Shadow
features.summary: Adds a shadow inside the edges of the layer contents so they look recessed. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Outer Glow
features.summary: Adds a glow radiating outward from the layer contents. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Satin
features.summary: Applies interior shading for a silky, satin-like finish. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Stroke
features.summary: Draws an outline around the layer contents. Applied as an editable, animatable Photoshop-style layer style that renders after transforms.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers. The id appears only in the Types-for-Adobe list (and a hyperbrew manual list). Applying a style has no object-model method; once applied its properties are set through the layer style property groups listed.

features.name: Lock switch
features.summary: Locks a layer so it cannot be selected or edited in the Composition or Timeline panels; a locked layer flashes when you try to change it.

automation.notes: Shortcut locks the selected layers. Hyperbrew name Lock (Switches submenu block).

features.name: Motion Blur switch
features.summary: Turns motion blur on for a layer; the blur appears only when the composition Enable Motion Blur switch is on (or the render settings enable it).

features.name: Move In point to composition start
features.summary: Slides selected layers so their In points sit at the beginning of the composition.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Move In point to current time
features.summary: Slides each selected layer in time so that its In point lands on the current time.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Move Out point to composition end
features.summary: Slides selected layers so their Out points sit at the end of the composition.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Move Out point to current time
features.summary: Slides each selected layer in time so that its Out point lands on the current time.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Move layer set so earliest In point is at current time
features.summary: Shifts all selected layers together so the earliest In point reaches the current time, preserving their offsets.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Move layer set so latest Out point is at current time
features.summary: Shifts all selected layers together so the latest Out point reaches the current time, preserving their offsets.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Adjustment Layer
features.summary: Adds an empty layer whose effects are applied to the composite of every layer beneath it in the stacking order; masks on it limit where the effects apply.

automation.notes: No dedicated creation method: a script adds a solid and turns on its adjustment flag.

features.name: Camera
features.summary: Adds a camera layer to the composition through the Camera Settings dialog; the camera then defines the view of the 3D layers.

automation.notes: Opens the Camera Settings dialog (modal). Camera options themselves are outside this domain. addCamera(name, centerPoint) creates the layer without the dialog; the menu command opens Camera Settings.

features.name: Maxon Cinema 4D File
features.summary: Creates a new Cinema 4D scene file, imports it and adds it as a layer so the scene can be edited in Cinema 4D and rendered through Cineware.

automation.notes: Opens a save dialog and then launches Cinema 4D. Command lists have 4007 (Types-for-Adobe NewMAXONCINEMA4DFile, grouped under File) and 4008 (hyperbrew Cinema4DFile); the Layer menu entry is not established.

features.name: Light
features.summary: Adds a light layer to the composition through the Light Settings dialog, illuminating and shadowing 3D layers.

automation.notes: Opens the Light Settings dialog (modal). Light options themselves are outside this domain.

features.name: Null Object
features.summary: Adds an invisible null layer that renders nothing but has full transform properties, typically used as a parent or as a controller carrying expression control effects.

automation.notes: Needs an active Timeline or Composition panel. The new null has its anchor point at its upper-left corner.

features.name: Adobe Photoshop File
features.summary: Creates a blank composition-sized PSD with safe-zone guides, launches Photoshop, imports the file and adds it as the top layer; saved edits in Photoshop update the layer.

automation.notes: Opens a save dialog and then launches Photoshop. Command lists have 3147 (Types-for-Adobe NewAdobePhotoshopFile, grouped under File) and 3148 (hyperbrew AdobePhotoshopFile); which one is the Layer menu entry is not established.

features.name: Shape Layer
features.summary: Creates an empty shape layer to which shapes and shape attributes can then be added.

features.name: Solid
features.summary: Creates a solid-color footage item and a layer that uses it in the active composition; the dialog sets name, size (Make Comp Size matches the composition), pixel aspect ratio and color.

automation.notes: Opens the Solid Settings dialog. Solids are filed in the Solids folder of the Project panel. File > Import > Solid creates only the footage item (footage domain).

features.name: Text
features.summary: Creates an empty text layer in the active composition and places an insertion point for typing; character and paragraph formatting belong to the text tools.

features.name: Move layers 1 frame earlier or later
features.summary: Shifts selected layers one frame earlier (Page Up) or later (Page Down) in time.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Move layers 10 frames earlier or later
features.summary: Shifts selected layers ten frames earlier or later in time.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Opacity
features.summary: Uniform transparency of a whole layer (intensity for lights); the keypad shortcuts with Ctrl+Alt step it by 1% or 10%.

automation.notes: Shortcut opens the Opacity dialog for selected layers (modal).

features.name: Open Composition
features.summary: For a precomposition layer, opens its source composition in the Composition panel.

automation.notes: Needs a selected precomposition layer. Also available from the layer context menu.

features.name: Open Layer
features.summary: Opens the selected layer in its own Layer panel, showing it before transforms; for a precomposition layer it opens the layer rather than the source composition.

automation.notes: Needs one selected layer. Double-clicking a layer does the same; synthetic layers (text, shape) cannot be opened in a Layer panel.

features.name: Open Layer Source
features.summary: Opens the footage item behind the selected layer in the Footage panel (Alt/Option-double-click the layer as a mouse alternative).

automation.notes: Needs a selected layer that has a source item.

features.name: Orient Along Path
features.summary: Auto-orientation option that turns the layer to face the direction of its motion path; added Rotation values offset the result.

features.name: Pan Behind (Anchor Point) tool
features.summary: Tool that moves a layer anchor point while compensating Position so the layer stays put (Alt/Option-drag changes only Anchor Point); it also pans a layer behind its mask and slip-edits in the Timeline. Double-clicking it resets the anchor point.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable; dragging with it is interactive.

features.name: Parent column
features.summary: Shows or hides the Parent & Link column, where parenting is set with a menu or pick whip.

automation.notes: Panel display toggle with no scripting member or command id.

features.name: Parent & Link
features.summary: Makes one layer the parent of another so the child transforms (not opacity) follow the parent; set it with the Parent column menu or by dragging the pick whip, and choose None to unparent.

automation.notes: A layer has one parent; parenting cannot be animated. Ctrl/Cmd-clicking the pick whip removes the parent.

features.name: Parent with jump
features.summary: Variant of parenting in which the child takes on the parent transform values and jumps to its position (Alt/Option while assigning or removing; Shift moves the child to the parent location).

features.name: Paste layers at current time
features.summary: Pastes copied layers so the In point of the copies sits at the current time instead of the original times.

automation.notes: There is no clipboard member: Layer.copyToComp copies a layer to the top of a composition (documented as the same as copy and paste), and shifting the copy's startTime by the current time minus its inPoint puts its In point at the current time.

features.name: Position
features.summary: Where the layer anchor point sits in composition space; edit it by dragging, with arrow keys (1 or 10 pixels), in the Timeline panel, or numerically in the Position dialog.

automation.notes: Shortcut opens the Position dialog for selected layers (modal). 2065 is the hyperbrew Position entry in the Layer menu block; the Layer > Transform path is not shown on the help page.

features.name: Preserve Underlying Transparency
features.summary: Layer option that shows the layer only where the composite of layers below it is opaque, similar to a clipping mask in Photoshop.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name PreserveTransparency.

features.name: Best
features.summary: Layer quality that renders with subpixel positioning, anti-aliasing and full effect calculation; slowest but most accurate.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Draft
features.summary: Layer quality that skips anti-aliasing and subpixel positioning and approximates some effects, for faster interactive work.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Wireframe
features.summary: Layer quality that draws only a box for the layer without its contents, the fastest display option.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Quick Offset
features.summary: Ctrl+Alt (Cmd+Option) drag in the Timeline panel that staggers the selected layers (or keyframes) evenly in time in selection order, with an overlay reporting total and per-layer offset.

automation.notes: The gesture is interactive; scripts produce the same staggering by setting startTime per layer.

features.name: Quick Set Anchor
features.summary: Pop-over (from the Anchor Point icon in the Properties panel or at the pointer) that snaps the anchor point of selected 2D layers to one of nine corner or edge-center positions.

automation.notes: Beta feature at the time of the help page; needs selected layers.

features.name: Remove All
features.summary: Strips all layer styles from the selected layers; to remove just one style, select it in the Timeline panel and delete it.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers.

features.name: Rename layer
features.summary: Renames the selected layer (or property group, mask or effect) in the Timeline panel by entering a new name in place or choosing Rename from the context menu.

automation.notes: Needs one selected item. The Windows key is Enter on the main keyboard.

features.name: Reorder layers by dragging
features.summary: Changes the stacking (and therefore render) order by dragging layer names up or down in the Timeline panel; cut and paste reorders layers in their selection order.

features.name: Replace layer source
features.summary: Swaps the source of the selected layers for the footage item selected in the Project panel while keeping their properties, effects and keyframes; Alt/Option-dragging an item onto a layer does the same.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers and a selected Project panel item.

features.name: Reset property
features.summary: Restores a property or a whole property group to default values, via the Reset control next to a group or Reset in a property context menu; on animated properties a keyframe with the default value is added.

automation.notes: Command lists contain several ids named Reset (2521, 2605); none is clearly this item.

features.name: Reveal Layer Source In Project
features.summary: Selects the footage item used by the chosen layer in the Project panel.

automation.notes: Needs a selected layer with a source item; hyperbrew name RevealLayerSourceinProject.

features.name: Rotation
features.summary: Rotation of a 2D layer around its anchor point, expressed as whole revolutions plus degrees; the numeric keypad + and - keys rotate selected layers by 1 degree (10 with Shift).

automation.notes: Shortcut opens the Rotation dialog for selected layers (modal).

features.name: Rotation tool
features.summary: Tool for rotating layers by dragging in the Composition panel (Shift for 15-degree steps); for 3D layers its Set menu chooses Orientation or Rotation, and double-clicking it resets Rotation.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable; rotating with it is interactive.

features.name: Bicubic sampling
features.summary: Best-quality sampling method using bicubic resampling, generally better for photographic images and upscaling but prone to ringing on sharp edges.

automation.notes: Applies to selected layers set to Best quality. Ray-traced textures and most effects still sample bilinearly.

features.name: Bilinear sampling
features.summary: Best-quality sampling method that resamples pixels bilinearly for scaling and other transforms; the default and safer for hard-edged graphics.

automation.notes: Applies to selected layers set to Best quality.

features.name: Scale
features.summary: Layer size as percentages around the anchor point, with Constrain Proportions; drag handles in the Composition panel (Shift keeps proportions), type values, or change units to pixels through Edit Value.

automation.notes: Numeric keypad shortcuts nudge Scale of selected layers by 1% or 10%. 2066 is the hyperbrew Scale entry (opens a dialog).

features.name: Select Children
features.summary: Adds all child layers of the selected parent layer to the selection.

automation.notes: No command id; scripts select children by matching Layer.parent.

features.name: Select layer by number
features.summary: Selects a layer by typing its stacking-order number on the numeric keypad (digits typed quickly form multi-digit numbers); with Shift the layer is toggled in the selection.

features.name: Select next layer
features.summary: Moves the layer selection one step down the stacking order.

features.name: Select previous layer
features.summary: Moves the layer selection one step up the stacking order.

features.name: Send Layer Backward
features.summary: Moves selected layers down one position in the stacking order.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name MoveDown (SendBackward before 2020).

features.name: Send Layer To Back
features.summary: Moves selected layers to the bottom of the stacking order.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name MoveToBottom (SendtoBack before 2020).

features.name: Set In or Out point numerically
features.summary: Enters In or Out times in the In and Out columns of the Timeline panel; Alt/Option-clicking a value moves that point to the current time.

features.name: Show All Video
features.summary: Turns the Video switch on for every layer in the composition.

features.name: Shy
features.summary: Marks a layer as shy so it disappears from the Timeline layer outline while Hide Shy Layers is on; shy layers still render.

features.name: Slip edit
features.summary: Changes which source frames play inside a trimmed layer by dragging its pale slip-edit bar (or dragging with the Pan Behind tool) while the In and Out points stay put; selected keyframes move with the footage.

automation.notes: Interactive drag; a script reproduces it by shifting startTime and restoring the In and Out points.

features.name: Solid Settings
features.summary: Edits the name, size and color of the selected solid layer or solid footage item; Affect All Layers That Use This Solid updates every layer sharing the item instead of making a new one. The same dialog serves null and adjustment layers.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; needs a selected solid, null or adjustment layer. 2021 is listed as LayerSettings; the item is labelled for the selected layer type. Scripts change a solid color through the footage source; size is not settable on SolidSource.

features.name: Solo switch
features.summary: Limits previews and renders to the soloed layers of the same kind; other video layers are hidden while lights and audio stay active. Alt/Option-clicking a solo switch solos that layer alone.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name Solo.

features.name: Split Layer
features.summary: Cuts the selected layers (or all layers when none are selected) at the current time into two independent layers that keep all keyframes; a preference decides whether the new part goes above or below.

automation.notes: The two command lists name 2158 differently: Types-for-Adobe SplitLayer (Edit), hyperbrew DuplicatePreserveFile; the Types-for-Adobe name matches this item.

features.name: Switches and Modes columns
features.summary: Shows or hides the Layer Switches and Transfer Controls (Modes) columns in the Timeline panel, also available from the buttons at the lower left of the panel.

automation.notes: Panel display toggle with no scripting member or command id.

features.name: Track Matte
features.summary: Picks any layer in the composition as the matte for the selected layer from the Track Matte menu in the Modes column or with its pick whip; several layers can share one matte, and the matte layer video is switched off automatically.

automation.notes: Since 23.0 the matte no longer has to sit directly above the layer. Animating the matte layer makes a traveling matte.

features.name: Alpha Inverted Matte
features.summary: Makes the layer opaque where the matte alpha channel is fully transparent. Chosen with the Alpha/Luma and inverted toggles next to the Track Matte menu.

automation.notes: Needs a layer with a track matte. 2193 is the older Track Matte submenu entry; 4230 is the hyperbrew SetType entry added in 2024.

features.name: Alpha Matte
features.summary: Makes the layer opaque where the matte alpha channel is fully opaque. Chosen with the Alpha/Luma and inverted toggles next to the Track Matte menu.

automation.notes: Needs a layer with a track matte. 2192 is the older Track Matte submenu entry; 4229 is the hyperbrew SetType entry added in 2024.

features.name: Luma Inverted Matte
features.summary: Makes the layer opaque where matte pixels have zero luminance. Chosen with the Alpha/Luma and inverted toggles next to the Track Matte menu.

automation.notes: Needs a layer with a track matte. 2195 is the older Track Matte submenu entry; 4232 is the hyperbrew SetType entry added in 2024.

features.name: Luma Matte
features.summary: Makes the layer opaque where matte pixels are at full luminance, useful for mattes without an alpha channel. Chosen with the Alpha/Luma and inverted toggles next to the Track Matte menu.

automation.notes: Needs a layer with a track matte. 2194 is the older Track Matte submenu entry; 4231 is the hyperbrew SetType entry added in 2024.

features.name: No Track Matte
features.summary: Removes the track matte from the selected layer so it no longer takes transparency from another layer.

automation.notes: removeTrackMatte keeps the stored matte type; the legacy trackMatteType property set to NO_TRACK_MATTE also clears it.

features.name: Transform properties
features.summary: Property group every layer has (Anchor Point, Position, Scale, Rotation, Opacity, plus Orientation for 3D layers), all animatable from the Timeline panel.

features.name: Trim or extend a layer
features.summary: Changes the In or Out point of a layer by dragging the ends of its duration bar; stills, shapes, text, cameras, lights and time-remapped layers can be extended indefinitely.

automation.notes: Trimming never alters the source footage.

features.name: Trim In point to current time
features.summary: Sets the In point of each selected layer to the current time, trimming or extending it.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Trim Out point to current time
features.summary: Sets the Out point of each selected layer to the current time, trimming or extending it.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Trim layer set to earliest In point at current time
features.summary: Trims or extends the selected layers as a group so the earliest In point is at the current time while keeping their relative offsets.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Trim layer set to latest Out point at current time
features.summary: Trims or extends the selected layers as a group so the latest Out point is at the current time while keeping their relative offsets.

automation.notes: Acts on the selected layers.

features.name: Unlock All Layers
features.summary: Clears the Lock switch on every layer in the active composition.

features.name: Use Blend Ranges From Source
features.summary: Applies the advanced blend-if ranges stored in the source Photoshop file when compositing the layer.

features.name: Video switch
features.summary: Eyeball switch that turns rendering of a layer on or off; on an adjustment layer it toggles the effects, on a camera or light it turns the layer on or off. Shy layers are still rendered, so this switch is the way to exclude a layer.

automation.notes: Shortcut acts on the selected layers.

domains.name: Keyframes and animation
domains.covers: Keyframes, interpolation, the Graph Editor, motion paths, easing, wiggle and smoothing, and Animation menu commands.

features.name: Add keyframe on a motion path with the Pen tool
features.summary: Clicking a motion path with the Pen or Add Vertex tool inserts a new spatial keyframe at that frame; clicking a graph segment with the Pen tool does the same in the Graph Editor.

automation.notes: The click itself is interactive; a key at a given time can be added by script.

features.name: Add [x] Keyframe
features.summary: Animation menu command, named after the selected property, that sets a keyframe at the current time without changing the value ([x] stands for the property name). The keyboard equivalent is Alt+Shift (Option on macOS) plus the property's reveal shortcut, for example P for Position or M for Mask Path.

automation.notes: Needs a selected property. Id 2518 is hyperbrew AddKeyframe; the mapping to this menu item is by name only.

features.name: Allow Keyframes Between Frames
features.summary: Graph Editor option that lets keyframes be dragged to sub-frame times for fine timing.

automation.notes: Graph Editor option that only affects dragging keys interactively; no member or command id. Scripts already place keys at any time with Property.setValueAtTime.

features.name: Auto-Select Graph Type
features.summary: Graph type option that uses speed graphs for spatial properties and value graphs for everything else.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Auto Zoom Height
features.summary: Graph Editor toggle that keeps the vertical scale fitted to the panel height, leaving horizontal zoom manual and disabling vertical pan and zoom.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Bezier direction handles (Graph Editor)
features.summary: Dragging, extending or splitting (Alt/Option-drag) the direction handles of Bezier keyframes reshapes the value or speed curve on each side of a key.

automation.notes: Dragging is interactive; the resulting speed and influence can be set numerically.

features.name: Change multiple keyframe values at once
features.summary: With several keyframes of one property selected, typing a value sets them all to it, while scrubbing or dragging in a viewer offsets them all by the same amount.

features.name: Copy and paste keyframes
features.summary: Edit > Copy and Edit > Paste move keyframe selections, including ones spanning several layers, to the current time on matching or compatible properties without creating new layers.

automation.notes: Select the source keys with Property.setSelectedAtKey, set the destination time with CompItem.time and select the destination layer or property (PropertyBase.selected), then run Edit > Copy (19) and Edit > Paste (20). Needs selected keyframes and a destination. Scripts can instead rebuild the keys with Property.setValuesAtTimes.

features.name: Create Keyframes from Data
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that bakes the data streams of a data (MGJSON) layer into ordinary keyframes, after which they no longer follow the data file.

automation.notes: Needs a selected data footage layer. Id 4036 is hyperbrew CreateDataFootageLayerKeyframes.

features.name: Create Nulls From Paths.jsx
features.summary: Bundled ScriptUI panel with Points Follow Nulls, Nulls Follow Points and Trace Path buttons that build expression-linked nulls for the selected Bezier mask or shape path.

automation.notes: Bundled ScriptUI panel whose Points Follow Nulls, Nulls Follow Points and Trace Path buttons must be clicked; its Window menu item takes an install-specific id. Needs a selected path property; parametric shapes must first be converted to Bezier paths.

features.name: Data-driven animation
features.summary: Imported JSON, MGJSON, CSV or TSV data drives layer properties through expressions or the Property Link pick whip; MGJSON streams can vary over time while the others hold static values.

automation.notes: Import the data file with Project.importFile and link properties by setting Property.expression to an expression that reads the footage's sourceData or dataValue (see the expressions records). Create Keyframes from Data (4036) and Align Video to Data (4041) are menu commands that need a selected data layer.

features.name: Data property group
features.summary: Top-level group that a data footage layer shows in place of Transform, holding the file's hierarchy as properties expression-linked to the source file.

automation.notes: Values are read through the generic property tree; they update when the data file changes.

features.name: Default Position Properties to Separated Dimensions
features.summary: Composition preference that creates Position as separate X, Y and Z properties by default.

features.name: Default Spatial Interpolation to Linear
features.summary: Composition preference that makes new spatial keyframes Linear instead of Auto Bezier; existing keys and properties that already have keys are unaffected.

features.name: Delete keyframes
features.summary: Removes selected keyframes with the Delete key, or a single key in the Graph Editor by Ctrl/Command-clicking it with the Selection tool.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes.

features.name: Deselect all keyframes, properties, and property groups
features.summary: Keyboard command that clears the selection of keyframes, properties and property groups while leaving layers selected.

features.name: Easy Ease
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that sets speed 0 with 33.33% influence on both sides of the selected keyframes so motion slows into and out of them; also a Graph Editor button.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes.

features.name: Easy Ease In
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that eases only the incoming side of the selected keyframes.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes.

features.name: Easy Ease Out
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that eases only the outgoing side of the selected keyframes.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes.

features.name: Edit Value
features.summary: Keyframe context-menu item that shows the keyframe value and opens a dialog for typing a new one.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog; needs a selected keyframe. Two command ids are named EditValue in hyperbrew, so none is cited.

features.name: Edit Speed Graph
features.summary: Graph type option that plots the rate of change, where dragging keyframes and direction handles adjusts incoming and outgoing speed and influence.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Edit Value Graph
features.summary: Graph type option that shows every property as a value-over-time curve.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Enable Auto-keyframe
features.summary: Timeline panel menu mode in which changing any interpolatable property switches on its stopwatch and records a keyframe at the current time; off by default and ignored for menus, checkboxes and Source Text.

automation.notes: Id 4015 is hyperbrew EnableAutoStopwatch; matched to this toggle by name and behaviour, not confirmed by a second list.

features.name: Expand or contract a group of keyframes
features.summary: Alt/Option-dragging the first or last of three or more selected keyframes scales their timing proportionally in layer bar mode.

automation.notes: Interactive drag only; no member and no command id.

features.name: Exponential Scale
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that replaces linear Scale change between two selected keys with exponential change, mimicking an optical zoom; intermediate keys are replaced.

automation.notes: Needs a selected start and end Scale keyframe.

features.name: Fit All
features.summary: Graph Editor button that rescales time and value so every displayed curve fits the graph.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Fit Selection
features.summary: Graph Editor button that rescales time and value so the selected keyframes fill the graph.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Graph Editor
features.summary: Timeline panel mode that replaces layer bars with value or speed curves for the shown properties so keyframes and interpolation can be edited graphically.

automation.notes: Timeline view toggle; no command id in either list and no member.

features.name: Snap (Graph Editor)
features.summary: When on, dragged keyframes snap to other keyframe values and times, the current time, layer In/Out points, markers, work area and composition bounds; Ctrl/Command toggles it mid-drag.

automation.notes: Interactive drag behaviour; no member and no command id.

features.name: Convert selected keyframes to Hold, Linear or Auto Bezier
features.summary: Buttons at the bottom of the Graph Editor that switch the interpolation of selected keyframes to Hold, Linear or Auto Bezier in one click.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes.

features.name: Show Audio Waveforms
features.summary: Graph Editor option that overlays the audio waveform of layers with a property in the graph.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Show Layer In/Out Points
features.summary: Graph Editor option that marks layer In and Out points with brace symbols.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Show Layer Markers
features.summary: Graph Editor option that draws layer markers as small triangles for layers that have a property in the graph.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Show Graph Tool Tips
features.summary: Turns the hover readouts of layer, property, time and value in the Graph Editor on or off.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Auto Bezier interpolation
features.summary: Bezier variant whose handles are recalculated automatically to keep a smooth transition; it is the default for spatial properties and becomes Continuous Bezier once a handle is dragged.

features.name: Bezier interpolation
features.summary: Interpolation method with two independent direction handles per key, allowing any mix of curves and sharp corners on graphs and motion paths.

features.name: Continuous Bezier interpolation
features.summary: Bezier variant whose two handles stay aligned so change passes smoothly through the key while the handle positions remain manually set.

features.name: Hold interpolation
features.summary: Temporal-only method that keeps a value unchanged until the next key, then jumps; useful for strobe effects and sudden appearances.

features.name: Linear interpolation
features.summary: Interpolation method giving a constant rate of change between two keys, producing straight segments and abrupt speed changes at each keyframe.

automation.notes: Ctrl/Command-clicking a Bezier-family key in layer bar mode also switches it to Linear.

features.name: Go to previous or next keyframe of selected layers
features.summary: Holding Shift with the J or K navigation keys limits the current-time indicator jump to keyframes and markers of the selected layers and properties.

automation.notes: Shift+K moves forward. Equivalent by reading key times of selected properties and setting the composition time.

features.name: Keyframe color labels
features.summary: Assigns one of the shared label colours to selected keyframes so groups of keys can be told apart and selected together; label colours themselves are edited in the Labels preferences.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes when done from the menu.

features.name: Copy keyframe data as tab-delimited text
features.summary: Copied keyframes from one layer can be pasted into a spreadsheet or text editor as tab-delimited rows, edited, and pasted back into After Effects.

automation.notes: Edit > Copy (19) with keyframes selected puts the tab-delimited text on the system clipboard, and Edit > Paste (20) applies such text to the selected layer. ExtendScript has no clipboard member, so the text has to be read from or placed on the clipboard outside After Effects; Property.keyTime and keyValue give the same values directly.

features.name: KeyframeEase
features.summary: Scripting object holding one dimension of a keyframe's temporal ease as a speed and an influence percentage, used when reading or writing incoming and outgoing velocity.

features.name: Use Keyframe Icons / Use Keyframe Indices
features.summary: Timeline panel menu choice that draws keyframes either as interpolation-shaped icons or as sequential numbers in layer bar mode.

automation.notes: Timeline display preference; no member and no command id.

features.name: Keyframe Interpolation
features.summary: Dialog that sets temporal interpolation, spatial interpolation and the roving behaviour of the selected keyframes, each with a Current Settings choice that leaves values unchanged.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog; needs selected keyframes.

features.name: KeyframeInterpolationType
features.summary: Enumeration of the keyframe interpolation kinds the object model accepts for incoming and outgoing interpolation: Linear, Bezier and Hold.

features.name: Keyframe navigator
features.summary: Arrows and a diamond box in the A/V Features column that jump the current-time indicator to the previous or next keyframe of a property and add or remove a keyframe at the current time.

automation.notes: Navigation is reproduced by reading key times and setting the composition time.

features.name: Keyframe Velocity
features.summary: Dialog for typing incoming and outgoing speed and influence of the selected keyframe, with a Continuous option that locks incoming and outgoing velocity together.

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog; needs selected keyframes. Units vary by property.

features.name: Keys column
features.summary: Optional Timeline column that moves the keyframe navigator arrows out of the A/V Features column into a column of their own.

automation.notes: Timeline display layout only; no object-model member and no command id in either list.

features.name: On All Layers
features.summary: Label-group selection scope that picks same-colour keyframes on every layer of the composition.

automation.notes: Needs a selected keyframe.

features.name: On Selected Layers
features.summary: Label-group selection scope that picks same-colour keyframes on the selected layers only.

automation.notes: Needs a selected keyframe.

features.name: Visible Keyframes on All Layers
features.summary: Label-group selection scope limited to keyframes on twirled-open properties across all layers.

automation.notes: Needs a selected keyframe.

features.name: Visible Keyframes on Selected Layers
features.summary: Label-group selection scope limited to keyframes on twirled-open properties of the selected layers.

automation.notes: Needs a selected keyframe.

features.name: Motion paths
features.summary: Spatial properties such as Position, Anchor Point and effect points show their animation as a dotted path whose boxes are keyframes; keys and handles can be dragged in the Composition or Layer panel, and dot spacing shows speed.

automation.notes: Dragging is interactive; the same key values and spatial tangents can be set by script. Display requires Motion Paths in View Options.

features.name: Motion Sketch
features.summary: Panel that records Position keyframes for the selected layer as you drag in the Composition panel, with Capture Speed At, Smoothing, Show Wireframe and Show Background options and a Start Capture button.

automation.notes: Opens the panel from the Window menu. Its menu ids are install-specific (5017, 5053 in the published lists), so look up by name with app.findMenuCommandId("Motion Sketch"). Capture itself is interactive (dragging in the Composition panel) and limited to the work area.

features.name: Move keyframes in time
features.summary: Drags selected keyframes to a new time while keeping their spacing, or nudges them one frame (ten with Shift) with Alt/Option plus the arrow keys; Shift-dragging snaps to the current-time indicator.

automation.notes: No member retimes an existing key: a script reads the key (time, value, interpolation, ease), removes it with removeKey, re-creates it at the new time with setValueAtTime and restores interpolation and ease (and spatial tangents, roving and labels where used). The Alt/Option+arrow nudges have no command id.

features.name: Null Controllers for Path Points
features.summary: Creates one null per vertex of the selected shape or mask path, each driving its vertex through expressions.

automation.notes: Needs a selected Path or Mask Path property. No command id in either list.

features.name: Null Controllers for Positional Points
features.summary: Creates a matching-dimension null, named and coloured after its target, that drives the selected layer's Position (or a selected Anchor Point, effect point, shape point or Puppet pin) through expressions and a Layer Control.

automation.notes: Also under Layer > Create and the property context menu. Needs a selected layer or positional property; requires the JavaScript expression engine and unique layer names. No command id in either list.

features.name: Null Tracing Along Path
features.summary: Creates a single null that travels along the selected path and orients to it, with a controller effect for progress and looping.

automation.notes: Needs a selected Path or Mask Path property. No command id in either list.

features.name: Nulls Following Path Points
features.summary: Creates one null per vertex of the selected path that follows its vertex, so other layers can be parented to an animated path.

automation.notes: Needs a selected Path or Mask Path property. No command id in either list.

features.name: Create a motion path from a mask, shape, or paint path
features.summary: Pasting a copied mask, shape, paint or Illustrator/Photoshop path into Position or Anchor Point creates a two-second motion path whose middle keys rove for constant speed.

automation.notes: Select the Mask Path or shape Path property (PropertyBase.selected) and run Edit > Copy (19), then select Position or Anchor Point and run Edit > Paste (20). Needs a selected destination property.

features.name: 3D model options (Properties panel)
features.summary: For 3D model layers, the panel offers Compositing Options (Casts Shadows, Accepts Shadows, Accept Lights, Shadow Color) and Animation Options for choosing embedded animations.

automation.notes: Casts Shadows, Accepts Shadows and Accepts Lights are the layer's Material Options properties. Shadow Color and the choice of embedded animation have no member in the 26.0 object model.

features.name: Auto-Open Panel
features.summary: Toolbar option for the Type, Shape and Pen tools that opens the Properties panel when the tool is chosen.

features.name: Camera Options (Properties panel)
features.summary: For camera layers, the panel shows Point of Interest, Position, Orientation and X/Y/Z Rotation plus Camera Options and Camera Settings.

features.name: Essential Properties (Properties panel)
features.summary: Shows a precomp layer's Essential Properties, including font controls not available in the Timeline view of those properties.

automation.notes: The values shown are the precomp layer's Essential Properties group (match name "ADBE Layer Overrides"), which scripts read and set like other properties. The panel display itself is not scriptable.

features.name: Layer Transform (Properties panel)
features.summary: Section shown for every layer type with Anchor Point, Position, Scale, Rotation and Opacity controls and stopwatches.

features.name: Light Options (Properties panel)
