features.summary: For light layers, the panel shows Layer Transform and a Light Options section for light type and behaviour.

features.name: Properties
features.summary: Contextual panel that shows the key properties of the selected layers, such as transforms, text, shape, camera, light and Essential Properties, so they can be edited and keyframed without twirling open the Timeline.

automation.notes: Opens the panel from the Window menu. Its menu ids are install-specific (5004 in the published lists), so look up by name with app.findMenuCommandId("Properties"). The panel shows properties of the selected layers; the properties themselves are set through the object model.

features.name: Shape Properties and Shape Transform (Properties panel)
features.summary: Sections shown for shape layers that expose shape attributes and per-shape transform controls.

features.name: Property (keyframe API)
features.summary: Scripting object for a single animatable layer or effect property; it exposes the keyframe list, per-key values, times, interpolation, eases, roving and labels.

features.name: Proportional Scrubbing
features.summary: Ctrl+Alt (Command+Option) while scrubbing a property value spreads the change over selected layers in selection order: the first gets none, the last gets all, the rest an even share.

automation.notes: Interactive scrub gesture; no member and no command id. For Scale, the last layer's Constrain Proportions setting applies.

features.name: Puppet Advanced Pin Tool
features.summary: Advanced-engine tool whose pins carry position, scale and rotation, adjusted with an outer ring and square handle (Shift constrains to 15 degrees or 5%).

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; placing and dragging pins is interactive and no documented member creates pins or meshes. The enum value is listed in Types-for-Adobe, not the scripting guide. Limit: a script can choose the Puppet Advanced Pin tool (Project.toolType, done by manage_puppet) but cannot place, move or delete pins or create a mesh; no documented object-model member does, so pins are placed by hand in the Composition panel. Once pins exist, their Position properties can be keyframed by path (manage_puppet list, then set_keyframes).

features.name: Puppet Bend Pin Tool
features.summary: Advanced-engine tool whose pins take their position from surrounding pins while you control their scale and rotation, for effects like breathing or a wagging tail.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; placing and dragging pins is interactive and no documented member creates pins or meshes. The enum value is listed in Types-for-Adobe, not the scripting guide. Limit: a script can choose the Puppet Bend Pin tool (Project.toolType, done by manage_puppet) but cannot place, move or delete pins or create a mesh; no documented object-model member does, so pins are placed by hand in the Composition panel. Once pins exist, their Position properties can be keyframed by path (manage_puppet list, then set_keyframes).

features.name: Duplicate Puppet mesh
features.summary: Duplicating a Mesh group (or clicking inside the original outline) makes another mesh with its own copy of the pixels for separate deformation.

automation.notes: Needs the Mesh group selected in the Timeline panel. Limit: duplicating needs an existing mesh, which only placing a pin with a Puppet tool creates. manage_puppet duplicates it with PropertyBase.duplicate() on the mesh found by match name (ADBE FreePin3 Mesh Group); the match names of the Puppet groups are not documented in the scripting guide and wait for validation in After Effects.

features.name: Puppet effect
features.summary: Effect added by the Puppet tools (not from the Effect menu) that holds meshes and pins; its match name is ADBE FreePin3.

automation.notes: Adding the effect by match name gives an empty instance; meshes and pins come from the interactive tools.

features.name: Puppet Engine
features.summary: Per-effect choice between the Advanced puppet engine (default since 15.1) and the Legacy engine, which treat pins and starch differently.

automation.notes: Exposed as a property in the Timeline panel; no match name for it is documented in the scripting guide, so a script route is not confirmed.

features.name: Triangles / Density
features.summary: Mesh resolution control: Triangles sets a target triangle count in the Legacy engine, and Density sets triangle size and count in the Advanced engine.

automation.notes: Shown in the Tools panel options and in the Mesh group in the Timeline panel; property match names are not documented.

features.name: Expansion
features.summary: Mesh option that grows the mesh beyond its outline, for example to include a stroke (default 3 pixels).

automation.notes: Shown in the Tools panel options and in the Mesh group; property match names are not documented.

features.name: Mesh Rotation Refinement
features.summary: Advanced-engine property limiting how far Position and Starch pins rotate to reduce distortion; higher values give looser, more flexible bending.

automation.notes: Property match name "ADBE FreePin3 Auto Rotate Pins" (display name Mesh Rotation Refinement) directly inside the Puppet effect ("ADBE FreePin3"), as recorded in a published ExtendScript dump of the effect's properties, where it accepts expressions. Advanced engine only.

features.name: In Front and Extent (Overlap pin)
features.summary: Overlap pin properties: In Front sets apparent closeness (cumulative, default 50, best keyed with Hold) and Extent sets how far its influence reaches.

automation.notes: Timeline properties of each pin; match names not documented.

features.name: Puppet Overlap Pin Tool
features.summary: Tool that places Overlap pins on the original outline to decide which parts of a deformed image appear in front.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; placing and dragging pins is interactive and no documented member creates pins or meshes. Limit: a script can choose the Puppet Overlap Pin tool (Project.toolType, done by manage_puppet) but cannot place, move or delete pins or create a mesh; no documented object-model member does, so pins are placed by hand in the Composition panel. Once pins exist, their Position properties can be keyframed by path (manage_puppet list, then set_keyframes).

features.name: Pin Type
features.summary: Advanced-engine property that switches an existing pin between Position and Starch.

automation.notes: Timeline property of each pin; match name not documented.

features.name: Puppet Position Pin Tool
features.summary: Tool that applies the Puppet effect on first click, builds a deformation mesh from the clicked outline and places Position (Deform) pins whose movement is keyframed automatically.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; placing and dragging pins is interactive and no documented member creates pins or meshes. The shortcut cycles through the Puppet tools. Limit: a script can choose the Puppet Position Pin tool (Project.toolType, done by manage_puppet) but cannot place, move or delete pins or create a mesh; no documented object-model member does, so pins are placed by hand in the Composition panel. Once pins exist, their Position properties can be keyframed by path (manage_puppet list, then set_keyframes).

features.name: Puppet Record Options
features.summary: Tools-panel dialog that sets Speed, Smoothing and Use Draft Deformation for sketching pin motion.

automation.notes: Modal dialog opened from the Tools panel options; its settings only affect interactive pin sketching. No member or command id.

features.name: Reset (Puppet effect)
features.summary: Reset on the Puppet effect returns Deform pins to their original places at the current time; a second Reset removes all pins and meshes.

automation.notes: Effect reset button; hyperbrew id 2521 is named Reset but its menu is unclear, so it is not cited.

features.name: Show (mesh)
features.summary: Tools panel option that displays the triangle mesh of the Puppet effect.

automation.notes: Viewer display toggle; no member and no command id.

features.name: Puppet Sketch tool
features.summary: Holding Ctrl/Command with a Puppet tool turns it into a recorder: dragging selected pins records their motion in real time, then the current-time indicator returns to the start.

automation.notes: Temporary tool reached only by a modifier key during an interactive drag; it has no ToolType value or command id.

features.name: Amount and Extent (Starch pin)
features.summary: Starch pin properties: Amount sets stiffening strength (cumulative, negative cancels) and, in the Legacy engine, Extent sets its reach.

automation.notes: Timeline properties of each pin; match names not documented.

features.name: Puppet Starch Pin Tool
features.summary: Tool that places Starch pins to stiffen parts of the mesh so they distort less.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; placing and dragging pins is interactive and no documented member creates pins or meshes. Limit: a script can choose the Puppet Starch Pin tool (Project.toolType, done by manage_puppet) but cannot place, move or delete pins or create a mesh; no documented object-model member does, so pins are placed by hand in the Composition panel. Once pins exist, their Position properties can be keyframed by path (manage_puppet list, then set_keyframes).

features.name: Quick Apply result categories
features.summary: Settings in Quick Apply that choose which result types appear (Effects, Menu Commands, Animation Presets); typing e:, p: or m: first narrows a single search the same way.

automation.notes: Setting inside the interactive Quick Apply search dialog; no member or command id. Scripts apply effects with PropertyGroup.addProperty and presets with Layer.applyPreset directly.

features.name: Quick Apply to new layer or adjustment layer
features.summary: Holding Ctrl/Command while confirming a Quick Apply effect or preset creates a new solid or layer to hold it, and adding Alt/Option creates a new adjustment layer instead.

automation.notes: Modifier keys used while confirming a result in the interactive Quick Apply dialog; no member or command id. A script creates the solid or adjustment layer itself and applies the effect or preset to it.

features.name: Show dialog at cursor location
features.summary: Quick Apply option that opens the dialog next to the pointer instead of where it was last used.

features.name: Reveal Animating Properties
features.summary: Shows only the properties that have keyframes or expressions on the selected layers.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers (or all layers). The help page name differs from the command lists, which call 4011 RevealPropertiesWithAnimation and list a separate 2387 RevealPropertiesWithKeyframes not named in the help pages.

features.name: Reveal in Timeline
features.summary: Context-menu command (or double-click) in the Properties panel that twirls open and shows the chosen property in the Timeline panel.

automation.notes: Id 2536 is hyperbrew RevealinTimeline; the same command also appears in the Essential Graphics panel.

features.name: Reveal Modified Properties
features.summary: Shows only the properties changed from their default values on the selected layers.

automation.notes: The command lists name it RevealAllModifiedProperties.

features.name: Reverse paste keyframes
features.summary: Pastes copied keyframes at the current time in reversed time order, useful for loops, bounces and rewinds.

automation.notes: Needs keyframes on the clipboard and a selected destination.

features.name: Rove Across Time
features.summary: Lets intermediate spatial keyframes float in time so speed stays even across a range; Lock To Time pins them back. Not available on the first or last key.

automation.notes: Spatial properties only; needs selected keyframes. Also set from the Roving menu of the Keyframe Interpolation dialog.

features.name: RPF Camera Import
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that reads camera data stored in an RLA or RPF sequence on the selected layer and creates keyframed camera layers from it.

automation.notes: Needs a selected RLA/RPF sequence layer. The Types-for-Adobe id is in the 5000 plug-in range and is not cited.

features.name: Select all visible keyframes and properties
features.summary: Keyboard command that selects every keyframe and property currently shown in the Timeline panel.

features.name: Select Equal Keyframes
features.summary: Keyframe context-menu command that selects every keyframe of the property holding the same value as the clicked keyframe.

automation.notes: Needs a selected keyframe.

features.name: Select Following Keyframes
features.summary: Keyframe context-menu command that selects all keyframes after the selected one on the same property.

automation.notes: Available only when exactly one keyframe is selected.

features.name: Select Keyframe Label Group
features.summary: Submenu that selects keyframes sharing the label colour of the selected keyframe, with scope options for selected or all layers and for visible keyframes only.

automation.notes: Needs a selected keyframe; also in the keyframe context menu.

features.name: Select keyframes
features.summary: Keyframes are selected by clicking, Shift-clicking or marquee-dragging, and all keyframes of a property are selected by clicking the property name or Alt/Option-clicking a graph segment.

features.name: Select Previous Keyframes
features.summary: Keyframe context-menu command that selects all keyframes before the selected one on the same property.

automation.notes: Available only when exactly one keyframe is selected.

features.name: Separate Dimensions
features.summary: Splits a Position property into separate X, Y and (for 3D layers) Z Position properties that animate independently, or recombines them; also a button in the Graph Editor and the Position context menu.

automation.notes: Needs a selected Position property. Recombining may lose some speed and path detail.

features.name: Sequence Layers
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that places selected layers one after another in selection order, optionally overlapping them by a duration with a Dissolve Front Layer or Cross Dissolve Front And Back Layers transition (a negative duration leaves gaps).

automation.notes: Opens a modal dialog; needs two or more selected layers shorter than the composition. The Types-for-Adobe id for it is in the 5000 plug-in range and is not cited.

features.name: Show Animated Properties
features.summary: Show Properties choice that displays every animated property of the selected layers.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Show Graph Editor Set
features.summary: Show Properties choice that displays only properties whose Graph Editor switch (next to the stopwatch) is on.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Show Reference Graph
features.summary: Draws the graph type not being edited in the background for reference, with its values listed at the right edge.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Show Selected Properties
features.summary: Show Properties choice that limits the Graph Editor to the properties selected in the layer outline.

automation.notes: Display-only option of the Graph Editor; neither command list has an id for it and no object-model member controls it.

features.name: Show Transform Box
features.summary: Graph Editor option that draws a free-transform box around multiple selected keyframes so they can be moved, scaled (negative scale reverses them), tapered or skewed in time and value.

automation.notes: Interactive bounding-box editing; no member and no command id.

features.name: Smoother
features.summary: Panel that thins and smooths selected keyframes of a spatial path or temporal graph within a Tolerance, applying Bezier interpolation; most useful after Motion Sketch.

automation.notes: Opens the panel from the Window menu. Its menu ids are install-specific (5020, 5059 in the published lists), so look up by name with app.findMenuCommandId("Smoother"). Smoothing needs at least three selected keyframes and the panel's Apply button, which scripts cannot press.

features.name: Time-Vary Stopwatch
features.summary: The stopwatch beside a property name turns keyframing on for that property and sets a keyframe at the current time; turning it off discards every keyframe and keeps the value at the current time.

automation.notes: Enabling is equivalent to creating the first key; disabling is equivalent to removing all keys (Property.isTimeVarying reports the state but is read-only).

features.name: Time-Reverse Keyframes
features.summary: Keyframe assistant that flips the order of the selected keyframes within each property's original time span without reversing layer playback; markers stay put.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes.

features.name: Toggle Hold Keyframe
features.summary: Switches Hold on or off as the outgoing interpolation of the selected keyframes.

automation.notes: Needs selected keyframes. The shortcut table describes the key as toggling between Hold and Auto Bezier.

features.name: Wiggler
features.summary: Panel that adds random deviations to a selected keyframe range, with Apply To (spatial path or temporal graph), Noise Type (smooth or jagged), dimension choices, Frequency and Magnitude.

automation.notes: Opens the panel from the Window menu. Its menu ids are install-specific (5022, 5061 in the published lists), so look up by name with app.findMenuCommandId("Wiggler"). Applying needs at least two selected keyframes and the panel's Apply button, which scripts cannot press; the wiggle expression (Property.expression) is a scriptable alternative.

domains.name: Expressions
domains.covers: Expressions and the expression language, the expression controls effects, and the expression editor.

features.name: Add Expression
features.summary: Attaches a default expression to the selected property and opens its expression field in the Timeline panel; Alt-clicking (Option-clicking on macOS) the property stopwatch does the same.

automation.notes: Needs a selected property that can take an expression. Setting Property.expression to a string adds the expression from a script.

features.name: Convert Expression to Keyframes
features.summary: Evaluates the expression on the selected property at every frame, writes the results as keyframes and switches the expression off while keeping its text.

automation.notes: Needs a selected property that has an expression.

features.name: Copy Expression Only
features.summary: Copies only the expression of the selected property, without its keyframes, so it can be pasted onto other properties or layers.

automation.notes: Needs a selected property with an expression. Reading Property.expression on one property and writing it to another does the same from a script.

features.name: Copy With Property Links
features.summary: Copies the selected properties or layers so that pasting them creates expressions linking each pasted property back to the original, using a comp() reference that works across compositions.

automation.notes: Needs selected properties or layers. The two command lists name id 10310 differently: hyperbrew records it only as Copy, Types-for-Adobe as CopyWithPropertyLinks.

features.name: Copy With Relative Property Links
features.summary: Like Copy With Property Links, but the generated links use thisComp so they resolve inside whichever composition the properties are pasted into.

automation.notes: Needs selected properties or layers. No command id found in either list.

features.name: Enable Expression
features.summary: Per-property switch (the equals-sign button under the property) that turns an expression off without deleting it; a disabled expression shows a slash through the switch.

automation.notes: Property.expressionEnabled toggles one property. The hyperbrew list also has EnableExpressions (10450) and DisableExpressions (10451); the help pages document only the switch, so where those two commands sit in the menus is not confirmed.

features.name: Expression auto-complete
features.summary: As you type, the expression editor suggests methods plus composition, layer, footage and effect names from the project in the right comp(), layer(), footage() or effect() context.

automation.notes: Turned on or off by the Auto Complete option in the Scripting & Expressions preferences.

features.name: Expression editor
features.summary: The resizable code field under a property in the Timeline panel (or at the bottom of the Graph Editor) where expressions are typed, with syntax colouring, auto-complete and inline error display.

automation.notes: The field itself is interactive; its content is the Property.expression string. Press Enter on the numeric keypad or click outside to commit.

features.name: Expressions Engine
features.summary: Project Settings option on the Expressions tab that chooses whether expressions in the project are evaluated by the JavaScript engine or the Legacy ExtendScript engine.

automation.notes: Set in the modal Project Settings dialog. Project.expressionEngine accepts "javascript-1.0" or "extendscript". Older projects open with Legacy ExtendScript.

features.name: Expression errors
features.summary: When an expression fails to evaluate, After Effects marks it in the editor with an inline message and shows a warning banner with the line number at the bottom of the Composition and Layer panels.

automation.notes: Property.expressionError (read-only) returns the error text of a property's last expression, so a script can find failing expressions; Project.autoFixExpressions replaces text in broken expressions. The inline marker and the warning banner are display only.

features.name: Expression Language menu > Text > Font
features.summary: Dialog opened from the Expression Language menu that lets you pick a typeface and style and inserts its PostScript-style font name into the expression, avoiding font-name errors.

automation.notes: Dialog only; a script writes the font's PostScript name into the expression text with Property.expression instead. Fonts named only inside expressions are not counted as project fonts for syncing or the Resolve Fonts dialog unless a layer also uses them.

features.name: Expression Language menu
features.summary: Pop-up menu under an expression that lists the After Effects expression objects, attributes and methods and inserts the chosen one at the insertion point or in place of selected text.

automation.notes: An editing aid inside the expression field; there is no member or command id for it. Scripts write the finished text to Property.expression instead.

features.name: Expression pick whip
features.summary: Spiral button beside an expression field that is dragged onto another property, layer or value to write the reference to it into the expression automatically.

automation.notes: Dragging the whip is interactive; the scripted equivalent is writing the generated reference text into Property.expression.

features.name: Expression selector attributes
features.summary: textIndex, textTotal and selectorValue are extra attributes available only inside a text animator's Expression selector, giving the current character, word or line index, the total count and the value from the selector above.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression. Using them outside an Expression selector is a syntax error.

features.name: Expressions
features.summary: JavaScript-based snippets attached to an animatable property that compute its value at each frame, used to link properties, generate motion procedurally and replace hand-set keyframes.

automation.notes: Any property where Property.canSetExpression is true accepts an expression string through Property.expression.

features.name: Show Expression Editor
features.summary: Graph Editor option that shows or hides the expression field for the selected property at the bottom of the Graph Editor.

automation.notes: Display toggle in the Graph Editor options menu with no object-model member or command id.

features.name: JavaScript expression engine
features.summary: Default expression engine based on a modern ECMAScript (V8 on Windows) that evaluates faster than ExtendScript and allows newer syntax such as let, const, arrow functions and modern array and string methods.

automation.notes: Selected per project with Project.expressionEngine = "javascript-1.0".

features.name: Expression function library (.jsx)
features.summary: A .jsx file imported as footage can hold custom functions and data that expressions call through footage("name.jsx"), giving a shared library across layers.

automation.notes: Import the .jsx file as a footage item; under the JavaScript engine, library code must prefix built-ins with thisLayer. or thisProperty. and use vector math functions on arrays.

features.name: Camera attributes and methods
features.summary: Expression access to camera layer settings: point of interest, zoom, depth of field, focus distance, aperture, blur level, iris and highlight settings, and active state.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Color Conversion methods
features.summary: Converters between RGBA and HSLA colour arrays and from hex strings to RGBA: rgbToHsl, hslToRgb and hexToRgb.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Comp attributes and methods
features.summary: Attributes of a composition reachable from expressions, such as layer() lookup by index, name or relative offset, layerByComment, composition markers, size, duration, frame duration, shutter settings, background colour and active camera.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Dropdown Menu attributes
features.summary: Expression attributes on dropdown menu properties that return the selected item's text, the full list of item strings, or the selected text at a given time (text, items, textAtTime).

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Effect attributes and methods
features.summary: Expression access to an applied effect: whether it is active and its parameters by name or index through param().

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Footage attributes and methods
features.summary: Attributes of a footage item reachable from expressions, including size, duration and frame rate plus data access for JSON, CSV and TSV sources (sourceText, sourceData, dataValue, dataKeyCount, dataKeyTimes, dataKeyValues).

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Global objects, attributes and methods
features.summary: Top-level expression elements available everywhere: comp(), footage(), thisComp, thisProject, thisLayer, thisProperty, time, colorDepth, value and posterizeTime().

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Interpolation methods
features.summary: Functions that map an input range to an output range linearly or with eased curves: linear, ease, easeIn and easeOut.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Key attributes and methods
features.summary: Keyframe objects returned by key() and nearestKey() expose a keyframe's value, time and index.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Layer 3D attributes and methods
features.summary: Expression access to 3D layer orientation, X/Y/Z rotation and material options such as light transmission, shadows, ambient, diffuse, specular and metal.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Layer General attributes and methods
features.summary: Basic layer attributes for expressions: width, height, index, parent, in and out points, start time, video and audio presence, active and enabled state, plus sampleImage for reading pixel colours.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Layer Properties attributes and methods
features.summary: Expression access to a layer's transform properties, audio levels, time remap, layer markers and name.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Layer Space Transforms methods
features.summary: Methods that convert points and vectors between layer, composition and world space (toComp, fromComp, toWorld, fromWorld, their Vec variants and fromCompToSurface).

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Layer Sub-objects attributes and methods
features.summary: Expression accessors from a layer to its source item, the source time, its source bounding rectangle (sourceRectAtTime), and its effects and masks by name or index.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Light attributes and methods
features.summary: Expression access to light layer settings: point of interest, intensity, colour, cone angle and feather, and shadow darkness and diffusion.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: MarkerKey attributes
features.summary: Marker keyframes expose their comment, duration, chapter, URL, frame target, cue point fields and parameters; composition markers also report whether they are protected regions.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Mask attributes and methods
features.summary: Expression access to a layer mask's opacity, feather, expansion and inverted state.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Other Math methods
features.summary: Angle unit converters degreesToRadians and radiansToDegrees, used alongside the standard JavaScript Math object.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Path methods
features.summary: Methods on mask, shape and brush-stroke paths that read points and tangents, test whether the path is closed, sample a point, tangent or normal along it, and build a new path with createPath().

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Project attributes
features.summary: Read-only project information for expressions through thisProject: the project file path, its bits per channel and whether colours blend with 1.0 gamma.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Property attributes and methods
features.summary: Methods every animatable property offers to expressions: value and valueAtTime, velocity and speed, wiggle and temporalWiggle, smooth, loopIn/loopOut and their duration forms, keyframe access (key, nearestKey, numKeys) and propertyGroup navigation.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Random Numbers methods
features.summary: Seeded uniform and Gaussian random values and smooth noise for expressions: seedRandom, random, gaussRandom and noise.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Text style object
features.summary: Object returned by sourceText.style or getStyleAt() that exposes a text layer's character and paragraph styling (font, size, faux styles, caps, tracking, leading, baseline, fill, stroke and more) and chainable set functions to change it in an expression.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression. Requires the JavaScript expression engine.

features.name: Time conversion methods
features.summary: Functions that convert between seconds and frames, timecode, NTSC timecode, feet and frames, or the project's current time display format (timeToFrames, framesToTime, timeToTimecode and related).

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Vector Math methods
features.summary: Array arithmetic and geometry helpers for expressions: add, sub, mul, div, clamp, dot, cross, normalize, length and lookAt.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Legacy ExtendScript expression engine
features.summary: Older ECMAScript 3 based expression engine kept for compatibility; some of its syntax (if without else at the end, this() shorthand, snake_case methods, sourceText[i] indexing) must be rewritten to run under the JavaScript engine.

automation.notes: Selected per project with Project.expressionEngine = "extendscript".

features.name: Linking text styles across layers
features.summary: A Source Text expression can take the whole style of a main text layer and optionally override parts of it, so many titles follow one master layer's font and formatting.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Paragraph attributes in expressions
features.summary: Expressions can read and set paragraph options for the whole text layer, including direction, every-line composer, first-line indent, justification, leading type, margins, space before and after, and hanging Roman punctuation.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Per-character text styling in expressions
features.summary: Style set functions accept a start index and character count, so an expression can restyle individual characters or words (font, size, bold, superscript) with the text reflowing as it would from the Character panel.

automation.notes: Language element used inside expression text, not an application command; a script puts an expression that uses it on a property by writing the string to Property.expression.

features.name: Expression Editor preferences
features.summary: Editor options for the expression field: font size (8-24 pt), syntax highlighting, line numbers, indent guides, brace matching, auto-inserted and auto-indented braces, folding, word wrap, tabs and tab width, backspace unindent, inline errors and auto-complete.

automation.notes: Set in the Preferences dialog; preference key names are not documented.

features.name: Expression editor Theme
features.summary: Chooses a predefined colour theme for the expression editor or a custom one with per-element colours (text, background, keywords, comments, numbers and so on) and selection opacity, previewed live; custom themes can be saved.

automation.notes: Set in the Preferences dialog; preference key names are not documented.

features.name: Show Warning Banner When Project Contains Expression Errors
features.summary: Preference that controls whether failing expressions raise the warning banner at the bottom of the Composition and Layer panels.

automation.notes: Set in the Preferences dialog; the preference key name is not documented.

features.name: Expression Pick Whip Writes Compact English
features.summary: Preference that makes the pick whip write language-independent dotted property names (transform.position) instead of quoted display names.

automation.notes: Set in the Preferences dialog; the preference key name is not documented.

features.name: Remove Expression
features.summary: Deletes the expression from the selected property so it goes back to its static or keyframed value; Alt-clicking the stopwatch again also removes it.

automation.notes: Needs a selected property with an expression. Writing an empty string to Property.expression clears it.

features.name: Reveal Expression Errors
features.summary: Shows only the properties of the selected layers whose expressions currently fail, so the errors can be found and fixed.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers.

features.name: Show only properties with expressions
features.summary: Keyboard command that collapses the selected layers to just the properties that carry expressions.

automation.notes: Keyboard command (EE) that changes which properties the Timeline shows; no command id and no member for property visibility. Needs selected layers.

features.name: Show Post-Expression Graph
features.summary: Graph Editor button that overlays the value or velocity curve after the expression is applied, drawn brightly over the dimmer pre-expression curve.

automation.notes: Display toggle in the Graph Editor with no object-model member or command id.

domains.name: Masks and shapes
domains.covers: Masks and mask modes, shape layers, shape groups and operators, and the pen and shape tools.

features.name: Ellipse
features.summary: Adds a parametric ellipse path with Size and Position properties.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Shape - Ellipse.

features.name: Fill
features.summary: Adds a solid-color fill paint operation for the paths above it in the group.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Graphic - Fill.

features.name: Gradient Fill
features.summary: Adds a linear or radial gradient fill with start and end points and highlight controls.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Graphic - G-Fill. Gradient fills and strokes can be added and their type, start and end points and highlight set, but the Colors property (ADBE Vector Grad Colors) has no settable value in scripting; gradient colours are edited by hand in the Gradient Editor.

features.name: Gradient Stroke
features.summary: Adds a stroke painted with a linear or radial gradient.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Graphic - G-Stroke.

features.name: Group (Empty)
features.summary: Adds an empty group to hold other shape attributes, with its own transform and blend mode.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Group.

features.name: Merge Paths
features.summary: Combines all paths above it in the group into one compound path using Merge, Add, Subtract, Intersect or Exclude Intersections.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Merge.

features.name: Offset Paths
features.summary: Expands (positive Amount) or contracts (negative) paths by offsetting them, and can make concentric copies.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Offset.

features.name: Path
features.summary: Adds a free Bezier path whose vertices are edited in the Composition panel.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Shape - Group.

features.name: Polystar
features.summary: Adds a parametric star or polygon path with point count, rotation and inner and outer radius and roundness.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Shape - Star.

features.name: Pucker & Bloat
features.summary: Pulls vertices out while bending segments in (pucker), or the reverse (bloat).

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - PB.

features.name: Rectangle
features.summary: Adds a parametric rectangle path with Size, Position and Roundness properties.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Shape - Rect.

features.name: Repeater
features.summary: Renders virtual copies of the paths, fills and strokes above it, applying its Transform group cumulatively to each copy; always added at the end of the group.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Repeater.

features.name: Round Corners
features.summary: Rounds path corners by a Radius value.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - RC.

features.name: Stroke
features.summary: Adds a solid-color stroke paint operation with width, caps, joins, dashes, taper and wave.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Graphic - Stroke.

features.name: Trim Paths
features.summary: Shows only part of a path between animatable Start, End and Offset values, giving write-on results.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Trim.

features.name: Twist
features.summary: Rotates paths more at the center than at the edges, clockwise for positive angles.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Twist.

features.name: Add Vertex tool
features.summary: Pen-group tool that inserts a vertex where you click on a path segment.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable; editing is interactive.

features.name: Wiggle Paths
features.summary: Randomly jags paths into peaks and valleys of varying size that animate on their own, with size, detail, correlation and phase controls.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Roughen.

features.name: Wiggle Transform
features.summary: Self-animating random offsets of position, anchor point, scale and rotation; placed after a Repeater it randomizes each copy separately.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Wiggler.

features.name: Zig Zag
features.summary: Turns paths into regular peaks and valleys with a set size, ridges per segment and smooth or corner points.

automation.notes: Also in the Add menu of the Tools panel; needs a selected shape layer or group, and Alt/Option places the item at the end of the group. Match name ADBE Vector Filter - Zigzag.

features.name: Auto-trace
features.summary: Generates Bezier masks that outline the alpha, red, green, blue or luminance channel at the current frame or across the work area, with Invert, Blur, Tolerance, Threshold, Minimum Area, Corner Roundness, Apply To New Layer and Preview options.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; needs selected layers, which are switched to Best quality. Layer > Auto-trace... (command 3044) opens a modal dialog, and neither the object model nor any other command generates traced masks. Scripts can only add masks from known vertices (add_mask, set_bezier_path).

features.name: Closed
features.summary: Toggles the selected mask or shape path between open and closed.

automation.notes: Needs a selected path. Only closed masks affect transparency.

features.name: Composite
features.summary: Fill and stroke option that sets render order within the group; Above Previous In Same Group overrides the default bottom-to-top painting.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Composite Order.

features.name: Convert To Bezier Path
features.summary: Turns a parametric shape path (rectangle, ellipse, polystar) into a free Bezier path whose vertices can be edited.

automation.notes: Needs a selected parametric path in a shape layer; conversion adjusts the shape Position.

features.name: Convert Vertex tool
features.summary: Pen-group tool that toggles a vertex between smooth and corner and, on RotoBezier paths, drags to adjust vertex tension (Alt/Option with the Pen tool activates it).

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable; editing is interactive.

features.name: Create Shapes from Vector Layer
features.summary: Converts the selected Illustrator, PDF or SVG footage layer into a native shape layer placed above it (the original is muted), keeping gradient fills, gradient strokes and transparency; newer builds label it Create Shapes and Text from Vector Layer and can also make editable text.

automation.notes: Works on one selected footage layer at a time; freeform gradients and Illustrator blend modes are dropped. 3973 is Types-for-Adobe CreateShapesFromVectorLayer (hyperbrew CreateFootageOutlines).

features.name: Dashes
features.summary: Turns a stroke into dashes by adding up to three dash and gap pairs plus an Offset that slides the pattern along the path.

automation.notes: The Add A Dash Or Gap button adds entries; match names ADBE Vector Stroke Dashes, ADBE Vector Stroke Dash 1, ADBE Vector Stroke Gap 1, ADBE Vector Stroke Offset.

features.name: Delete mask
features.summary: Removes the selected mask from its layer.

automation.notes: Needs a selected mask (in the Timeline panel or Layer panel); pressing Delete removes it. Id 2368 is RemoveMask in both command lists.

features.name: Delete Vertex tool
features.summary: Pen-group tool that removes the vertex you click from a path.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable; editing is interactive.

features.name: Direct Selection tool
features.summary: Temporary variant of the Selection tool on shape layers that selects a clicked shape group directly regardless of nesting depth.

automation.notes: Temporary modifier of the Selection tool while clicking in a viewer; no ToolType value or member.

features.name: Constrain shape while drawing
features.summary: Holding Shift makes squares and circles and keeps polygons and stars from rotating.

automation.notes: Works only during an interactive drag with a shape tool; the resulting values are ordinary shape properties afterwards.

features.name: Change star inner roundness while drawing
features.summary: Raises (Page Up) or lowers (Page Down) the inner roundness of a star during the drag.

automation.notes: Works only during an interactive drag with a shape tool; the resulting values are ordinary shape properties afterwards.

features.name: Change outer roundness while drawing
features.summary: Right Arrow maximizes rounded-rectangle roundness or increases polygon and star outer roundness; Left Arrow does the opposite.

automation.notes: Works only during an interactive drag with a shape tool; the resulting values are ordinary shape properties afterwards.

features.name: Change points or roundness while drawing
features.summary: Raises (Up Arrow) or lowers (Down Arrow) the point count of a star or polygon, or the roundness of a rounded rectangle, during the drag.

automation.notes: Works only during an interactive drag with a shape tool; the resulting values are ordinary shape properties afterwards.

features.name: Reposition shape while drawing
features.summary: Holding the spacebar (or middle mouse button) moves the shape or mask being drawn instead of resizing it.

automation.notes: Works only during an interactive drag with a shape tool; the resulting values are ordinary shape properties afterwards.

features.name: Change star outer radius only while drawing
features.summary: Holding the key keeps a star inner radius fixed while the drag changes the outer radius; for rectangles and ellipses it scales around the center.

automation.notes: Works only during an interactive drag with a shape tool; the resulting values are ordinary shape properties afterwards.

features.name: Duplicate mask
features.summary: Copies selected masks onto the same layer; masks can also be copied, cut and pasted to other layers, where a pasted mask replaces a selected one.

automation.notes: Needs selected masks.

features.name: Ellipse tool
features.summary: Draws ellipses and circles (Shift) as masks or shapes. On a shape layer it makes a parametric path unless Alt/Option is held at the start of the drag.

automation.notes: Q activates and cycles the Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon and Star tools. Selecting the tool is scriptable; drawing with it is interactive.

features.name: Feather Falloff
features.summary: Chooses the falloff curve of a mask feather: Smooth (default) or Linear.

automation.notes: Needs selected masks. 3988 Smooth, 3989 Linear.

features.name: Feather point extent
features.summary: Radius of a feather point, edited by dragging its extent handle or numerically from the point context menu, along with its corner angle.

automation.notes: 3993 is the hyperbrew FeatherEditExtent command (opens a dialog). The point context menu's Edit Extent command (3993) opens a dialog and needs a selected feather point; scripts set Shape.featherRadii and featherRelCornerAngles instead (set_bezier_path featherPoints).

features.name: Feather point Hold
features.summary: Context-menu option that keeps the feather radius constant from a feather point to the next one.

automation.notes: 3991 is the hyperbrew FeatherHold command.

features.name: Feather point tension
features.summary: Smoothness of the feather boundary through a feather point, set by Alt/Option-dragging its extent handle or numerically from the point context menu.

automation.notes: 3992 is the hyperbrew FeatherEditTension command (opens a dialog). The point context menu's Edit Tension command (3992) opens a dialog and needs a selected feather point; scripts set Shape.featherTensions instead (set_bezier_path featherPoints).

features.name: Variable-width mask feather
features.summary: Feather points placed along a closed mask with the Mask Feather tool set different feather widths around the path; points can be dragged, slid with arrow keys, snapped to the path or deleted.

automation.notes: Point editing is interactive; scripts write feather points through the Shape value of the mask path.

features.name: Fill Rule
features.summary: Rule deciding what counts as inside a self-intersecting or compound path: Non-Zero Winding (default, direction-aware) or Even-Odd.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Fill Rule.

features.name: Fill and Stroke options (Tools panel)
features.summary: Fill and Stroke controls in the Tools panel that set type (None, Solid Color, Linear Gradient, Radial Gradient), color, blending mode and opacity for new shapes or for selected shapes; Alt/Option-clicking a swatch cycles the type.

automation.notes: Defaults for interactive drawing, shown only when a shape layer is selected or a drawing tool is active. Existing fills and strokes are set through their Color and Opacity properties.

features.name: Free Transform Points
features.summary: Puts a bounding box around the selected path vertices or the whole mask or shape path so they can be moved, scaled and rotated together around a movable anchor; Esc or Enter exits.

automation.notes: Needs selected vertices or a selected mask or Path property; the transform itself is interactive. Double-clicking a path with the Selection tool also enters this mode. Free Transform Points (command 2051) enters an interactive bounding-box mode on selected vertices, and scripts cannot select vertices. The same move, scale and rotation about an anchor is reached by rewriting the Shape value's vertices and tangents (set_bezier_path transform).

features.name: Gradient Editor
features.summary: Color picker mode for editing gradient color and opacity stops of a gradient fill or stroke; the Colors property can be keyframed.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; the gradient colours (ADBE Vector Grad Colors) have no documented scripting setter.

features.name: Gradient Start Point, End Point and Highlight
features.summary: Properties mapping a gradient onto a shape: Start and End Point for direction and scale, plus Highlight Length and Angle to offset a radial center; also draggable in the Composition panel.

automation.notes: Match names ADBE Vector Grad Start Pt, ADBE Vector Grad End Pt, ADBE Vector Grad HiLite Length, ADBE Vector Grad HiLite Angle.

features.name: Group Shapes
features.summary: Wraps the selected shapes or shape attributes in a new group with its own transform, centered anchor point and blend mode.

automation.notes: Needs selected shapes at the same grouping level. No single grouping method: scripts add an ADBE Vector Group and move items into it.

features.name: Hide Locked Masks
features.summary: Hides the outlines of locked masks in the viewers while keeping their effect.

automation.notes: Hide Locked Masks (2524) is a toggle with no object-model member, so a script cannot read whether locked masks are currently hidden; manage_masks toggles it on the selected layers.

features.name: Target menu (Layer panel)
features.summary: Layer panel menu that names the mask a new drawing will replace; set it to None to add a new mask instead.

automation.notes: Layer panel menu that only affects interactive drawing; scripts replace a mask by setting its Mask Path (MaskPropertyGroup.maskPath) or add one through the layer's Masks group.

features.name: Line Cap
features.summary: End style of open strokes and dashes: Butt Cap, Round Cap or Projecting Cap.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Stroke Line Cap.

features.name: Line Join
features.summary: Corner style of strokes: Miter Join, Round Join or Bevel Join, with Miter Limit deciding when a miter falls back to a bevel.

automation.notes: Match names ADBE Vector Stroke Line Join and ADBE Vector Stroke Miter Limit.

features.name: Lock Other Masks
features.summary: Locks every mask on the layer except the selected ones, often combined with Hide Locked Masks to isolate masks.

automation.notes: Needs selected masks.

features.name: Mask path color
features.summary: Outline color used for a mask in the viewers and next to its name in the Timeline panel, changed through the color swatch; preferences can pick contrasting or cycling colors automatically.

features.name: Mask Expansion
features.summary: Grows or shrinks the area a mask influences by a pixel offset from the path (scrubbable to plus or minus 32,000) without changing the path itself.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name MaskExpansion.

features.name: Mask Feather
features.summary: Softens mask edges over a horizontal and vertical width (up to 32,000 pixels, Gaussian falloff, straddling the edge); the dialog sets it numerically.

automation.notes: Shortcut opens the Mask Feather dialog (modal). F reveals the property. Feather is clipped at the layer bounds.

features.name: Mask Feather tool
features.summary: Pen-group tool for adding and adjusting variable-width feather points on closed masks.

automation.notes: Reached with G from the Pen tool. Selecting the tool is scriptable; placing points is interactive.

features.name: Create a mask or shape path from a motion path
features.summary: Pastes copied Position or Anchor Point keyframes into a selected Mask Path or shape Path property to turn the motion path into an outline (offset because layer and composition spaces differ).

automation.notes: Select the Position or Anchor Point keyframes with Property.setSelectedAtKey and run Edit > Copy (19), then select the Mask Path or shape Path property (PropertyBase.selected) and run Edit > Paste (20). The result is offset because layer and composition spaces differ.

features.name: Mask Interpolation
features.summary: Smart Mask Interpolation panel that creates intermediate mask path keyframes between two selected keyframes, with Keyframe Rate, Keyframe Fields, Use Linear Vertex Paths, Bending Resistance, Quality, Add Mask Path Vertices, Matching Method, Use 1:1 Vertex Matches and First Vertices Match.

automation.notes: Opens the panel from the Window menu. Its menu ids are install-specific (5016, 5058 in the published lists), so look up by name with app.findMenuCommandId("Mask Interpolation"). Interpolating needs two adjacent selected Mask Path keyframes and the panel's Apply button, which scripts cannot press.

features.name: Inverted
features.summary: Swaps what counts as inside and outside a mask, so the mask cuts out its interior instead of keeping it.

automation.notes: Needs selected masks or a layer with masks.

features.name: Lock mask
features.summary: Lock switch on a mask that prevents selecting or targeting it in any panel.

automation.notes: Hyperbrew name Locked.

features.name: Add (mask mode)
features.summary: Default mode: the mask adds its coverage to the masks above it. Chosen from the mode menu beside the mask name.

automation.notes: Mask modes cannot be keyframed. The key works only while drawing or dragging a closed mask with the mouse button held (for the Pen tool, while closing the path). Hyperbrew name under the Mask > Mode submenu.

features.name: Darken (mask mode)
features.summary: Where masks overlap, the lowest transparency value wins. Chosen from the mode menu beside the mask name.

automation.notes: Mask modes cannot be keyframed. The key works only while drawing or dragging a closed mask with the mouse button held (for the Pen tool, while closing the path). Hyperbrew name under the Mask > Mode submenu.

features.name: Difference (mask mode)
features.summary: Masks act normally where they do not overlap and cancel out where they do. Chosen from the mode menu beside the mask name.

automation.notes: Mask modes cannot be keyframed. The key works only while drawing or dragging a closed mask with the mouse button held (for the Pen tool, while closing the path). Hyperbrew name under the Mask > Mode submenu.

features.name: Intersect (mask mode)
features.summary: Keeps only the area where the mask overlaps the masks above it. Chosen from the mode menu beside the mask name.

automation.notes: Mask modes cannot be keyframed. The key works only while drawing or dragging a closed mask with the mouse button held (for the Pen tool, while closing the path). Hyperbrew name under the Mask > Mode submenu.

features.name: Lighten (mask mode)
features.summary: Where masks overlap, the highest transparency value wins. Chosen from the mode menu beside the mask name.

automation.notes: Mask modes cannot be keyframed. The key works only while drawing or dragging a closed mask with the mouse button held (for the Pen tool, while closing the path). Hyperbrew name under the Mask > Mode submenu.

features.name: None (mask mode)
features.summary: Mask has no effect on the layer alpha; useful when the path only feeds an effect or shape. Chosen from the mode menu beside the mask name.

automation.notes: Mask modes cannot be keyframed. The key works only while drawing or dragging a closed mask with the mouse button held (for the Pen tool, while closing the path). Hyperbrew name under the Mask > Mode submenu.

features.name: Subtract (mask mode)
features.summary: Removes the mask area from the masks above, for example to cut a hole. Chosen from the mode menu beside the mask name.

automation.notes: Mask modes cannot be keyframed. The key works only while drawing or dragging a closed mask with the mouse button held (for the Pen tool, while closing the path). Hyperbrew name under the Mask > Mode submenu.

features.name: Mask Motion Blur
features.summary: Per-mask motion blur: Same As Layer follows the layer switch, On blurs regardless of it, Off never blurs; the composition motion blur switch must be on.

automation.notes: Needs selected masks. 2798 SameAsLayer, 2799 On, 2800 Off.

features.name: Mask
features.summary: Scripting class for one mask on a layer, exposing its path, mode, feather, opacity, expansion, inversion, lock, color, RotoBezier and motion-blur settings.

features.name: Mask Opacity
features.summary: Controls how strongly a closed mask affects the layer alpha inside the mask; the area outside is always transparent.

automation.notes: TT reveals the property. Hyperbrew name MaskOpacity (dialog entry).

features.name: Mask Path
features.summary: Animatable property holding the mask outline; set keyframes on it to animate or rotoscope the mask (M reveals it, Alt+Shift+M / Option+Shift+M sets a keyframe).

automation.notes: Mask path coordinates are in layer space.

features.name: Mask Reference
features.summary: Compositing option on an effect that limits it to one or more masks on the same layer, so feather, opacity and mask modes shape where the effect shows.

automation.notes: Added with the + button under an effect Compositing Options. Effect masks do not change the layer alpha. Only masks on the same layer can be referenced.

features.name: Mask Shape
features.summary: Dialog that sets a mask path numerically: Reset To a Rectangle or Ellipse of a given bounding box, also reached by clicking the underlined Mask Path value.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; Needs selected masks or a layer with masks.

features.name: Merge Paths Mode
features.summary: Calculation used by Merge Paths: Merge (compound path, used for text conversion), Add, Subtract, Intersect or Exclude Intersections.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Merge Type.

features.name: New Mask
features.summary: Adds a rectangular mask the size of the layer frame to the selected layer, ready to be reshaped or set numerically in Mask Shape.

automation.notes: Needs a selected layer. Scripts add a mask with match name ADBE Mask Atom to the Masks group and assign a Shape.

features.name: Offset Paths Copies and Copy Offset
features.summary: Offset Paths controls that make concentric copies of a shape and push them outward or inward, with Line Join and Miter Limit for the offset corners.

automation.notes: Match names ADBE Vector Offset Copies, ADBE Vector Offset Copy Offset, ADBE Vector Offset Line Join.

features.name: Paste path from Illustrator or Photoshop
features.summary: Pastes a path copied in Illustrator (with AICB clipboard output) or Photoshop (72 dpi document) as a new mask on the selected layer or into a selected mask or shape Path property.

automation.notes: Edit > Paste (20) with the layer or a target path property selected. The clipboard must already hold a path copied in Illustrator (with AICB output) or Photoshop; ExtendScript cannot fill the clipboard. Extra pasted paths beyond the first become masks.

features.name: Pen tool
features.summary: Draws Bezier or RotoBezier paths vertex by vertex as masks on a selected layer or shapes on a shape layer; clicking makes corners, dragging makes curves, and clicking the first vertex closes the path.

automation.notes: G toggles between the Pen and Mask Feather tools (a preference can turn this off). The RotoBezier checkbox in the Tools panel sets the path type. Selecting the tool is scriptable; drawing is interactive.

features.name: Temporarily switch pen tools
features.summary: With the Selection tool over a path, holding the keys temporarily gives the Pen tool, Add Vertex over a segment or Convert Vertex over a vertex; Ctrl/Cmd with a pen tool gives the Selection tool.

automation.notes: Held modifier during interactive editing; no member or command.

features.name: Polygon tool
features.summary: Draws regular polygons, which become polystar paths without inner radius or inner roundness. On a shape layer it makes a parametric path unless Alt/Option is held at the start of the drag.

automation.notes: Q activates and cycles the Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon and Star tools. Selecting the tool is scriptable; drawing with it is interactive.

features.name: Rectangle tool
features.summary: Draws rectangles and squares (Shift) as masks on a selected layer or as shapes on a shape layer; double-clicking it creates one the size of the layer. On a shape layer it makes a parametric path unless Alt/Option is held at the start of the drag.

automation.notes: Q activates and cycles the Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon and Star tools. Selecting the tool is scriptable; drawing with it is interactive.

features.name: Remove All Masks
features.summary: Deletes every mask on the selected layers.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers.

features.name: Rename mask
features.summary: Gives a mask a descriptive name in the Timeline panel (Enter/Return or the Rename context command).

features.name: Repeater Copies, Offset and Composite
features.summary: Repeater controls for the number of copies, an offset that shifts which copies are transformed, whether copies stack above or below, and start and end opacity across the copies.

automation.notes: Match names ADBE Vector Repeater Copies, ADBE Vector Repeater Offset, ADBE Vector Repeater Order, ADBE Vector Repeater Transform.

features.name: Reverse Path Direction
features.summary: Path button that flips the direction of a path, used with the non-zero winding rule to punch holes in compound paths.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Shape Direction.

features.name: Rounded Rectangle tool
features.summary: Draws rectangles with rounded corners; arrow keys or the mouse wheel change roundness during the drag. On a shape layer it makes a parametric path unless Alt/Option is held at the start of the drag.

automation.notes: Q activates and cycles the Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon and Star tools. Selecting the tool is scriptable; drawing with it is interactive.

features.name: Select next or previous mask
features.summary: Moves the mask selection to the next mask on the layer (add Shift for the previous one).

features.name: Set First Vertex
features.summary: Makes the selected vertex the first vertex of an animated path, which governs vertex matching between keyframes, the start of pasted motion paths and Trim Paths.

automation.notes: Needs one selected vertex; the first vertex is drawn slightly larger. Set First Vertex (command 2768) needs one selected vertex, which scripts cannot select. Rotating the order of the Shape value's vertices, tangents and feather segments makes another vertex first (set_bezier_path firstVertex); this applies to closed paths.

features.name: Duplicate shape group while transforming
features.summary: Alt/Option-dragging a selected shape group in group selection mode moves, rotates or scales a copy instead of the original.

automation.notes: Interactive drag modifier with no member or command; PropertyBase.duplicate is the scripted way to copy a group.

features.name: Shape group Blend Mode
features.summary: Blending mode of a shape group, fill or stroke within the shape layer.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Blend Mode. ADBE Vector Blend Mode takes the position in its Blend Mode menu; the scripting documentation does not list the values, so the tools take that number (1 = Normal) rather than mode names.

features.name: Shape group Transform
features.summary: Transform property group of each shape group (anchor point, position, scale, skew, rotation, opacity) that moves every shape in the group, shown as a dashed box in the Composition panel.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Transform Group; properties such as ADBE Vector Position and ADBE Vector Skew.

features.name: Shape layer
features.summary: Synthetic vector layer whose Contents group holds shapes made of paths, fills, strokes and path operations; it is always continuously rasterized and cannot be opened in the Layer panel.

automation.notes: Contents match name ADBE Root Vectors Group; layer match name ADBE Vector Layer.

features.name: Shape
features.summary: Value object describing a Bezier path (vertices, in and out tangents, closed flag and variable-width feather points) used for mask paths and shape-layer paths.

features.name: Create shape or mask the size of the layer
features.summary: Double-clicking a shape tool in the Tools panel creates a mask the size of the selected layer, replaces a selected mask or shape path, or makes a composition-sized shape when nothing is selected.

automation.notes: Add a mask ("ADBE Mask Atom" in the layer's "ADBE Mask Parade" group) and set its Mask Path to a closed Shape with vertices at the layer's corners (0,0 to width,height). The double-click gesture itself is interactive.

features.name: Shape selection modes
features.summary: Four levels of selecting shape-layer content: the whole layer, a group (double-click to descend), free-transform of several vertices, and path editing of individual vertices.

automation.notes: Interactive selection levels in the viewer; scripts select properties with PropertyBase.selected instead.

features.name: Star tool
features.summary: Draws stars with adjustable point count and inner and outer radius and roundness, stored as polystar paths. On a shape layer it makes a parametric path unless Alt/Option is held at the start of the drag.

automation.notes: Q activates and cycles the Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon and Star tools. Selecting the tool is scriptable; drawing with it is interactive.

features.name: Taper
features.summary: Property group of a stroke that narrows its width toward the start and end of the path for a hand-drawn look.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Stroke Taper.

features.name: Wave
features.summary: Property group of a stroke that modulates its width in waves along the path.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Stroke Wave.

features.name: Stroke Width (Tools panel)
features.summary: Tools panel control setting the stroke width in pixels for new shapes or the selected shapes.

automation.notes: The Tools panel default is not scriptable; existing strokes use ADBE Vector Stroke Width. The Tools panel's Stroke Width default for new shapes has no object-model member or command. Scripts set ADBE Vector Stroke Width on existing strokes (set_shape_content width) and on strokes they add.

features.name: Length Units
features.summary: Taper setting choosing whether taper lengths are a Percentage of the path or Pixels; pixels keep the taper constant when the path length changes.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Length Units.

features.name: Start Ease and End Ease
features.summary: Roundness of the taper curve: negative values give pointed ends, zero linear, positive rounder ones.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Start Ease, ADBE Vector Taper End Ease.

features.name: Start Length and End Length
features.summary: How far from each end of the stroke the taper extends.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Start Length, ADBE Vector Taper End Length.

features.name: Start Width and End Width
features.summary: Thickness the stroke narrows to over the start and end taper lengths.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Start Width, ADBE Vector Taper End Width.

features.name: Tool Creates Shape / Tool Creates Mask
features.summary: Tools panel buttons shown with a shape or pen tool active that decide whether drawing on a selected shape layer adds a shape or a mask.

automation.notes: Tools panel option for interactive drawing; scripts add masks or shape groups directly.

features.name: Trim Multiple Shapes
features.summary: Trim Paths option for several paths in a group: trim them all at once or one after another as a compound path.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Trim Type.

features.name: Ungroup Shapes
features.summary: Dissolves the selected shape group, moving its contents up one level.

automation.notes: Needs one selected group.

features.name: Unlock All Masks
features.summary: Clears the lock on all masks of the selected layers.

automation.notes: Needs selected layers.

features.name: Wave Amount
features.summary: Depth of the width waves along the stroke.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Wave Amount.

features.name: Wave Phase
features.summary: Shifts the waves along the path; animating it makes them travel.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Wave Phase.

features.name: Wave Units
features.summary: Measures wavelength in Pixels (suits open paths) or Cycles (keeps closed paths seamless).

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Wave Units.

features.name: Wavelength
features.summary: Spacing of the waves, or the number of waves when units are Cycles.

automation.notes: Native After Effects strokes only; tapered strokes are not imported from Illustrator. Match name ADBE Vector Taper Wavelength.

features.name: Wiggle Paths Correlation
features.summary: How closely each vertex wiggles in step with its neighbors; lower values give a more jagged result.

automation.notes: Wiggles/Second set to 0 with an animated Temporal Phase gives smooth acceleration.

features.name: Zig Zag Points
features.summary: Zig Zag option choosing smooth (wavy) or corner (jagged) peaks.

automation.notes: Match name ADBE Vector Zigzag Points.

domains.name: Text
domains.covers: Text layers, character and paragraph formatting, text animators and selectors, and fonts.

features.name: Add Text Selector
features.summary: Adds a Range, Wiggly or Expression selector to the selected animator group; also in the animator group's Add menu and the Composition panel context menu for selected characters.

automation.notes: Needs a selected animator group. Selectors live in the animator's "ADBE Text Selectors" group.

features.name: Center Text
features.summary: Centres each line within the paragraph.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue; the change applies to every paragraph in the layer.

features.name: Left Align Text
