features.summary: Scales how strongly the animator properties affect the selected characters, from 0% to 100%.

automation.notes: Set through the selector property with match name "ADBE Text Selector Max Amount".

features.name: Ease High and Ease Low
features.summary: Controls how quickly characters change while moving between fully selected and unselected.

automation.notes: Set through the selector property with match name "ADBE Text Levels Max Ease" and "ADBE Text Levels Min Ease".

features.name: Selector Mode
features.summary: Sets how a selector combines with the text and with the selectors above it (Add, Subtract, Intersect and so on), much like mask modes.

automation.notes: Set through the selector property with match name "ADBE Text Selector Mode".

features.name: Randomize Order and Random Seed
features.summary: Applies the range selection to characters in a random order, with Random Seed fixing the order so duplicated animators can match.

automation.notes: Set through the selector property with match name "ADBE Text Random Seed" (Randomize Order is in the same Advanced group).

features.name: Shape
features.summary: Sets the falloff between selected and unselected characters: Square, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Triangle, Round or Smooth.

automation.notes: Set through the selector property with match name in the Range selector's "ADBE Text Range Advanced" group. Limit: Shape, Based On ("ADBE Text Range Type2") and Randomize Order are not in the scripting guide's match-name list; set_text_animator uses those match names with English display-name fallbacks and the menu order Square, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Triangle, Round, Smooth.

features.name: Smoothness
features.summary: Controls how long the transition between characters takes when the Square shape is used; 0% gives a typewriter step.

automation.notes: Set through the selector property with match name "ADBE Text Selector Smoothness".

features.name: Units and Based On
features.summary: Chooses percentage or index units for Start, End and Offset and whether selection counts characters, characters excluding spaces, words or lines.

automation.notes: Set through the selector property with match name "ADBE Text Range Units" (Based On is in the same Advanced group).

features.name: Show Font Names in English
features.summary: Lists CJK font names in English in the font menus.

automation.notes: Changes only how the font menus list names; no member or command id.

features.name: Adobe Single-line Composer
features.summary: Composition method that breaks one line at a time, preferring to compress spacing, for manual control over breaks.

automation.notes: Single-line composition is TextDocument.everyLineComposer = false. Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue; the change applies to every paragraph in the layer.

features.name: Small Caps
features.summary: Displays lowercase letters as small capitals, using the font's own small caps if it has them and synthesizing them otherwise.

automation.notes: TextDocument.smallCaps is read-only; set FontCapsOption via fontCapsOption. Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Use Smart Quotes
features.summary: Replaces straight quotation marks with curly opening and closing quotes as you type.

automation.notes: Affects only interactive typing; scripts set TextDocument.text directly, where the option does not apply.

features.name: Source Text
features.summary: Text layer property that stores the characters and their formatting; keyframing it (hold keyframes) changes the words or styling over time, and expressions can generate it.

automation.notes: Match name "ADBE Text Document". Source Text keyframes are always hold keyframes.

features.name: Space After Paragraph
features.summary: Adds space below each selected paragraph.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue; the change applies to every paragraph in the layer.

features.name: Space Before Paragraph
features.summary: Adds space above each selected paragraph.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue; the change applies to every paragraph in the layer.

features.name: Stroke Color
features.summary: Sets the colour of the outline drawn centred on each character's path.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Stroke Over Fill / Fill Over Stroke
features.summary: Decides whether the stroke of the selected characters is drawn on top of or behind their fill.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Stroke Width
features.summary: Sets the thickness of the character outline.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Subscript
features.summary: Shrinks the selected characters and lowers them below the baseline.

automation.notes: TextDocument.subscript is read-only; set fontBaselineOption. Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Superscript
features.summary: Shrinks the selected characters and raises them above the baseline.

automation.notes: TextDocument.superscript is read-only; set fontBaselineOption. Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Tate-Chuu-Yoko
features.summary: Sets a short run of horizontal characters, such as numbers, upright inside a line of vertical text.

automation.notes: The scripting guide equates BASELINE_VERTICAL_CROSS_STREAM with tate-chu-yoko. Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Text animator group (Animate menu)
features.summary: Animate menu in the Timeline Switches/Modes column (mirroring Animation > Animate Text) that creates an animator group with a default Range selector; the group's Add menu adds further properties or selectors that share it.

automation.notes: Animator groups can be renamed, reordered, copied and deleted like other property groups. Match name "ADBE Text Animator".

features.name: Left-to-Right / Right-to-Left Text Direction
features.summary: Paragraph panel buttons that set paragraph direction for languages such as Arabic and Hebrew.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue; the change applies to every paragraph in the layer.

features.name: TextDocument
features.summary: Scripting value of a text layer's Source Text property that carries the string plus its character and paragraph formatting and box geometry.

automation.notes: Changes take effect only after the edited TextDocument is written back with Property.setValue.

features.name: Text layer
features.summary: Synthetic vector layer that holds editable point or paragraph text, continuously rasterized, with Source Text, path options, more options and text animator groups.

automation.notes: TextLayer is a subclass of AVLayer; its Text property group has match name "ADBE Text Properties".

features.name: Path Options (text on a path)
features.summary: Choosing a mask in the Path menu of a text layer's Path Options lays the text along that open or closed mask, after which text or path can be animated.

automation.notes: The Path property takes the index of a mask on the same layer. Closed masks used as paths should have mask mode None.

features.name: Horizontal / Vertical text orientation
features.summary: Type-tool context commands that turn a selected text layer's horizontal text into vertical text or back; not available while editing text.

automation.notes: Needs a selected text layer. Ids 3065 Horizontal and 3066 Vertical are inferred from their hyperbrew names only.

features.name: Toggle Character and Paragraph panels
features.summary: Tools panel button, shown while a type tool is active, that opens or closes the Character and Paragraph panels; Auto-Open Panels opens them whenever a type tool is chosen.

automation.notes: Id 3013 is inferred from its hyperbrew name ShowTextPanels only. Limit: id 3013 (Show Text Panels) is known by its command-list name only; show_text_panels runs it, unverified in After Effects.

features.name: Tracking
features.summary: Loosens or tightens spacing evenly across the selected characters; tracking and manual kerning add together.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Tsume
features.summary: Reduces the space around each selected character by a percentage without scaling the glyph itself; mainly for CJK text.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Universal Text Engine
features.summary: Text composer used by new text layers that handles mixed scripts, right-to-left languages such as Arabic and Hebrew and Indic scripts, ordering and animating characters by their direction.

automation.notes: Older layers using the Latin/CJK engine can be switched to the Universal Text Engine by script, not back.

features.name: Variable font axes
features.summary: OpenType variable fonts expose continuous design axes (weight, width, slant, italic, optical size and custom ones); the Variable Font pop-up in the Properties panel adjusts them for the whole layer or selected characters.

automation.notes: Per-character static axis values set in the pop-up have no documented setter; scripts animate axes through text animators with addVariableFontAxis. Limit: per-character static axis values set in the Character panel's axis pop-up have no documented setter. Scripts read a font's axes (FontObject.hasDesignAxes, designAxesData) and drive axes through text animators with PropertyGroup.addVariableFontAxis; set_text_animator and find_fonts do both.

features.name: Variable Font Spacing
features.summary: Chooses how character spacing compensates when variable axis animation changes glyph widths: Adaptive, Per-Character or Default (none).

automation.notes: Match name "ADBE Text Variable Font Spacing"; appears only when a variable font axis is animated. Limit: the property exists only while a variable font axis is animated, and its pop-up values (Adaptive, Per-Character, Default in the help) have no documented numeric mapping; set_text_options takes the 1-based menu position.

features.name: Vertical Scale
features.summary: Stretches or squeezes the selected characters in height as a percentage of normal.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Set vertical scale to 100%
features.summary: Returns the vertical scale of the selected text to 100%.

automation.notes: Read the Source Text value (a TextDocument), change the member and write it back with Property.setValue. Setting it on the TextDocument applies to the whole layer; TextDocument.characterRange() targets part of the text.

features.name: Vertical Type tool
features.summary: Creates and edits text that runs top to bottom with lines stacked right to left, as point or paragraph text.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; typing with it is interactive. LayerCollection.addVerticalText creates vertical text directly.

features.name: Wiggly selector
features.summary: Selector that randomly varies how much each character is affected over time, with Max/Min Amount, Wiggles/Second, Correlation, temporal and spatial phase, Lock Dimensions and Random Seed.

automation.notes: Needs a selected animator group. Id 3041 is matched by its hyperbrew name Wiggly. The selector's match name is not listed in the scripting guide. Limit: the scripting guide's match-name list has no Wiggly selector or its settings. set_text_animator adds it as "ADBE Text Wiggly Selector" and finds settings by match name, falling back to the English display names ("Wiggly Selector", "Max Amount", "Wiggles/Second", ...), which only resolve in an English install. Needs a check in After Effects.

domains.name: Effects
domains.covers: The Effect menu and the Effects & Presets panel: every effect category and animation presets.

features.name: Add Grain
features.summary: Adds synthetic film grain, with presets for common film stocks.

automation.notes: Match name "VISINF Grain Implant": add it to a layer's Effects group (match name "ADBE Effect Parade") with addProperty. Works in 8, 16 bpc; supports Multi-Frame Rendering (effect list). Its Effect menu command id in the 2025 list is position-dependent and changes with installed plug-ins; prefer addProperty. Needs a target layer; the Effect menu item applies to the selected layers.

features.name: Advanced Lightning

automation.notes: Match name "ADBE Lightning 2": add it to a layer's Effects group (match name "ADBE Effect Parade") with addProperty. Works in 8 bpc; supports Multi-Frame Rendering (effect list). Its Effect menu command id in the 2025 list is position-dependent and changes with installed plug-ins; prefer addProperty. Needs a target layer; the Effect menu item applies to the selected layers.

features.name: Angle Control
features.summary: Adds a keyframable angle property for expressions to read.

automation.notes: Match name "ADBE Angle Control": add it to a layer's Effects group (match name "ADBE Effect Parade") with addProperty. supports Multi-Frame Rendering (effect list). Its Effect menu command id in the 2025 list is position-dependent and changes with installed plug-ins; prefer addProperty. Needs a target layer; the Effect menu item applies to the selected layers. Expression control effects only hold values for expressions; they do not change the image. Apply to a selected layer (often a null). From a script, add match name "ADBE Angle Control" to the layer's Effects group with PropertyGroup.addProperty.

automation.notes: applyPreset(File) applies to the selected layers of the layer's composition, or to a new solid if none is selected. The menu command opens a file dialog.

features.name: Apply Color LUT
features.summary: Applies a colour lookup table file to the layer.

automation.notes: Match name "ADBE Apply Color LUT2": add it to a layer's Effects group (match name "ADBE Effect Parade") with addProperty. Works in 8, 16, 32 bpc; supports Multi-Frame Rendering (effect list). Its Effect menu command id in the 2025 list is position-dependent and changes with installed plug-ins; prefer addProperty. Needs a target layer; the Effect menu item applies to the selected layers.

features.name: Apply an effect
features.summary: Adds an effect to the selected layers, by dragging or double-clicking it in the Effects & Presets panel or choosing it from the Effect menu.

automation.notes: Script route: layer.property("ADBE Effect Parade").addProperty(matchName). Adding to an indexed group invalidates earlier references to its properties; re-fetch them by index.

features.name: Apply most recent animation preset
features.summary: Applies the animation preset used most recently to the selected layers.

automation.notes: A keyboard shortcut; our sources give no command id for it. Layer.applyPreset with the preset file applies a known preset.

features.name: Apply most recent effect
features.summary: Applies the effect used most recently to the selected layers; the Effect menu shows it under that effect's name.

automation.notes: The 2025 list names id 2452 Last Effect; the 2015 PDF says the most-recent-effect item has no fixed id. Needs selected layers. The Effect menu item for the last effect is labelled with that effect's name, so app.findMenuCommandId cannot find it; the 2025 command list gives 2452 while the 2015 list says it has no fixed id, and scripts cannot read which effect was last applied. set_effect_controls applies an effect by name instead.

features.summary: Copies the frame currently shown in the Composition, Layer or Footage panel to the system clipboard as a PNG (up to 16 bpc, plus a bitmap on Windows), keeping transparency when the transparency grid is on.

automation.notes: Copies what the viewer displays, including display colour transforms; wait for the frame to finish rendering. CompItem.saveFrameToPng writes a frame to a file instead.

features.name: Current-time indicator
features.summary: Red line in the time ruler marking the frame being viewed; moving it changes the current time in the Timeline, Layer and Footage panels, and Shift-dragging snaps to keyframes, markers and points.

features.name: Cycle panels in active frame
features.summary: Moves to the previous or next panel tab in the active frame, such as between open Timeline panels.

automation.notes: Keyboard command with no menu item, so no command id; no member covers it. Viewer.setActive can bring a known viewer forward.

features.name: Cycle through tools
features.summary: Repeating a tool's key, or Alt/Option-clicking its button, steps through the hidden tools in that group; holding a tool key activates it only while held.

automation.notes: Holding a key for a temporary tool does not work for every tool.

features.name: Cycle items in viewer
features.summary: Steps backward or forward through the items listed in the active viewer's menu, such as open compositions.

automation.notes: Shift+. goes forward.

features.name: Delete Workspace
features.summary: Removes a saved workspace chosen in a dialog; the active workspace cannot be deleted.

automation.notes: Opens a dialog; no member deletes workspaces.

features.name: Pause viewer updates (Caps Lock)
features.summary: Caps Lock stops viewers from rendering new images, marked by a red bar, while controls still update; also useful to scrub only cached frames and to avoid redraws during final render.

features.name: Dock or group panels
features.summary: Dragging a panel by its gripper (or a group by the group gripper) onto edge docking zones places it alongside others, while centre or tab-area grouping zones stack it as a tab.

automation.notes: Drag-and-drop only.

features.name: Dolly control modes
features.summary: The Dolly control can move toward the cursor (default), to the cursor, or along the camera's view direction.

automation.notes: Shift+3 cycles the modes. Mapping of enum values to labels inferred from names.

features.name: Edit Guide
features.summary: Context-menu dialog that changes an existing guide's position, units, pinning and colour.

automation.notes: Beta feature.

features.name: Edit Workspaces
features.summary: Dialog for reordering workspaces and choosing which appear in the workspace bar or its overflow menu.

automation.notes: Modal dialog. Window > Workspace > Edit Workspaces (command 4023) opens a modal dialog; there is no scripting member to reorder, hide or delete workspaces.

features.name: Edit this, look at that (locked viewers)
features.summary: With a Composition viewer locked and another composition's Timeline active, view and preview shortcuts act on the locked viewer, so edits upstream can be previewed downstream.

automation.notes: Behaviour of locked viewers; unlock to stop it.

features.name: Export Guides
features.summary: Saves all guides in the current view to a .guides file for reuse in other views, projects or Premiere.

automation.notes: Opens a save dialog. View > Export Guides (command 4159) opens a save dialog, and the Item.guides array that would let a script write the file itself is not in the After Effects 26.0 typings this server audits against.

features.name: Adaptive Resolution
features.summary: Lowers resolution (and ray-trace quality in ray-traced comps) while dragging or scrubbing, down to the limit set in Previews preferences.

automation.notes: The Adaptive Resolution Priority preference sets the minimum resolution and whether 3D quality or resolution drops.

features.name: Draft
features.summary: Uses a single ray per pixel in ray-traced 3D compositions for quick previews.

automation.notes: Errors in Classic 3D compositions.

features.name: Fast Draft
features.summary: Downsampled preview at 1/4 resolution for laying out complex or ray-traced scenes, with effects and mattes still on.

features.name: Fast Previews
features.summary: Viewer menu choosing the speed/quality mode used while interacting: Off (Final Quality), Adaptive Resolution, Draft, Fast Draft or Wireframe.

automation.notes: Not available on Layer or Footage viewers through scripting.

features.name: Off (Final Quality)
features.summary: Previews at final quality with no interaction shortcuts.

features.name: Wireframe
features.summary: Draws layers as outlines for the fastest interaction; sends nothing to external video preview.

features.name: Resize window to fit screen
features.summary: Resizes the application or floating window to the screen; pressing again makes its contents fill the screen.

automation.notes: Keyboard command with no menu item, so no command id; no member covers it. No member positions application windows.

features.name: Go forward or backward 1 frame
features.summary: Steps the current time by one frame; the Preview panel Next/Previous Frame buttons do the same.

automation.notes: Page Up steps back.

features.name: Go forward or backward 10 frames
features.summary: Steps the current time by ten frames.

automation.notes: Shift+Page Up steps back.

features.name: Go to layer In or Out point
features.summary: Moves the current time to the selected layer's In point or Out point (earliest In / latest Out with several selected).

automation.notes: O goes to the Out point.

features.name: Go to previous or next In or Out point
features.summary: Jumps to the nearest layer In or Out point before or after the current time.

automation.notes: A script scans the layers' In and Out points and sets AVItem.time to the nearest one before or after the current time.

features.name: Go to beginning or end
features.summary: Moves the current time to the first or last frame of the composition, layer or footage.

automation.notes: End goes to the last frame.

features.name: Go to Time
features.summary: Jumps to a typed time; the current-time display also accepts +N or +-N to move relative to the current time.

features.name: Go to previous or next visible item
features.summary: Jumps to the previous or next keyframe, marker or work-area boundary visible in the time ruler; with Shift it covers selected layers and properties.

automation.notes: A script collects keyframe, marker and work-area times and sets AVItem.time to the nearest earlier or later one. Which items are visible in the time ruler depends on the Timeline twirl state, which scripts cannot read, so the script chooses the properties itself.

features.name: Go to beginning or end of work area
features.summary: Moves the current time to the work area start or end.

automation.notes: Shift+End for the end.

features.name: Choose grid and guide options
features.summary: Viewer button menu for showing safe zones, grid, proportional grid, guides, rulers and 3D reference axes; Alt/Option-click toggles safe zones.

automation.notes: Viewer button menu; its items are recorded separately (Show Grid 2277, Show Guides 2274, Show Rulers 2280).

features.name: Hand tool
features.summary: Pans the view in Composition, Layer and Footage panels; also available temporarily by holding the spacebar, H or the middle mouse button, and double-clicking its button centres the composition.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; dragging with it in a viewer is interactive. Hold Shift to pan faster.

features.name: Import Guides
features.summary: Adds guides from a .guides file (JSON) to the current view, keeping existing guides; Premiere guide files also work.

automation.notes: Opens a file dialog. View > Import Guides (command 4158) opens a file dialog. Guides can be recreated from a list with edit_comp_guides instead.

features.name: Info panel
features.summary: Panel reporting what is under the pointer (colour values and coordinates in composition or layer space), drag changes, durations and In/Out points, and status messages about current operations.

features.name: Display source filename in Info panel
features.summary: Shows in the Info panel which source file supplies the frame at the current time for the selected layer.

features.name: Layer bounding boxes and selection indicators
features.summary: 3D layers, including beveled, extruded and curved ones, show dashed bounding boxes with handles and solid corners, and corner marks appear on the layer that a click would select.

automation.notes: Display behaviour.

features.name: Live Update
features.summary: Redraws the image while dragging layers or values; when off, wireframes are shown during interaction. Holding Alt/Option inverts it temporarily.

automation.notes: Timeline panel menu option that only affects redrawing during interactive dragging; no member or command id.

features.name: Lock Guides
features.summary: Prevents guides from being moved accidentally.

features.name: Enable Compressed Frames (Lossless)
features.summary: Lossless Compressed Playback compresses disk-cached preview frames without quality loss so more frames fit and longer stretches can be previewed.

automation.notes: On by default.

features.name: Magnification Behavior
features.summary: Chooses whether zooming centres on the panel or follows the pointer.

features.name: Magnification ratio
features.summary: Control in the lower left of viewers that shows and sets zoom, including Fit, Fit up to 100%, and preset percentages; Ctrl/Cmd applies a choice to all views.

automation.notes: Zoom changes display only, not composition pixels. ViewOptions.zoom accepts 0.01-16.

features.name: Maintain Current Workspace When Opening Projects
features.summary: Keeps the current panel layout when opening a project that was saved with a different workspace.

automation.notes: Preference key not documented.

features.name: Maximize or restore panel
features.summary: Toggles the panel under the pointer between filling the application window and its docked size; double-clicking a tab does the same.

automation.notes: Viewer.maximized applies only to viewer panels.

features.name: Enable Mercury Transmit
features.summary: Sends the viewer image (without overlays) to an external video device or monitor through Mercury Transmit at the viewer's resolution setting.

automation.notes: macOS without a keypad: Control+Shift+/. Fast Draft and Wireframe send nothing.

features.name: Disable video output when in the background
features.summary: Stops sending frames to the external monitor while another application is in front.

features.name: Video Device
features.summary: Chooses which outputs receive video preview: Adobe DV over FireWire, attached computer monitors, or third-party I/O hardware with its own Setup options.

features.name: Video preview during render queue output
features.summary: Sends frames to the external monitor while the render queue renders.

features.name: Scroll or zoom with the mouse wheel
features.summary: The wheel zooms viewers and the Timeline and scrolls list panels; Alt/Option zooms at the pointer (or in time over the time ruler) and Shift scrolls horizontally, even in inactive panels.

automation.notes: Pointer interaction.

features.name: Move window to main monitor
features.summary: Moves the application or floating window to the main monitor and fits it there.

automation.notes: Keyboard command with no menu item, so no command id; no member covers it. No member positions application windows.

features.name: Multiple monitors
features.summary: The application window stays on the main monitor while floating panel windows can sit on other displays; the monitor setup is saved with the workspace.

automation.notes: Layout arrangement done by dragging.

features.name: New viewer
features.summary: Creates another viewer of the same type; the shortcut also locks the current one and splits the frame for the new viewer.

features.name: New Workspace
features.summary: Saves the current panel arrangement under a new name so it appears in the Workspace menu.

automation.notes: Opens a naming dialog. Unlock viewers first; locked viewers are not saved. Window > Workspace > New Workspace (command 3565, title ends in an ellipsis) opens a naming dialog; there is no scripting member to save a workspace.

features.name: Open, close and show panels
features.summary: Choosing a panel in the Window menu opens it or brings it to the front; the Close button or shortcuts close it, and scrolling over tabs switches the active panel.

automation.notes: Each panel's Window menu item opens it (recorded on the panel records); File > Close (4) closes the active panel; CompItem.openInViewer and Viewer.setActive bring viewers forward. Scrolling over tabs is pointer-only.

features.name: Orbit control modes
features.summary: The Orbit control can pivot around the cursor (default), around the scene, or around the camera's point of interest.

automation.notes: Shift+1 cycles the modes. Enum names come from Types-for-Adobe; mapping of each value to its UI label is inferred from the names.

features.name: Pan control modes
features.summary: The Pan control can move relative to what is under the cursor (default) or move the camera and its point of interest.

automation.notes: Shift+2 cycles the modes. Mapping of enum values to labels inferred from names.

features.name: Panel Background Color
features.summary: Sets the colour of the empty area around the image in the Composition, Layer and Footage panels to one of five grays or a custom colour.

automation.notes: Display setting of the viewer or panel; the 26.0 object model (Viewer, View, ViewOptions) has no member for it and no published list gives a command id.

features.name: Columns in panels
features.summary: Project, Timeline and Render Queue panels show columns that can be toggled from the heading context menu or Columns in the panel menu, reordered by dragging and resized.

automation.notes: Interactive layout state.

features.name: Panel, viewer and context menus
features.summary: Panel menus hold commands for the active panel, viewer menus list the items a viewer can show and lock options, and context menus act on the clicked item.

automation.notes: Interactive menus; individual commands are recorded separately.

features.name: Search and filter in panels
features.summary: Search fields in the Project, Timeline and Effects & Presets panels filter their lists; spaces mean AND, commas mean OR, recent searches are offered and up to ten can be saved with Shift-click.

automation.notes: Interactive search fields; scripts filter project items and layers by iterating them.

features.name: Toggle Pixel Aspect Ratio Correction
features.summary: Displays non-square-pixel footage and compositions corrected to square pixels on screen; turning it off saves processing.

automation.notes: Display setting of the viewer or panel; the 26.0 object model (Viewer, View, ViewOptions) has no member for it and no published list gives a command id. Quality follows the Zoom Quality preference.

features.name: Play Around Current Time
features.summary: Previews a span from a preroll before the current time to a postroll after it, both set in seconds.

automation.notes: Small settings dialog opened from the Preview panel Range menu; no member.

features.name: Play/Stop preview
features.summary: Starts or stops a preview of the active composition, layer or footage using the settings of the shortcut shown in the Preview panel.

automation.notes: The hyperbrew list also has a PlayPreview entry at 10550 (2022 onward); which one maps to this menu item is unverified. Esc or clicking elsewhere also stops previews. The hyperbrew list has two Play Preview ids (10314 and 10550) and which one is Composition > Preview > Play Current Preview is unverified. Playback is interactive (Esc or a click stops it) and returns nothing a call could report, so it is left out until the id is checked in After Effects.

features.name: Cache Before Playback
features.summary: Renders frames into cache before playback starts so it runs at full speed.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id. Off by default for all shortcuts.

features.name: Frame Rate and Skip
features.summary: Sets the preview frame rate (Auto matches the composition) and how many frames to skip to speed up playback.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Enable Preview from Disk Cache
features.summary: High Performance Preview Playback: playback draws frames from the disk cache as well as RAM, so previews are no longer limited by RAM size.

automation.notes: On by default.

features.name: Full Screen
features.summary: Plays the preview full screen.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id. Off by default.

features.name: Include Overlays and Layer Controls
features.summary: Shows grids, guides, safe margins and selected layer controls during playback as configured in View Options.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Include Video / Include Audio / Mute Audio
features.summary: Chooses whether a preview plays video, audio, or both, and can mute audio; at least one Include option stays on.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Loop
features.summary: Repeats the preview range continuously.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Preview panel
features.summary: Panel with playback buttons and per-shortcut preview settings for what plays, looping, caching, range, frame rate, skipping, resolution and what happens on stop.

automation.notes: 2031 is in Types-for-Adobe only.

features.name: Range
features.summary: Sets what plays: Work Area, Work Area Extended by Current Time, Entire Duration, or Play Around Current Time.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Reset preview settings
features.summary: Restores default settings for every preview shortcut; Alt/Option-click restores behaviours that imitate RAM Preview and Standard Preview from CC 2014 and earlier.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Preview resolution
features.summary: Resolution used only for this preview shortcut, overriding the composition's setting.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Preview Shortcut
features.summary: Picks which preview key (Spacebar, Shift+Spacebar, Numpad 0, Shift+Numpad 0, Alt/Option+Numpad 0) the panel settings apply to; each key keeps its own settings.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: If caching, play cached frames / Move time to preview time
features.summary: Stop options: stopping during caching can play what is cached instead of halting, and the current time can jump to where playback stopped.

automation.notes: Preview panel option stored per preview shortcut; no documented scripting member or command id.

features.name: Previews Favor Active Camera
features.summary: In multi-view 3D layouts, previews play through the Active Camera view; turning it off uses the frontmost view.

features.name: Primary Viewer
features.summary: Marks the single viewer or view that drives audio and external video preview; when off, the most recently active one is used.

automation.notes: Display setting of the viewer or panel; the 26.0 object model (Viewer, View, ViewOptions) has no member for it and no published list gives a command id.

features.name: Proportional grid
features.summary: Grid divided into a set number of horizontal and vertical sections that scales with the frame size.

automation.notes: Display setting of the viewer or panel; the 26.0 object model (Viewer, View, ViewOptions) has no member for it and no published list gives a command id.

features.name: Purge snapshot
features.summary: Frees the memory of one snapshot slot.

automation.notes: A single slot cannot be purged by script. Application.purge with PurgeTarget.SNAPSHOT_CACHES, or Edit > Purge > Snapshot (2481), clears all slots.

features.name: Region of Interest
features.summary: Draws a rectangle limiting which part of the frame is rendered for previews, saving memory and time; the button toggles between it and the full frame.

automation.notes: Drawn interactively in the viewer; no member. Crop Comp to Region of Interest (2997) is a separate composition command.

features.name: Reset workspace
features.summary: Returns the current workspace to its last saved layout.

automation.notes: The menu item names the current workspace.

features.name: Resize panel groups
features.summary: Dragging the divider between groups resizes all groups sharing it; dragging an intersection resizes in both directions.

automation.notes: Drag only.

features.name: Auto
features.summary: Preview-only resolution that follows the zoom level so pixels too small to display are not rendered; ignored when Preserve Resolution When Nested is on.

automation.notes: No documented resolutionFactor value for Auto.

features.name: Custom
features.summary: Sets separate horizontal and vertical down-sample factors.

automation.notes: Opens a small dialog.

features.name: Full
features.summary: Renders every pixel of the composition.

automation.notes: resolutionFactor [1,1]. Resolution/Down Sample Factor menu at the bottom of the Composition panel or View > Resolution.

features.name: Half
features.summary: Renders every other row and column, a quarter of the pixels.

automation.notes: resolutionFactor [2,2].

features.name: Resolution/Down Sample Factor
features.summary: Per-composition setting for how many pixels are rendered for previews and, by default, output: Full, Half, Third, Quarter, Custom or (preview only) Auto.

automation.notes: 2037 is the Resolution submenu.

features.name: Quarter
features.summary: Renders one sixteenth of the pixels.

automation.notes: resolutionFactor [4,4].

features.name: Third
features.summary: Renders one ninth of the pixels.

automation.notes: resolutionFactor [3,3].

features.name: Ruler zero point
features.summary: Dragging from the ruler corner sets a new origin, and the Info panel then reports pointer coordinates from it; double-clicking the corner resets it.

automation.notes: Drag interaction.

features.name: Title/Action Safe
features.summary: Overlays action-safe and title-safe margins, plus center-cut margins for 16:9 frames, to keep content inside areas visible on all displays.

automation.notes: Display setting of the viewer or panel; the 26.0 object model (Viewer, View, ViewOptions) has no member for it and no published list gives a command id. Margins are set in Grids & Guides preferences.

features.name: Scroll to current time
features.summary: Scrolls the Timeline panel so the current-time indicator is centred.

automation.notes: Timeline view state changed from the keyboard or the Time Navigator; no member or command id.

features.name: Scrub video and audio
features.summary: Dragging the current-time indicator previews frames manually; modifier variants scrub audio with or without video, and Alt/Option-drag scrubs without stopping a running preview.

automation.notes: Pointer interaction.

features.name: Selection tool
features.summary: Default tool for selecting, moving and scaling layers and handles in viewers; double-clicking its button resets Scale to 100% for selected layers.

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; dragging with it in a viewer is interactive.

features.name: Share View Options
features.summary: Applies viewer option changes to every view in the layout instead of only the active one; holding Ctrl/Cmd reverses it temporarily.

features.name: Show Cache Indicators
features.summary: Shows green (RAM) and blue (disk) bars in the time ruler for cached frames; Ctrl/Cmd-choosing it adds per-layer cache indicators.

automation.notes: Timeline panel display option; no member or command id.

features.name: Show Channel
features.summary: Viewer menu that displays RGB, a single colour channel or alpha as grayscale, colourised channels, straight RGB, and (in the Layer panel) alpha boundary or alpha overlay.

automation.notes: Alt/Option-clicking the button toggles between alpha and RGB.

features.name: Show Grid
features.summary: Displays a square grid over the view for alignment; it is never rendered.

features.name: Show Guides
features.summary: Shows or hides guides in the active view; guides are never rendered.

features.name: Show bounding boxes inside precomps
features.summary: Shows bounding boxes for the characters of per-character 3D text and the layers inside collapsed precompositions.

automation.notes: Called Show Internal Wireframes on the bounding box page and Show Bounding Boxes for Layers Within Pre-Comps on the preferences page; on by default.

features.name: Show Layer Controls
features.summary: Shows or hides masks, motion paths, camera and light wireframes, effect control points, layer handles and 3D axes in the view.

automation.notes: Works during preview as well.

features.name: Show Rulers
features.summary: Shows rulers along the top and left of the view, from which guides are dragged.

features.name: Show Snapshot
features.summary: While held, displays a stored snapshot in the active viewer (any viewer type), resized to fit; it never becomes part of the composition.

automation.notes: Shown only while the key is held; no member or command id.

features.name: Smooth Zoom
features.summary: Magnification Type option that zooms continuously to any value, with decimal hot-text entry and finer scroll and pinch zoom, instead of fixed steps.

automation.notes: Legacy keeps the fixed zoom steps. Shift speeds and Ctrl/Cmd slows scroll zooming.

features.name: Snap to Grid
features.summary: Makes layer and mask edges snap to grid lines while dragging.

features.name: Snap to Guides
features.summary: Makes layer and mask edges snap to guides while dragging.

features.name: Solo Panels in Stack
features.summary: In a stacked group, opening one panel collapses the others; turning Solo off lets several stay open.

automation.notes: Alt/Option-click a tab toggles it. No documented member or id.

features.name: Stacked Panel Group
features.summary: Panel group mode where panels collapse to vertically stacked tabs that expand with a click, set from Panel Group Settings in the panel menu.

automation.notes: Ctrl/Cmd-click a tab to expand or collapse all panels in the stack. No documented member or id.

features.name: Switch to workspace
features.summary: Activates the workspace assigned to a shortcut slot.

automation.notes: Shift+F11 and Shift+F12 are the other slots.

features.name: Take Snapshot
features.summary: Stores the current view image in one of four slots, with a sound, for later comparison.

automation.notes: Keyboard command with no menu item, so no command id; no member covers it. The Composition panel snapshot button is interactive.

features.name: Time Navigator
features.summary: Bracketed bar above the Timeline time ruler whose start and end handles set the visible time span; the Info panel shows its range when clicked.

automation.notes: Drag interaction.

features.name: Toggle Composition and Timeline panel activation
features.summary: Switches keyboard focus between the Composition panel and the Timeline panel of the current composition.

automation.notes: Keyboard command with no menu item, so no command id; no member covers it. Viewer.setActive activates a viewer but no member activates the Timeline panel.

features.name: Toggle Mask and Shape Path Visibility
features.summary: Shows or hides mask and shape paths in the view.

automation.notes: Display setting of the viewer or panel; the 26.0 object model (Viewer, View, ViewOptions) has no member for it and no published list gives a command id.

features.name: Toggle Transparency Grid
features.summary: Shows a checkerboard behind transparent areas instead of the composition background colour.

features.name: Tools panel
features.summary: Toolbar (or dockable panel) of tools; buttons with a triangle hide related tools, tool-specific options appear when a tool is active, and Auto-Open Panels opens related panels for some tools.

automation.notes: Id 2010 toggles the panel; Project.toolType reads or sets the active tool.

features.name: Multi-touch gestures
features.summary: Pinch to zoom and two-finger drag to pan in the Composition, Layer, Footage and Timeline panels on touch screens and trackpads.

automation.notes: Touch interaction.

features.name: Trackpad Scrolling
features.summary: With Smooth zoom, makes two-finger scrolling either zoom the viewer or pan it like the Hand tool.

features.name: Transparency grid size and colors
features.summary: Grids & Guides preferences for the checkerboard square size and its two colours (default light gray and white, or custom).

features.name: Undock Panel / Undock Frame
features.summary: Panel menu commands that float the panel or its whole group in a separate window; Ctrl/Cmd-dragging does the same.

automation.notes: No command id or member is known.

features.name: Select view layout
features.summary: Splits the Composition panel into one, two or four views, each with its own options; middle-clicking activates a view without changing layer selection.

automation.notes: Ids are OneCompView, TwoCompViews, FourCompViews (hyperbrew); the list also has 1Up/2Up/3Up (2691-2693) from 2021 on, whose relation is unclear.

features.name: View
features.summary: Scripting object for one view inside a viewer (one pane of a multi-view layout) with its display options.

features.name: View Options
features.summary: Dialog choosing which layer controls (handles, masks, motion paths, wireframes, effect points and others) each view shows.

automation.notes: Modal dialog; per view. View > View Options (command 2776) opens a modal dialog. Its rulers, guides, grid and transparency options that scripting exposes are set by set_view_options through ViewOptions; the rest (for example layer controls per type) have no scripting member.

features.name: ViewOptions
features.summary: Scripting object holding a view's display state: channel shown, transparency checkerboard, exposure, fast preview mode, guides, rulers and zoom.

automation.notes: fastPreview cannot be read or set in Layer or Footage viewers.

features.name: Toggle Viewer Lock
features.summary: Locks a viewer to its current item so opening another item creates a new viewer instead of replacing it.

automation.notes: Display setting of the viewer or panel; the 26.0 object model (Viewer, View, ViewOptions) has no member for it and no published list gives a command id. Locked viewers are not stored in saved workspaces.

features.name: Viewer
features.summary: Scripting object for a Composition, Layer or Footage viewer panel (app.activeViewer), exposing its type, views, active view and maximized state.

features.name: Workspace bar
features.summary: Strip on the right of the Tools panel with one-click buttons for workspaces, a draggable divider to resize it, and a chevron menu for those that do not fit.

automation.notes: Interactive UI element.

features.name: Color workspace
features.summary: Layout for colour work that includes the Lumetri Scopes panel.

automation.notes: No command id in our sources; workspace ids shift with the workspace list.

features.name: Essential Graphics workspace
features.summary: Layout for building Motion Graphics templates around the Essential Graphics panel.

automation.notes: No command id in our sources; workspace ids shift with the workspace list.

features.name: Learn workspace
features.summary: Simplified layout with the Learn panel docked beside the Project, Composition and Timeline panels.

automation.notes: Reached through Help > Learn After Effects.

features.name: Libraries workspace
features.summary: Layout that brings the Creative Cloud Libraries panel forward.

features.name: Workspace
features.summary: Window submenu listing predefined and saved workspaces (panel layouts) plus commands to create, edit, reset and delete them; the same list is in the workspace bar.

automation.notes: Submenu (command 2738); each workspace and workspace command is its own menu item, recorded separately (for example Standard, 3580). Workspaces are stored as XML files in the ModifiedWorkspaces preferences folder.

features.name: Review workspace
features.summary: Switches to the layout built around Frame.io review and approval.

automation.notes: Frame.io features need sign-in. Workspace ids shift with the workspace list.

features.name: Standard workspace
features.summary: Switches to the general-purpose default panel layout.

features.name: Zoom to 100%
features.summary: Sets the Composition, Layer or Footage view to actual pixels.

automation.notes: Main-keyboard slash.

features.name: Fit up to 100%
features.summary: Fits the frame in the viewer but never magnifies beyond 100%.

automation.notes: The fitted level depends on the panel size, which scripts cannot read; ViewOptions.zoom sets an explicit level instead.

features.name: Zoom In
features.summary: Increases viewer magnification around the centre of the active view.

features.name: Zoom in or out in time
features.summary: Expands or compresses the Timeline time ruler using the zoom buttons, slider or keys.

automation.notes: Timeline view state changed from the keyboard or the Time Navigator; no member or command id.

features.name: Zoom Out
features.summary: Decreases viewer magnification around the centre of the active view.

features.name: Zoom Quality
features.summary: Viewer quality preference trading speed for accuracy when scaling viewer images and pixel aspect ratio correction: Faster, More Accurate Except Cached Preview, or More Accurate.

features.name: Zoom to fit
features.summary: Fits the whole frame in the viewer.

automation.notes: The fitted level depends on the panel size, which scripts cannot read; ViewOptions.zoom sets an explicit level instead.

features.name: Zoom to frame level
features.summary: Toggles the Timeline between single-frame detail and the whole composition duration; double-clicking the Time Navigator does the same.

automation.notes: Timeline view state changed from the keyboard or the Time Navigator; no member or command id.

features.name: Show entire composition duration
features.summary: Zooms the Timeline out to the whole duration and back to the Time Navigator span.

automation.notes: Timeline view state changed from the keyboard or the Time Navigator; no member or command id.

features.name: Zoom tool
features.summary: Clicking or dragging magnifies the view around a point; with Alt/Option it zooms out; double-clicking its button sets the view to 100% (200% on macOS per the help page).

automation.notes: Selecting the tool is scriptable through Project.toolType; dragging with it in a viewer is interactive.
